meta.title: Programa de Inglês Executivo
meta.subtitle: Desenho Curricular · 144 aulas · 7 módulos
meta.tagline: Contextualização, Tréplica e Tempos Verbais — com trilha leve de MBA Executivo.
meta.particularity: Construído sobre as suas necessidades: eixos dedicados de Contextualização, Tréplica e Tempos Verbais, com os marcos contratuais do projeto em aula própria. As aulas-ponte alimentam o seu objetivo de um MBA executivo bilíngue, com temas de economia, geopolítica e sotaques do dia a dia.

overview: Um programa de inglês para a sua rotina de Gerente de Contratos em um grande projeto de data center hyperscale. Começa por um bloco de Survival para destravar a comunicação e aprofunda no vocabulário técnico do seu universo de obra, incluindo os marcos contratuais do projeto. Traz três eixos sob medida, a partir das suas necessidades: Contextualização (situar o porquê antes do quê), Tréplica (defender a posição na segunda e na terceira troca) e Tempos Verbais (passado, presente e futuro sob pressão). As aulas mais leves se conectam ao seu objetivo de um MBA executivo bilíngue, além de economia, geopolítica e sotaques.
logic: Após o bloco inicial de Survival (aulas 1–10, sem intercalação), a cada quatro aulas de conteúdo aprofundado (CORE) a quinta é uma aula mais leve (BRIDGE) — extraída do módulo de MBA Executivo, História da Amazon, Economia & Sotaques (M6) — preservando o engajamento ao longo das 144 aulas. As seis aulas finais (CAPSTONE) consolidam o aprendizado em apresentações conduzidas pelo gerente, todas dentro do universo de data center hyperscale com cliente Amazon, conectadas aos quatro marcos contratuais do projeto.

legend.desc: Aula de conteúdo principal — desenvolvimento técnico, contratual, de gestão ou de survival.
Aula intercalada — MBA Executivo, história da Amazon, economia, geopolítica, sotaque ou idiom.
Apresentação final do gerente — seis cenários do universo data center Amazon.

distribution.name: Engenharia Civil, Data Center & Marcos Amazon

modules.name: BUSINESS SURVIVAL & DESTRAVAR
modules.objective: Bloco de abertura para destravar a comunicação de negócios cotidiana — abertura de reuniões, e-mails, telefonemas, small talk profissional, números/datas/dinheiro em reunião, jantares de negócios e recuperação de mal-entendidos. Todas as aulas vivem dentro do universo corporativo, sem fugir do contexto do gerente de contratos. Funciona como aquecimento antes do mergulho técnico nos módulos seguintes e constrói o repertório de 50 business phrases que retornam ao longo de todo o curso. Endereça diretamente a fala do Júlio em entrevista — "falta vocabulário e timidez por medo de errar" — abrindo espaço para a língua fluir antes de carregar o vocabulário técnico do data center.

modules.name: LIDERANÇA OPERACIONAL & CONTEXTUALIZAÇÃO
modules.objective: Desenvolver vocabulário e fluência para a atuação do gerente de contratos como líder de equipe — coordenação de coordenadores de prazo, custo, design e safety, condução de feedback, reporting para a diretoria e tomada de decisão sob pressão na obra. Inclui um eixo dedicado de "Contextualização" (3 aulas), pedido explícito do aluno em entrevista: "a primeira coisa que eu preciso fazer em toda reunião é contextualizar — explicar o motivo, o contexto, e só depois expor o trabalho".

modules.name: GESTÃO DE CONTRATO & CLIENTE AMAZON
modules.objective: Cobrir o ciclo de vida do contrato em inglês do ponto de vista operacional — interpretação de cláusulas, gestão de escopo, change orders, claims, notificações formais, NDAs específicos de data center hyperscale e closeout. Capacita o gerente de contratos a defender posições contratuais com o representante da Amazon (owner's representative, procurement, gerentes hyperscale) e com os interlocutores multinacionais do cliente — americanos, indianos, latinos e outras nacionalidades citadas pelo aluno na entrevista.

modules.name: ENGENHARIA CIVIL, DATA CENTER & MARCOS AMAZON
modules.objective: Coração técnico do programa — fortemente reponderado para o segmento de data center hyperscale, que é o universo de obra do aluno (Amazon AWS). Cobre fundações, estrutura, MEP crítico (cooling com CRAC/CRAH, chillers e ARRUs, redundância elétrica com UPS e geradores, BMS, EPMS), specs, submittals, RFIs, vendors globais (Eaton, Schneider, Cummins, Vertiv), procurement, controle de qualidade, prazo, custo, HSE e — eixo dedicado — os quatro marcos contratuais Amazon citados pelo aluno: NEA, H2C, PFHO e PCO, cada um com uma aula exclusiva.

modules.name: REUNIÕES, TRÉPLICA & TEMPOS VERBAIS
modules.objective: Aplicar o inglês nas situações reais de interação operacional — média de 10 reuniões semanais em inglês na rotina do aluno em fase crítica de obra. Cobre status updates, war rooms, steering committees, negociações de preço, escopo e prazo, conversas difíceis, telefonemas e e-mails. Traz um eixo dedicado de "Tréplica" (6 aulas) e um eixo de "Tempos Verbais" (2 aulas) — ambas dores explicitamente trazidas pelo aluno em entrevista: "tenho deficiência forte nas colocações em relação a tempo: passado, presente, futuro".

modules.name: MBA EXECUTIVO, AMAZON, ECONOMIA & SOTAQUES
modules.objective: Bridges intercaladas a cada 5 aulas para oxigenar o curso com os temas que o Júlio levantou como seu objetivo pessoal além do trabalho: "eu gosto muito de economia e geopolítica" e "meu desejo é fazer um Executive MBA bilíngue". Quatro trilhas: (1) MBA Executivo (administração, marketing, finanças, estratégia, operações, inovação, liderança — 10 aulas); (2) História da Amazon (2 aulas, da fundação ao pivô AWS); (3) economia global, geopolítica e cultura americana (5 aulas); (4) compreensão de sotaques (americano, indiano, australiano, leste europeu, latino — 5 aulas), todos citados pelo aluno. Completam-se com 3 trilhas de idioms para o repertório do dia a dia.

modules.name: CAPSTONE — DATA CENTER AMAZON
modules.objective: Encerrar o curso com seis apresentações conduzidas pelo gerente de contratos, todas dentro do universo de data center hyperscale com cliente Amazon. As seis aulas percorrem o ciclo completo do projeto pela lógica dos marcos contratuais do próprio aluno: pitch comercial, kickoff pós-NEA, war room pré-H2C, negociação com vendor sob pressão, QBR executivo com audiência multinacional e handover final na transição PFHO → PCO com lessons learned.

capstoneDetail.title: Pitch comercial: Amazon AWS hyperscale data center proposal
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: a Amazon sonda a Racional para construir um novo data center hyperscale em um site greenfield. O gerente de contratos apresenta a empresa, cases comparáveis em mission critical, capacidade de cooling, redundância elétrica, prazo de comissionamento e a estrutura comercial proposta, em reunião com o owner's representative e o Procurement Lead da Amazon — interlocutores americanos e indianos.

capstoneDetail.title: Kickoff meeting & mobilization pós-NEA
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: contrato assinado e NEA emitido. O gerente conduz o kickoff meeting com o time da Amazon e seus partners — apresenta a equipe Racional (coordenadores de design, MEP, instalações, qualidade e HSE), o cronograma macro, os riscos mapeados e o plano dos primeiros 90 dias de mobilização do site, com foco nos próximos marcos contratuais.

capstoneDetail.title: War room: comissionamento pré-H2C sob pressão
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: faltam três semanas para o H2C e a redundância elétrica falha em um startup. O gerente conduz a war room com Eaton, Schneider, sua equipe interna e o cliente Amazon, defendendo o plano de recuperação, negociando prazos com vendors e mediando entre o gerente de instalações e o gerente de comissionamento — voto de Minerva sob pressão.

capstoneDetail.title: Vendor negotiation: switchgear delivery 60 days behind
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: um vendor americano avisa em conference call que a entrega dos switchgears principais está 60 dias atrasada e o projeto entra em rota de colisão com o marco PFHO. O gerente conduz a negociação direta com o VP do vendor, discute liquidated damages, alternativas técnicas e o plano de schedule recovery.

capstoneDetail.title: QBR executivo: monthly review com Amazon NA
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: monthly Quarterly Business Review com a liderança hyperscale da Amazon na sede norte-americana. O gerente apresenta cost vs. budget, indicadores de qualidade, status de comissionamento por marco, KPIs de HSE, riscos abertos e pedidos de decisão — sustentando tréplicas e perguntas de fundo de uma audiência executiva multinacional (americana, indiana e australiana).

capstoneDetail.title: Handover PFHO → PCO & lessons learned
capstoneDetail.scenario: Cenário: obra concluída. O gerente apresenta o relatório final ao cliente: a jornada PFHO → PCO, cost vs. budget consolidado, indicadores de qualidade e prazo, certificações obtidas, lições aprendidas com cada vendor e a proposta de expansão (fase 2 do mesmo site) para a Amazon.

lessons.title: Greetings & first encounters in business contexts (formal vs. casual)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe abrir um encontro de negócios com naturalidade — cumprimentar, apresentar-se e escolher o tom certo (formal ou informal) com o cliente AWS — sem travar por medo de errar.
lessons.overview:
Every meeting starts with a greeting. The first words are small, but they set the tone. At Racional, you work with big clients like Amazon, Microsoft and Google. With the AWS team, you say hello many times each week. A clear and friendly start helps you a lot.

In English, there are two tones. The formal tone is for a first meeting or a senior person. You say: "It is a pleasure to meet you." The casual tone is for people you already know. You say: "Good to see you again!" American teams are often casual, but they like a polite start too.

You are the contracts manager for the Amazon data center project. People will look at you first. A good greeting shows you are calm and ready. This is the first step, and it is easy. When you have these words ready, your English starts to flow.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "It's a pleasure to meet you" (primeira vez), "Good to see you again" (já se conhecem) e "Thanks for joining" (abertura da reunião).

Lembre da diferença clássica: meet = primeira vez; see = de novo. Na dúvida, comece formal — é sempre seguro descer para o informal depois.
lessons.situation: Primeira call da semana com o time da AWS no contrato do data center. Algumas pessoas você já conhece; uma é nova. Você precisa cumprimentar todo mundo no tom certo.
lessons.context: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining today. Sarah, good to see you again. I don't think we have met. I'm Júlio, the contracts manager here at Racional. It is a pleasure to meet you. How are you doing today?

vocab.example: Pleased to meet you. I'm Júlio.
Good to see you again, Sarah.
Thanks for joining today.
Hi Mark, how are you doing?
May I introduce my colleague Ana?
We shake hands at the first meeting.
We are on a first name basis.
A first email is usually formal.
The tone here is casual.
I greet the client first.
Welcome aboard, Mark.
I go by Júlio.
I'm honored to meet you.
Nice to meet you. Likewise!

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Estes quatro termos abrem qualquer encontro. "Likewise" é a resposta curta e elegante a "nice to meet you".

exercises.title: 2. Primeira vez ou de novo?
exercises.prompt: Sarah já trabalha com você há meses. Como você a cumprimenta no início da call?

options.text: Nice to meet you, Sarah.
options.whyWrong: "Meet" é só para a primeira vez. Vocês já se conhecem.

options.text: Good to see you again, Sarah.
Welcome aboard, Sarah.
options.whyWrong: "Welcome aboard" é para quem está chegando agora ao time.

exercises.explanation: Com quem você já conhece, use "see you again". "Meet you" fica reservado ao primeiro encontro.

exercises.title: 3. Apresente-se a alguém novo
exercises.prompt: I don't think we have met. I'm Júlio, and it is a ___ to meet you.
exercises.explanation: "It is a pleasure to meet you" é a abertura formal segura para um primeiro contato. Soa profissional e gentil.

exercises.title: 4. Abra a call
exercises.prompt: Escreva a abertura de uma call com o time da AWS. Cumprimente quem você já conhece e apresente-se a alguém novo. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (em inglês).
keywords: see you again|pleasure to meet you|to greet
exercises.modelAnswer: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining today. Sarah, good to see you again. I'm Júlio, the contracts manager. It is a pleasure to meet you.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos da aula. Frases curtas estão perfeitas neste nível.

exercises.title: 5. Diga em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Good morning. Thanks for joining. I'm Júlio, the contracts manager at Racional.
exercises.translation: Bom dia. Obrigado por participar. Eu sou o Júlio, o gerente de contratos da Racional.
exercises.prompt: Você abre a primeira call da semana com a AWS. Diga esta frase com calma e em tom amigável.
exercises.explanation: Fale devagar e claro. Esta abertura curta funciona em quase toda reunião.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, abra uma call com o time da AWS por uns 15 segundos: cumprimente quem você já conhece, apresente-se a uma pessoa nova e diga seu cargo na Racional.
takeaways: I can greet people in a meeting.
I can say my name and my job.
I can choose a formal or a casual tone.
I can start a call with the AWS team.

lessons.title: Introducing yourself, your role & your company
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe apresentar-se de forma completa — seu nome, seu cargo e sua empresa — para o cliente AWS, em poucas frases simples e seguras.
lessons.overview:
When you meet a new person at work, you give three things: your name, your role, and your company. This is your business card in words. For you, it is short and strong: "I'm Júlio. I am the contracts manager at Racional."

Racional is a Brazilian construction company. It was founded in 1971, so it has more than 50 years of work. The company has built more than 620 projects and over 10 million square meters. The headquarters is in Brazil. These facts make your company sound strong and safe.

You are in charge of the contract for the Amazon data center. You handle the deals, the dates and the money with the AWS team. When you say this clearly, the client trusts you fast. A good self-introduction opens the door for everything else.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "I'm the contracts manager" (cargo), "I work for Racional" (empresa) e "I'm in charge of the Amazon contract" (responsabilidade).

Lembre: to be in charge of, to handle e to be responsible for dizem a mesma ideia — o que é seu para cuidar.
lessons.situation: Um novo gerente entrou no time da AWS. Ele pergunta quem é você e o que você faz no contrato do data center.
lessons.context: Hi, I'm Júlio. I am the contracts manager here at Racional. I work for a Brazilian construction company. We were founded in 1971. I am in charge of the contract for the Amazon data center. I handle the dates and the budget with your team.

vocab.example: I am the contracts manager.

vocab.pt: ser responsável por / estar à frente de
vocab.example: I am in charge of this contract.
I handle the dates and the money.
I am responsible for the budget.
I work for Racional.
Racional is a construction company.
Our headquarters is in Brazil.
We specialize in big projects.
I oversee the contract every week.
My role is contracts manager.
I work in the contracts department.

We deliver big projects.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: I am the contracts manager at Racional.
exercises.explanation: Esta é a frase-base da sua apresentação. Ouça, escreva e repita até sair sem pensar.

exercises.title: 2. Ordene a frase
exercises.explanation: "To be in charge of" + algo é a forma simples de dizer do que você cuida.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a apresentação
exercises.prompt: I ___ for Racional, a Brazilian construction company.
exercises.explanation: "I work for" + empresa é a forma padrão de dizer onde você trabalha.

exercises.title: 4. Qual é o melhor jeito?
exercises.prompt: Como você diz que cuida do contrato da Amazon?

options.text: I am in charge of the Amazon contract.
I am in charge the Amazon contract.
options.whyWrong: Falta o "of". A estrutura é sempre "in charge of".

options.text: I charge the Amazon contract.
options.whyWrong: "I charge" significa "eu cobro". Não é o sentido aqui.

exercises.explanation: A estrutura correta é "to be in charge of" + algo.

exercises.title: 5. Diga em voz alta
exercises.targetText: I'm Júlio. I work for Racional and I am in charge of the Amazon contract.
exercises.translation: Eu sou o Júlio. Trabalho para a Racional e sou responsável pelo contrato da Amazon.
exercises.prompt: Você se apresenta a um novo gerente da AWS. Diga nome, empresa e responsabilidade.
exercises.explanation: Três informações, três pedaços curtos. Fale devagar e com confiança.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, apresente-se a um novo gerente da AWS por uns 20 segundos: diga seu nome, seu cargo, que a Racional é uma construtora fundada em 1971 e que você cuida do contrato da Amazon.
takeaways: I can say my name and my role.
I can say I work for Racional.
I can say I am in charge of the Amazon contract.
I can describe my company in a few words.

lessons.title: Business email basics: structure, tone & sign-offs
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe escrever um e-mail de negócios simples — com abertura, pedido claro e fechamento — para o cliente AWS, sem medo de errar.
lessons.overview:
You write many emails every week. A good business email is short and clear. It has three parts: a friendly start, the main message, and a polite end. You do not need long words. You need clear words.

The start is easy: "I hope you are well." Then you say why you write: "I'm writing to confirm the date." If you need something, you ask in a kind way: "Could you please send the report?" At the end, you close with "Best regards" and your name. This works with the AWS team every time.

For you, the contracts manager on the Amazon project, email is a daily tool. You confirm dates, you follow up, and you send files. A clear email saves time and avoids mistakes. When your email is simple and polite, the client answers fast.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "I'm writing to..." (motivo), "Could you please..." (pedido educado) e "Best regards" (fechamento).

Lembre da estrutura: abertura amigável → motivo → pedido → fechamento. Frases curtas funcionam muito bem em e-mail.
lessons.situation: Você precisa enviar um e-mail à AWS para confirmar a data de uma reunião e pedir um relatório do data center.
lessons.context: Hi Sarah, I hope you are well. I'm writing to confirm the meeting on Friday. Could you please send the weekly report before the call? Thank you in advance. Best regards, Júlio.

vocab.example: Hi Sarah, I hope you're well.
I'm writing to confirm the date.
I'm writing to follow up on my email.
Please find attached the report.
Could you please confirm the date?
I want to confirm the meeting.
Please reply at your earliest convenience.
Looking forward to your reply.
Best regards, Júlio.
Kind regards, Júlio.
Thank you in advance for your help.
The subject line says "Meeting Friday".
Sarah is the recipient of the email.
Please reply by Friday.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Estes quatro termos aparecem em quase todo e-mail de negócios. "Best regards" fecha; "please find attached" anexa.

exercises.title: 2. Escreva um e-mail curto
exercises.prompt: Escreva um e-mail curto à Sarah (AWS) para confirmar uma reunião e pedir um relatório. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (em inglês).
keywords: I'm writing to|I hope you're well
could you please|best regards|thank you in advance
exercises.modelAnswer: Hi Sarah, I hope you're well. I'm writing to confirm the meeting on Friday. Could you please send the report? Thank you in advance. Best regards, Júlio.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos da aula. Mantenha as frases curtas e o tom educado.

exercises.title: 3. Qual fechamento usar?
exercises.prompt: Você termina um e-mail formal para um gerente da AWS. Qual fechamento é melhor?

options.text: Best regards, Júlio.
Bye, Júlio.
options.whyWrong: "Bye" é muito informal para um e-mail de negócios.

options.text: See you, Júlio.
options.whyWrong: "See you" é fala do dia a dia, não fechamento de e-mail formal.

exercises.explanation: "Best regards" e "Kind regards" são fechamentos seguros e profissionais.

exercises.title: 4. Ordene o pedido educado
exercises.explanation: "Could you please" + verbo é a forma educada de pedir algo por e-mail.

exercises.title: 5. Diga em voz alta
exercises.targetText: I'm writing to confirm the meeting. Could you please send the report?
exercises.translation: Escrevo para confirmar a reunião. Você poderia, por favor, enviar o relatório?
exercises.prompt: Leia em voz alta as duas frases-chave do seu e-mail à AWS.
exercises.explanation: Ler o e-mail em voz alta ajuda a fixar as frases para usar na escrita e na fala.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, dite um e-mail curto para a AWS por uns 15 segundos: abra com "I hope you're well", diga o motivo, faça um pedido educado e feche com "Best regards".
takeaways: I can start an email in a friendly way.
I can say why I am writing.
I can ask for something in a polite way.
I can close an email with best regards.

lessons.title: Business meeting openings: setting the tone in 2 minutes
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe abrir uma reunião nos primeiros dois minutos — dar boas-vindas, dizer o objetivo e apresentar a pauta — com o cliente AWS.
lessons.overview:
The first two minutes of a meeting are very important. You set the tone and you show the plan. A good start makes people calm and ready. You say hello, you say the goal, and you show the agenda. Then everybody knows what comes next.

The words are simple. "Let's get started." "The goal today is to review the schedule." "We will cover three points." These short lines give you control of the room. You do not need long speeches. You need a clear plan.

For you, the contracts manager on the Amazon data center, this matters every week. You lead or co-lead many calls with the AWS team. When you open well, the meeting stays on track and you finish on time. A strong start saves the whole call.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "Let's get started" (início), "The goal today is..." (objetivo) e "We will cover..." (pauta).

Lembre da sequência: boas-vindas → objetivo → pauta → primeiro item. Tudo em frases curtas.
lessons.situation: Você lidera a call semanal com a AWS sobre o cronograma do data center. Precisa abrir e apresentar a pauta nos primeiros dois minutos.
lessons.context: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. The goal today is to review the schedule. We will cover three points: the dates, the budget, and the next steps. Let's keep it on track so we finish on time.

vocab.example: Let's get started, everyone.
The goal today is to review dates.
The purpose of this call is the schedule.
Here is the agenda for today.
We will cover three points.
Let me walk through the plan.
Let's keep the call on track.
The first agenda item is the budget.
Let's wrap up in five minutes.
We have three action items.
I give the floor to Sarah.
The objective is clear.
Let me set expectations first.
Let's talk about the next steps.

options.text: Let's we start.

exercises.correctText: The goal today is to review the schedule.

exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos da aula. Mantenha as frases curtas e o plano claro.

exercises.title: 5. Diga em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Let's get started. The goal today is to review the schedule.
exercises.translation: Vamos começar. O objetivo de hoje é revisar o cronograma.
exercises.prompt: Você abre a call semanal com a AWS. Diga esta abertura com calma e clareza.
exercises.explanation: Estas duas frases dão controle da reunião logo no começo.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, abra uma call com a AWS por uns 20 segundos: dê boas-vindas, diga o objetivo do dia e apresente os itens da pauta.
takeaways: I can open a meeting in a clear way.
I can say the goal of the call.
I can present the agenda.
I can keep the meeting on track.

lessons.title: Business small talk & icebreakers: before & after meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe fazer small talk antes e depois das reuniões — quebrar o gelo com o cliente AWS de forma leve e natural.
lessons.overview:
Small talk is the easy chat before and after a meeting. It is not about work. It is about people. You ask about the weekend, the weather, or a trip. This builds trust, and trust is gold in business.

The words are short and warm. "How was your weekend?" "How about you?" "How's it going?" These lines break the ice. American teams like this a lot. They often start a call with one or two minutes of light chat before the real work begins.

For you, the contracts manager on the Amazon project, small talk is a real skill. You talk with the AWS team many times each week. A friendly chat before the call makes the hard parts easier later. People work better with people they like.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "How was your weekend?", "How about you?" e "How's it going?"

Lembre: small talk é leve e curto. Escolha temas seguros (fim de semana, clima, viagem) e nunca algo pesado. "By the way" é a ponte para voltar ao trabalho.
lessons.situation: A call com a AWS começa em dois minutos e todos estão entrando. Você quer quebrar o gelo com uma conversa leve.
lessons.context: Hi Mark, good to see you. How was your weekend? Mine was nice and quiet. How about you? It's great weather here today. By the way, shall we get started? I think everyone is here now.

vocab.example: We had some small talk before the call.

vocab.pt: como foi seu fim de semana
vocab.example: Hi Mark, how was your weekend?
Mine was good. How about you?
A small joke can break the ice.
A quick question is a good icebreaker.
Let's catch up before the call.

options.text: Who did you vote for?
options.whyWrong: Política não é tema seguro no ambiente de negócios.

exercises.explanation: Escolha temas leves: fim de semana, clima, viagem. Evite dinheiro e política.

exercises.title: 4. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Estes termos abrem e fecham o papo. "By the way" é a ponte de volta ao trabalho.

exercises.title: 5. Escreva um small talk curto
exercises.prompt: Escreva uma conversa leve antes da call com a AWS: cumprimente, pergunte sobre o fim de semana e devolva a pergunta. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (em inglês).
keywords: how was your weekend|how's it going
how about you|by the way|to break the ice
exercises.modelAnswer: Hi Mark, good to see you. How was your weekend? Mine was nice and quiet. How about you? By the way, shall we get started?
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos da aula. Mantenha o tom leve e amigável.

exercises.title: 6. Diga em voz alta

exercises.translation: Oi Mark, como foi seu fim de semana? O meu foi bom. E o seu?

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, faça um small talk de uns 15 segundos antes de uma call com a AWS: cumprimente, pergunte sobre o fim de semana, devolva a pergunta e proponha começar com "by the way, shall we get started?".
takeaways: I can make small talk before a meeting.
I can ask about the weekend.
I can return the question with "how about you?".
I can break the ice with a safe topic.

lessons.title: Numbers, dates, money & deadlines in business meetings (out loud)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe dizer em voz alta números, datas, dinheiro e prazos numa reunião com o cliente AWS — com clareza e sem hesitar.
lessons.overview:
In every meeting you say numbers, dates, and money. You say a deadline, a budget, or an amount. These small words carry big weight. One wrong number can cost time and money. So you say them slow and clear.

The key phrases are simple. "The deadline is Friday." "We are ahead of schedule." "The budget is fixed." You can also confirm: "Let me confirm the figures." When you say numbers out loud with calm, people trust your control of the project.

For you, the contracts manager on the Amazon data center, this is daily work. You talk about due dates, milestone dates, and money with the AWS team many times each week. Strong, clear numbers keep the contract safe and the client happy.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "The deadline is Friday" (prazo), "We are ahead of schedule" (adiantados) e "Let me confirm the figures" (conferir números).

Lembre: diga datas e números devagar e repita para confirmar. "By Friday", "within two weeks" e "no later than" deixam o prazo claro.
lessons.situation: Na call com a AWS, você fala do cronograma e do orçamento do data center: precisa dizer datas, valores e prazos em voz alta, sem errar.
lessons.context: The deadline is Friday, the tenth of June. We are ahead of schedule on two points. The budget is fixed for now. Let me confirm the figures with you. Please send the numbers no later than next week.

vocab.example: The deadline is Friday.
The due date is June tenth.
Please send it by Friday.
We will finish within two weeks.
Send it no later than Monday.
Let me confirm the figures.
The cost is two point five million.
The budget is fixed for now.
This is just an estimate.
The amount is correct.
We need to push back the date.
We are ahead of schedule.
We are behind schedule on one item.
The next milestone date is in July.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: The deadline is Friday, June tenth.
exercises.explanation: Datas e prazos precisam sair claros. Ouça, escreva e repita devagar.

exercises.title: 2. Adiantado ou atrasado?
exercises.prompt: O cronograma está melhor que o previsto. Como você diz isso na call?

options.text: We are ahead of schedule.
We are behind schedule.
options.whyWrong: "Behind schedule" significa atrasado — o oposto do que você quer dizer.

options.text: We are out of schedule.
options.whyWrong: "Out of schedule" não é a expressão usada. Use "ahead" ou "behind".

exercises.explanation: "Ahead of schedule" = adiantado. "Behind schedule" = atrasado.

exercises.title: 3. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Estes quatro termos voltam em toda call de cronograma e dinheiro com a AWS.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva um aviso de prazo
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 ou 3 frases para a AWS sobre o cronograma: diga um prazo, diga se estão adiantados ou atrasados e peça os números. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (em inglês).
keywords: ahead of schedule|behind schedule|to confirm the figures|budget
exercises.modelAnswer: The deadline is Friday, June tenth. We are ahead of schedule on two points. Please confirm the figures no later than next week.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos da aula. Datas e números devem ficar claros.

exercises.title: 5. Diga em voz alta
exercises.targetText: The deadline is Friday. We are ahead of schedule. Let me confirm the figures.
exercises.translation: O prazo é sexta-feira. Estamos adiantados. Deixe-me confirmar os números.
exercises.prompt: Na call com a AWS, você informa prazo, status e confirma os valores. Diga devagar e claro.
exercises.explanation: Diga números e datas com calma. Repetir para confirmar é sinal de controle, não de fraqueza.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, fale por uns 20 segundos sobre o cronograma do data center para a AWS: diga um prazo ("the deadline is..."), diga se estão adiantados ou atrasados e confirme os números.
takeaways: I can say dates and deadlines out loud.
I can say if we are ahead of or behind schedule.
I can talk about the budget and the amount.
I can confirm the figures with the client.

lessons.title: Business phone etiquette: switchboards, voicemails & holds
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe se virar ao telefone em inglês — atender, pedir para esperar, transferir e deixar/entender um recado de voicemail — quando precisar falar com a AWS por ligação.
lessons.overview:
The phone is a big part of your day. As contracts manager on the Racional and AWS data center project, you call the client many times every week. The video call shows a face and a chat box. The phone does not. So a phone call in English can feel harder. But it is also more predictable, because people use the same short phrases all the time.

Think about a normal call to the AWS team. First you reach the switchboard. You say who you are. You ask for the right person. Maybe the person is not available, so you leave a message on the voicemail. Or maybe you answer a call and you need to put the caller through to a colleague. These are small moments, but they happen on every project, from a small office to a 10 million square meter portfolio like Racional's.

The good news is simple. You do not need many words. You need a few ready phrases that you can say with no fear. When you know them, the phone stops being a problem. This lesson gives you those phrases for your calls with the AWS client.
lessons.intro:
O telefone tem frases prontas que você pode (e deve) decorar. Atender: "Hello, this is Júlio speaking." Pedir quem fala: "May I ask who's calling?" Pedir para esperar: "Could you hold on, please?" Transferir: "I'll put you through to Ana."

Se cair na caixa postal, deixe um recado com três coisas: quem você é, por que ligou e o pedido de retorno. "Hi, this is Júlio from Racional. Please call me back."
lessons.situation: Você liga para a AWS, cai na central telefônica (switchboard), pede para falar com Sarah, ela não está e você precisa deixar um recado na caixa postal.
lessons.context: Hello, this is Júlio speaking, from Racional. Could I speak to Sarah, please? Oh, she is not available? No problem. Could you take a message? Please tell her I called about the meeting. And please ask her to call me back. Thank you very much.

vocab.example: Hello, this is Júlio speaking.
May I ask who's calling?
Could you hold on, please?
I will put you through to Ana.
Please call me back later.
Could you take a message?
I want to leave a message.
I left a voicemail for Sarah.
The switchboard answered first.
Sorry, the line is busy.
Sorry, we got cut off.
Sorry, could you repeat that?
Could you speak up, please?
Is Sarah available now?

exercises.explanation: Quatro frases prontas cobrem quase toda ligação. Decore e o telefone deixa de assustar.

exercises.title: 2. Atendendo o telefone
exercises.prompt: Você atende uma ligação de trabalho da AWS. Qual é a forma profissional de se identificar?

exercises.title: 3. Peça para esperar

exercises.title: 4. Deixe um recado de voicemail
exercises.prompt: Escreva um recado curto de voicemail para a Sarah, da AWS: quem você é, por que ligou e peça o retorno. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula (ex.: this is ... speaking, call back, voicemail, take a message). A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
keywords: call back|take a message|available|put you through
exercises.modelAnswer: Hi Sarah, this is Júlio from Racional. I am calling about the meeting on Thursday. You are not available, so I leave a message. Please call me back when you can. Thank you.
exercises.explanation: Um voicemail com três pontos — quem, por que, retorno — é curto e eficiente. Vale ter o seu pronto.

exercises.title: 5. Atenda e transfira em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Hello, this is Júlio speaking, from Racional. May I ask who is calling? One moment, please. Could you hold on? I will put you through to Ana.
exercises.translation: Alô, é o Júlio falando, da Racional. Posso saber quem está ligando? Um momento, por favor. Você pode aguardar na linha? Vou transferir para a Ana.
exercises.prompt: Você atende uma ligação da AWS. Em voz alta: identifique-se, pergunte quem é, peça para esperar e transfira a ligação.
exercises.explanation: Praticar a ligação em voz alta tira o medo do telefone. Com as frases decoradas, você responde no automático.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, simule uma ligação para a AWS: atenda identificando-se, peça para falar com alguém, descubra que a pessoa não está e deixe um recado de voicemail com seu nome, o motivo e o pedido de retorno. Pode misturar inglês e português onde travar.
takeaways: I can answer the phone and say my name.
I can ask someone to hold and put them through.
I can ask the caller to repeat with no fear.
I can leave a short, clear voicemail message.

lessons.title: Business dinners & networking events
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe se virar num jantar de negócios ou evento de networking com o time da AWS — puxar conversa, falar de você em poucas palavras e manter o papo leve fora da reunião.
lessons.overview:
Not all work happens in the meeting room. A lot of trust is built at the business dinner, at the coffee before the call, at the networking event. This is where the relationship with the American AWS client grows. And here the English is easier than in a technical meeting, because the goal is to connect, not to decide.

At a dinner you only need three simple moves. First, you break the ice with an easy question, like "How was your trip?". Second, you say who you are in one line: "I take care of the contract on the project." Third, you give the question back to keep the talk alive: "What about you?". This light talk is called small talk, and it is real work.

For a company like Racional, with 50 years and clients such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google, these moments matter. The big contracts are technical, but the relationship is human. When you can get to know someone over dinner, the next hard meeting becomes much easier. So a short, warm conversation is a true business skill.
lessons.intro:
No jantar você precisa de frases curtas e prontas, ditas com calma. Quebrar o gelo: "Nice to meet you. How was your trip?" Falar de você em uma linha: "I take care of the contract on the project." Devolver a pergunta: "What about you?"

Lembre: num jantar, ouvir vale mais que falar. Uma boa pergunta carrega a conversa inteira.
lessons.situation: Depois de um dia de obra no data center, você janta com dois gerentes da AWS. Não é reunião — é relacionamento. Você precisa puxar conversa e se apresentar sem travar.
lessons.context: Nice to meet you. How was your trip from Seattle? Please, have a seat. Let me grab you a drink. I take care of the contract between Racional and AWS. So, is this your first time in Brazil? What about you?

vocab.example: Nice to meet you here.
How was your trip from Seattle?
Please, have a seat.
Let me grab you a drink.

A question can break the ice.

lessons.title: Recovering from misunderstandings in meetings: "sorry, could you repeat that?"
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe se recuperar de um mal-entendido na reunião — pedir para repetir, confirmar o que entendeu e checar com o cliente da AWS sem travar nem ter vergonha.
lessons.overview:
In a meeting with the AWS team, you will not understand everything. That is normal. The client speaks fast, the line is not always clear, and the topic is technical. The skill is not to understand every word. The skill is to recover when you miss something, in a calm and professional way.

You have simple tools for this. You can ask the person to repeat: "Sorry, could you repeat that?". You can ask them to speak slowly: "Could you speak slowly, please?". And you can confirm what you heard: "Do you mean the energization date?". These phrases protect you, and they also protect the contract, because a small misunderstanding on a data center project can become a big cost later.

You said in your interview that you feel shy about making mistakes. This lesson answers that fear directly. Asking the AWS client to repeat is not weak. It is professional. A good contracts manager at Racional makes sure the message is clear before acting. When you confirm and check, you show care, not weakness.
lessons.intro:
Quando não entender, você tem frases prontas. Pedir para repetir: "Sorry, could you repeat that?" Pedir mais devagar: "Could you speak slowly, please?" Confirmar: "Do you mean the energization date?" / "Is that correct?"

Lembre: pedir para repetir é profissional, não é falha. Confirmar evita erro caro no contrato.

lessons.context: Sorry, could you repeat that? I did not catch the last part. Could you speak slowly, please? So, do you mean the energization date is on Friday? I just want to make sure. Is that correct? Thank you, now it is loud and clear.

lessons.title: Survival kit: 50 business phrases for meetings, calls & emails
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você tem um kit de frases prontas de negócios para reuniões, calls e e-mails com a AWS — abrir, contribuir, discordar com educação, fechar e dar follow-up.
lessons.overview:
This lesson is your survival kit. It is a set of ready phrases for the three places where business happens in English: the meeting, the call and the email. You do not need to invent words in the moment. You pick a phrase from the kit and you use it. This is how you remove the fear of speaking that you talked about in your interview.

The kit has a phrase for every step. To open: "Let's get started. Thanks for joining." To add an idea: "Can I add something?". To disagree in a polite way: "I see your point, but...". To close: "Let's wrap up." And to follow up by email: "Please find attached the report. Looking forward to your reply. Best regards." Small phrases, big effect.

As a contracts manager at Racional, you live inside these moments many times a week with the AWS client. The same fifty phrases come back again and again across the whole course. When they become automatic, you save energy for the real content of the contract, not for the words. That is the goal of this kit.
lessons.intro:
Aqui você junta frases-âncora para os três cenários. Abrir: "Let's get started. Thanks for joining." Contribuir: "Can I add something?" Discordar com educação: "I see your point, but…" Fechar: "Let's wrap up." E-mail: "Please find attached… Best regards."

Não invente na hora: escolha do kit e use.
lessons.situation: Você conduz uma call semanal com a AWS e depois envia o e-mail de follow-up com os action items. Precisa abrir, contribuir, fechar e escrever — tudo com frases prontas.
lessons.context: Let's get started. Thanks for joining today. I have one item to flag. I see your point, but we need more time for that. Let's wrap up now. I will send the action items by email and follow up tomorrow. Best regards, Júlio.

lessons.title: Contextualização 1: setting the stage in business meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe "preparar o terreno" numa reunião — dar o contexto e o porquê antes do quê — para que um recém-chegado da AWS te acompanhe desde a primeira frase.
lessons.overview:
You said something important in your interview: "the first thing I need to do in every meeting is to give context — explain the reason, the background, and only then show the work." That instinct is gold. This lesson, the first of your contextualization axis, gives you the English to do it.

To set the stage means to prepare the ground before the details. A good opening has three beats. First, the background: where we are. Second, the purpose: why we are here today. Third, the roadmap: what we will cover. With these three, no one gets lost, not even a new person who just joined the call.

On the AWS data center project, new people enter the meetings all the time: a new project manager from Amazon, a new stakeholder, a new partner. As contracts manager at Racional, you are the person who frames the picture for them. When you set the stage well, the rest of the meeting is easier, and the client trusts that you are in control of the contract.
lessons.intro: Uma abertura de contexto tem três batidas: background (onde estamos), purpose (por que estamos aqui) e roadmap (o que vamos cobrir). Frases-âncora: "Let me set the stage." / "Quick context for those new to the call." / "I will walk you through the status."
lessons.situation: Um novo stakeholder da Amazon entra na call no meio do projeto. Antes de qualquer detalhe, você enquadra o cenário para ele acompanhar.
lessons.context: Thanks for joining, everyone. Let me set the stage. Quick context for those new to the call: we build a data center for AWS, and we are now in the electrical phase. The purpose today is to align on the next milestone. I will walk you through the status and the decision we need.

vocab.example: Let me set the stage first.

lessons.title: Contextualização 2: framing the why before the what
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe enquadrar o porquê antes do quê — explicar o motivo e a lógica de uma decisão para o cliente da AWS, conectando causa e efeito com clareza.
lessons.overview:
This is the second lesson of your contextualization axis. In the last lesson you set the stage. Now you go one step further: you explain the why before the what. People accept a decision much faster when they understand the reason behind it. So before you show the work, you give the rationale.

The English for this is built on cause and effect. You say "the reason is...", "that is why...", "because of the rain...", "as a result, we move the date." These small connectors link the cause to the effect. They help you make the case for your recommendation in a clear, calm way, without long and confusing sentences.

On the AWS data center project, you often need to justify a choice to protect the schedule or the cost. As contracts manager at Racional, you are the person who connects the dots for the client: this happened, that is why we did this, and as a result we recommend this. When the reason is clear, the client trusts the decision, and the meeting moves forward.
lessons.intro:
Aqui você liga causa e efeito com conectores simples. Frases-âncora: "The reason is…" / "That is why we…" / "Because of the rain, the date moves." / "As a result, we recommend…"

Lembre a regra do eixo: o porquê antes do quê. Primeiro o motivo, depois a decisão.
lessons.situation: A chuva atrasou uma etapa no data center. Antes de propor a nova data para a AWS, você explica o motivo e a lógica da decisão.
lessons.context: Let me explain the why first. The reason is the heavy rain last week. Because of the rain, we lost three days on the foundation. That is why the next step is late. As a result, my recommendation is to move the milestone to Monday. This protects the schedule.

vocab.example: The reason is the rain.

As a result, the date moves.

I want to make the case for Monday.

My recommendation is Monday.

lessons.title: Contextualização 3: explaining a problem to outsiders
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conseguir explicar um problema técnico do contrato AWS para pessoas de fora da obra, em inglês simples, dizendo o que aconteceu, o impacto e o que você está fazendo.
lessons.overview:
Every week, a contract manager talks to many people who are not on the site. At the Amazon data center, AWS leaders ask about progress. They do not know the technical words of a construction site. So your job is to explain a problem in simple words. This is called contextualization: first the reason, then the impact, then the work you are doing.

At Racional, a company with more than 50 years and 620 projects, this skill is very important. A good manager does not hide a problem. A good manager explains it well. When you say the impact and not the jargon, the client trusts you. The client sees that the situation is under control.

In this lesson you will learn easy phrases to do this. You will say what happened, you will say what it means for the client, and you will say your next step. Short and clear sentences help a lot. The client is busy, so you go straight to the bottom line.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "We found an issue with..." (Encontramos um problema com...), "In plain terms, this means..." (Em termos simples, isso significa...) e "We are working on a fix." (Estamos trabalhando numa solução).

A ideia é sempre a mesma: contexto primeiro, depois o impacto, depois a ação. Sem jargão técnico.
lessons.situation: Um diretor da AWS entra na reunião semanal e pergunta sobre um atraso na linha de energia. Você precisa explicar o problema sem termos técnicos.
lessons.context: We found an issue with the main power line. In plain terms, it can push the date back by one week. This is the impact, but it is under control. We are working on a fix now. I will keep you posted on Friday.

vocab.example: We have an issue with the test.
In plain terms, it is a small delay.
To put it simply, we need one more week.
The impact is one week of delay.
We had a small setback today.
I will explain it without the jargon.
The bottom line is one week.

vocab.pt: o que isso significa para você
vocab.example: What this means for you is a new date.
The problem is under control now.
We are working on a fix today.
I will keep you posted on Friday.
There is no impact on the budget.

lessons.title: MBA Admin 1: organizational structure & decision-making
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conhecer o vocabulário básico de estrutura organizacional e tomada de decisão, em inglês simples, conectando ao Executive MBA bilíngue que você quer fazer.
lessons.overview:
This is a BRIDGE lesson. It is lighter, and it connects to your personal goal: a bilingual Executive MBA. Today we talk about how companies are built and how they make decisions. This is the language of a business school class.

Every company has a structure. The org chart shows who reports to whom. Some companies are centralized: the top makes all decisions. Some are decentralized: managers decide on the ground. At Racional, with 620 projects, each site has managers with clear authority. Big decisions go up; small decisions stay on the site.

At the Amazon data center, AWS also has a clear chain of command. When a problem is big, you escalate it to the right level. This is good governance. In this lesson you learn easy words to talk about this in any MBA room or steering committee.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "Area managers report to me." (Os gerentes de área se reportam a mim) e "We escalate big decisions to the top." (Levamos as grandes decisões para o topo).

É o vocabulário de uma sala de MBA — e de um comitê da Amazon.
lessons.situation: Uma conversa no estilo MBA com o time da AWS sobre como as decisões fluem no projeto. Você fala a língua da gestão.
lessons.context: Our project is decentralized. Each area manager has authority on the site. They report to me. We escalate only the big decisions to the top. This keeps us fast, and we keep good governance.

vocab.example: Let's look at the structure.
The org chart shows who reports to whom.
Area managers report to me.
Decision-making is fast here.
The top makes all decisions. It is centralized.
Managers decide on the site. It is decentralized.
Each manager has authority.
I delegate small decisions to the team.
We follow the chain of command.
We escalate big problems to the top.
Good governance keeps us safe.
AWS is our main stakeholder.
The hierarchy is clear.
Each manager has accountability for their area.

lessons.title: Managing cross-functional teams (prazo, custo, design, safety)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conseguir coordenar uma reunião de status com os coordenadores de prazo, custo, design e safety, em inglês simples, mantendo a reunião curta e clara.
lessons.overview:
A contract manager leads many people. At the Amazon data center, you coordinate the coordinators: one for the schedule, one for the cost, one for the design, and one for safety. This is a cross-functional team. Each person has a different job, but they work for one goal.

Every week you run a status update. You go around the table. Each coordinator says if their area is on track or late. This is the heart of your work at Racional: many areas, one project, one date for AWS. A good leader keeps the meeting short and clear.

In this lesson you learn easy phrases to lead this meeting in English. You will ask for a status, you will check the next step, and you will set the priority. When you keep it short, the team respects your time and the client sees control.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "Let's go around the table." (Vamos passar a palavra a cada um), "Are we on track?" (Estamos no prazo?) e "Let's keep it short." (Vamos ser breves).

Uma reunião de status curta e clara é a marca de um bom líder.
lessons.situation: Você abre a reunião semanal de status na obra do data center. Os coordenadores de prazo, custo, design e safety estão na mesa.
lessons.context: Good morning, team. Let's keep it short today. We go around the table. Schedule, are we on track? Cost, any change? Design, any change order? Safety, all good? Then we set the next step for each area.

vocab.example: I lead a cross-functional team.
The safety coordinator is here.
I lead the weekly meeting.

Let's do a quick status update.

lessons.title: Performance reviews & feedback in the field
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conseguir dar feedback claro e honesto a um membro do time na obra, em inglês simples, reconhecendo pontos fortes e indicando o que melhorar.
lessons.overview:
A good leader gives feedback. At the Amazon data center, you lead coordinators and engineers. Sometimes you do a performance review. You tell the person what is good and what to improve. This is not easy, but it is important for the team to grow.

Good feedback has two parts. First, you recognize a strength: "You finished the report on time." Then you show an area to improve: "Next time, send it one day earlier." Be specific. Be honest but kind. At Racional, with more than 50 years, this is how teams get better.

In this lesson you learn easy phrases to give feedback in English. You will recognize good work, you will point out one thing to improve, and you will agree on a next step. When feedback is clear and honest, the person trusts you and the work improves.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "You did a great job on..." (Você fez um ótimo trabalho em...), "One area to improve is..." (Um ponto a melhorar é...) e "Let's agree on a next step." (Vamos combinar um próximo passo).

Primeiro o ponto forte, depois o ponto a melhorar. Sempre específico e honesto.
lessons.situation: Você conversa com um coordenador depois de uma entrega importante. Ele fez bem o trabalho, mas precisa melhorar um ponto.
lessons.context: Thank you for your work this week. You did a great job on the safety report. It was on time and clear. One area to improve is the cost numbers. Be more specific next time. Let's agree on a next step.

vocab.example: I have some feedback for you.
We do a performance review every month.

I want to point out one thing.
Please be more specific.

Let's agree on a next step.
I want to be honest with you.
I appreciate your effort.
This is constructive feedback.

lessons.title: Decision-making under pressure on-site
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conseguir explicar uma decisão tomada sob pressão na obra, em inglês simples, dizendo as opções, o risco e a razão da sua escolha.
lessons.overview:
On a big site, you must make fast decisions. At the Amazon data center, problems happen, and AWS needs answers fast. Decision-making under pressure is a key skill for a contract manager. You see the options, you weigh the risk, and you make a call.

Every choice has a trade-off. Maybe one option is fast but more risky. Maybe one option is safe but slow. Sometimes you act fast. Sometimes you hold off and wait for more data. The important thing is your rationale: the reason for the choice. At Racional, with 620 projects, a clear rationale protects you and the client.

In this lesson you learn easy phrases to explain a decision. You will say the options, you will say the risk, and you will stand by your choice. When you explain your reason well, the client trusts your decision, even under pressure.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "We had two options." (Tínhamos duas opções), "I made the call to..." (Eu decidi por...) e "My reason was..." (Minha razão foi...).

Opções, risco e razão: esta é a ordem para defender uma decisão sob pressão.
lessons.situation: Houve uma chuva forte na obra. Você precisou decidir rápido entre parar a concretagem ou continuar. Agora você explica a decisão para a AWS.
lessons.context: We had two options yesterday. Option one was to stop the work. Option two was to continue. I made the call to stop. The risk was too high with the rain. My reason was safety first. I stand by this decision.

lessons.title: Coaching & mentoring senior engineers
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conseguir orientar e desenvolver engenheiros sêniores do seu time, em inglês simples, usando perguntas abertas em vez de dar ordens.
lessons.overview:
A contract manager is also a coach. At the Amazon data center, you lead senior engineers with many years of experience. You do not give them orders all the time. You guide them. You mentor them. This helps them grow.

The secret of good coaching is the open question. Instead of "Do this," you ask "What do you think?" or "What is the root cause?" You listen first. Then you suggest, you do not command. This is a partnership. At Racional, with more than 50 years, senior people share a lot of knowledge when you ask the right question.

In this lesson you learn easy phrases to coach and mentor. You will ask open questions, you will listen, and you will support the engineer. When you coach well, your team grows and you empower strong people to find their own answers.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "What do you think?" (O que você acha?), "What is the root cause?" (Qual é a causa raiz?) e "How can I support you?" (Como posso te apoiar?).

Coaching é guiar com perguntas, não dar ordens.
lessons.situation: Um engenheiro sênior do seu time está travado num problema de projeto. Em vez de dar a resposta, você o ajuda a pensar.
lessons.context: Let's talk about this problem. What do you think is the root cause? I want to listen to you first. You have a lot of experience. What is your idea? I am here to support you, not to give orders.

lessons.title: MBA Marketing 1: positioning & segmentation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende dois conceitos básicos de marketing — posicionamento e segmentação — e sabe falar em inglês simples sobre o que faz uma marca se destacar.
lessons.overview:
This is a lighter bridge lesson. You said you want to do a bilingual Executive MBA one day, so we will read about marketing in simple English. Two ideas are very important: segmentation and positioning. Segmentation means we cut the big market into smaller groups. Positioning means we choose how people see our brand.

Racional is a 50-year-old company with 620+ projects and 10M+ m² built. Racional does not work for everyone. It works for big and demanding clients like Amazon, Microsoft and Google. This is a clear market segment: large, complex projects, like the AWS data center. The target audience is not a small house owner. It is a global company that needs speed, quality and safety.

Why does this matter for you? Because every day you show Racional to the AWS client. You are part of the positioning. When you are clear and reliable, the client sees Racional as a strong and safe partner. A good value proposition is simple: "We build big, complex projects well, on time, and safe." That is how Racional stands out from a competitor.
lessons.intro: Nesta ponte mais leve, foque em três estruturas-âncora que você vai usar para falar de marketing em inglês simples: "Our target audience is..." (nosso público-alvo é...), "We are different because..." (somos diferentes porque...) e "This helps us stand out." (isto nos ajuda a nos destacar).

lessons.title: Delegation & accountability across area managers
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe delegar uma tarefa com clareza e cobrar responsabilidade em inglês simples, mantendo o cliente AWS atualizado.
lessons.overview:
As a contracts manager at the AWS data center, you do not do every task alone. You lead a team. You have coordinators for cost, schedule, design and safety. To delegate well, you give a task to one person and you make the scope clear. Good delegation saves time and avoids mistakes on a big project like a hyperscale data center.

Delegation needs accountability. This means one person is the owner of the task. The owner must take ownership and follow through to the end. You do not need to micromanage. You trust the team, but you ask them to report back and keep you updated. This is how a manager stays in control without doing everything.

Before you delegate, remember your own rule: first you give the context. You explain the "why". Then you give the task and the clear expectations. With the AWS client, you have many meetings every week. Clear delegation means your coordinators come to those meetings ready, with the numbers and the status. That makes Racional look organized and reliable.
lessons.intro: Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora de delegação: "You are the owner of this task." (você é o responsável por esta tarefa), "Please keep me updated." (por favor, mantenha-me atualizado) e "Can you report back by Friday?" (pode me dar um retorno até sexta?). São frases curtas e fáceis de usar na obra.
lessons.situation: Você precisa passar uma tarefa de prazo para o coordenador de cronograma e deixar claro que ele é o responsável até o fim.
lessons.context: John, you are the owner of this task. Please take ownership and follow through. The scope is clear. I trust you. Keep me updated and report back by Friday. I will not micromanage you.

lessons.title: Conflict resolution between specialist teams
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe mediar um conflito entre duas equipes especialistas em inglês simples, achar um terreno comum e seguir em frente.
lessons.overview:
On a big project, teams do not always agree. The cost team wants to save money. The design team wants the best solution. The schedule team wants speed. This is normal. A conflict is not bad. The problem is when nobody helps to resolve it. As a contracts manager, your job is to mediate and find a solution.

To mediate well, you stay neutral. You do not take one side. You listen to both sides and you look for common ground — the part where both teams agree. Often the answer is to compromise: each side gives a little. The goal is a win-win, where both teams are happy enough to move forward.

This is very real at the AWS data center. With many meetings every week, small conflicts happen fast. If you can calm down a tense talk and focus on the interest behind the position, you protect the schedule and the client trust. A manager who can de-escalate a problem is a strong leader, even with simple English.
lessons.intro: Para a prática, guarde três frases-âncora de mediação: "Let's find common ground." (vamos achar um ponto em comum), "I understand both sides." (eu entendo os dois lados) e "How can we move forward?" (como podemos seguir em frente?). São frases neutras, que não tomam partido.
lessons.situation: O time de custo e o time de design discordam sobre uma solução. Você precisa mediar, manter a neutralidade e levar todos a uma decisão.
lessons.context: I understand both sides. Let's stay calm and find common ground. The cost team wants to save money. The design team wants quality. Let's compromise. We need a win-win, so we can move forward together.

lessons.title: Leading specialists you don't outrank technically
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe liderar, em inglês simples, especialistas que sabem mais que você na parte técnica — pedindo ajuda, fazendo boas perguntas e tomando a decisão final.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes you lead people who know more than you about the technical part. The engineer knows more about structure. The safety coordinator knows more about safety. This is normal. You are the contracts manager, not the subject-matter expert. Your job is not to know everything. Your job is to lead the team and make a call.

So how do you lead an expert? You rely on them and you ask the right questions. Two simple phrases help a lot: "Help me understand..." and "Can you walk me through it?" These show respect and they give you the input you need. You can defer to the expert on the technical detail, but you still make the final trade-off decision for the contract.

This is your daily reality at the AWS data center. You lead coordinators of cost, schedule, design and safety. You do not outrank them on the technical part. But you build credibility when you ask good questions, listen well, and then make a call. A good leader does not need to be the smartest person in the room. A good leader knows how to empower the experts and bridge their ideas into one decision.
lessons.intro: Para a prática, fixe três frases-âncora de liderança técnica: "Help me understand the risk." (me ajude a entender o risco), "Can you walk me through it?" (você pode me explicar passo a passo?) e "I will make the call." (eu vou tomar a decisão). Você pede a entrada técnica, mas a decisão final é sua.
lessons.situation: O engenheiro especialista sabe mais que você sobre a parte estrutural. Você precisa entender o trade-off e tomar a decisão final para o contrato.
lessons.context: I am not the expert here, so help me understand. Can you walk me through the trade-off? I rely on your input. I will ask the right questions, and then I will make the call.

lessons.title: Reporting up: weekly executive briefings to Amazon
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe dar um briefing executivo semanal para a Amazon em inglês simples — dizer o status, sinalizar riscos e propor os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
Every week you give a short briefing to the AWS client. This is called reporting up: you tell the senior people the status of the project. A good weekly update is short and clear. The client is busy. You need to keep it brief and go straight to the point: what is good, what is a risk, and what you need from them.

The most important words are about status. A task can be on track (on time), ahead of schedule (early), or behind schedule (late). Many teams use colors: green for good, amber for some risk, and red for a big problem. When there is a risk, you flag it early. You do not hide bad news. You show the key risk and the plan.

This is your weekly reality at the data center. You start with the context — the "why" — then the highlights, then any decision needed, and finally the next steps with a date, like "by Friday". A clear briefing builds trust. The AWS client sees that Racional knows the status and controls the project. Short, honest and on time — that is the goal.
lessons.intro: Para a prática, fixe três frases-âncora de briefing: "The project is on track." (o projeto está no prazo), "I want to flag one key risk." (quero sinalizar um risco principal) e "Next steps: we will finish by Friday." (próximos passos: terminamos até sexta). Curto e direto.
lessons.situation: É a reunião semanal de status com a equipe da AWS. Você tem cinco minutos para dar o briefing: status, um risco e os próximos passos.
lessons.context: Quick weekly update. The project is on track. I want to flag one key risk: the concrete delivery is behind schedule. I will keep it brief. Next steps: we will fix it by Friday.

lessons.title: Idioms 1: business idioms (ballpark, no-brainer, slam dunk)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende e usa alguns idioms comuns de negócios em inglês — como ballpark, no-brainer e slam dunk — em conversas com o cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
This is a lighter bridge lesson about business idioms. American people at AWS use these short expressions all the time. An idiom is a group of words with a special meaning. For example, a no-brainer is a very easy decision. A slam dunk is something sure to work. When you know these words, you understand the meeting better and you feel more confident.

Some idioms are very useful for a contracts manager. A ballpark figure is an approximate number — not exact. "Give me a ballpark figure" means "give me a rough number". To touch base is to talk quickly with someone. To be on the same page is to agree. To circle back is to return to a topic later. And the bottom line is the most important point.

At the AWS data center, you have many meetings every week. You do not need to use all the idioms yourself. But you must understand them when the American client uses them. Learn five or six well, like ballpark, no-brainer, on the same page and circle back. They will help you follow the conversation and sound natural.
lessons.intro: Nesta ponte mais leve, foque em três idioms fáceis para começar a usar: "Can you give me a ballpark figure?" (você pode me dar um número aproximado?), "That's a no-brainer." (isso é óbvio/decisão fácil) e "Let's circle back tomorrow." (vamos retomar isso amanhã).
lessons.situation: Numa call com a AWS, o cliente usa expressões idiomáticas o tempo todo. Você quer entender e, aos poucos, usar uma ou outra com naturalidade.
lessons.context: Can you give me a ballpark figure? Just a rough number is fine. For me, this decision is a no-brainer. Let's touch base tomorrow. The bottom line is: we will finish on time.

lessons.title: Executive presence for contract managers
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você projeta presença executiva em inglês simples — com frases curtas, ritmo lento e tom firme — para que o cliente da AWS perceba o gerente de contratos como uma figura calma e confiável, mesmo sob pressão.
lessons.overview:
Executive presence is not about perfect English. It is about how you come across in the room. A contract manager at Racional speaks with many people every week: AWS, suppliers, and the internal team. When you are composed and clear, people trust you. When you are nervous and fast, people doubt the message. The good news for an A1+ speaker is simple: short, firm sentences sound strong. You do not need big words.

Racional is a large builder. The company is more than 50 years old and has built over 620 projects and 10 million square meters. Today the team works on the Amazon data center for AWS. In these meetings, the client looks at the contract manager. They want calm answers, not long speeches. A few anchor phrases help a lot: "Let me be clear." "Here is my view." "I will get back to you." These short lines project confidence and keep your tone steady.

Presence also means honesty. When you do not have a number, you say so. "I do not have that now. I will get back to you today." This is strong, not weak. A leader can own a mistake and still look calm. The main tool is the pause. When you slow down and pause, you sound like the person in control. This is the goal: be the calm voice in a hard meeting with the client.
lessons.intro:
Presença executiva não é falar inglês perfeito. É transmitir calma, clareza e segurança. Em A1+, a boa notícia é simples: frases curtas e ditas com firmeza soam mais executivas do que frases longas e enroladas.

Relembre as frases-âncora que vamos praticar: "Let me be clear." (ancorar a posição), "Here's my view." (dar sua opinião) e "I'll get back to you." (comprar tempo com compromisso, em vez de inventar resposta).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião tensa do contrato AWS, o cliente questiona um atraso. Todos olham para você. A forma como você responde define se a sala confia no gerente de contratos.

lessons.title: Contract management overview
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende e nomeia, em inglês simples, as grandes etapas do ciclo de vida de um contrato — da assinatura ao encerramento — para conversar com a AWS sobre em que fase cada assunto está.
lessons.overview:
Every contract has a lifecycle. It has steps, and the steps come in order. For a contract manager at Racional, this is the map of the whole job. When you know the name of each step in English, you have power: you can tell the client exactly where an issue is. This makes hard meetings shorter and clearer.

The steps are simple. First, Amazon awards the contract and the parties sign it. Then comes mobilization: the team gets ready to start. After that is the execution phase, where the real work happens and each deliverable is built. During execution, new things come up: a change order for new work, or a claim for extra cost or time. At the end comes closeout and the handover of the building.

On the AWS data center, Racional runs many meetings every week. A key word is scope: this is everything the contract says you must do. When you say "that is out of scope," you mean it is not in the contract. The golden rule is easy: before you discuss a problem, say which phase it is in. This is the "context first" habit, and it organizes half of the conversation before you even start.
lessons.intro:
Esta aula abre o Módulo de Contratos. Todo contrato tem um ciclo de vida, com etapas em ordem: Award → Mobilization → Execution → Closeout.

Relembre duas frases-âncora que vamos praticar: "The contract is in the execution phase." (situar a fase) e "That is out of scope." (dizer que algo não está no contrato).

lessons.title: Reading & interpreting contracts in English
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue ler e interpretar, em inglês simples, as cláusulas mais comuns de um contrato — entendendo a diferença entre o que você deve, o que pode e o que não pode fazer.
lessons.overview:
Reading a contract in English looks hard, but there is a shortcut. A few key words control the meaning of each clause. When you know these words, you understand most of what matters. For a contract manager at Racional, this skill is gold: it lets you read the AWS contract and defend the right position with the client.

Three words are the most important. Shall and must mean an obligation — you have a duty to do it. May means a permission — it is a choice, not a duty. Shall not and may not mean a prohibition — you cannot do it. Other small words give clues too: within ten days is a deadline, subject to means there is a condition, and provided that means "only if."

When a sentence is confusing, ask four simple questions: who does it, what, by when, and under what condition. This opens almost any clause. On the AWS data center, the contract is large and the words are exact. So Racional reads with care and explains each clause in simple words for the team. The golden rule: find the obligation word first — shall, may, or shall not. That word tells you if it is a duty, a choice, or a "no."
lessons.intro:
Ler contrato em inglês assusta, mas há um atalho: palavras-chave controlam o sentido da cláusula. shall/must = deve (obrigação); may = pode (permissão); shall not = não pode (proibição).

Relembre duas frases-âncora que vamos praticar: "Shall means it is an obligation." e "We may request it, provided that we give notice."
lessons.situation: Você está lendo uma cláusula do contrato AWS com o time e precisa explicar, em inglês simples, se a Racional é obrigada a algo ou apenas tem a opção.
lessons.context: Let me read this clause. The contractor shall notify the owner within ten days. 'Shall' means it is an obligation, not a choice. We may request more time, but only provided that we give notice in writing. So we must notify. The extra time is optional.

vocab.example: Let me read this clause.
The contractor shall notify the owner.
We may request more time.
The contractor shall not assign the work.
This is an obligation, not a choice.
Payment is subject to approval.

The notice must be in writing.
The foregoing applies to both parties.
Let me interpret this clause.

exercises.title: 1. Palavra-chave → sentido
exercises.explanation: Essas quatro palavras-chave controlam o sentido da maioria das cláusulas. Domine-as e você lê contrato com segurança.

exercises.title: 2. Interprete uma cláusula
exercises.prompt: Em 2 ou 3 frases, explique ao seu time o que uma cláusula obriga e o que ela permite. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês da aula (ex.: shall, may, provided that). A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: This clause says the contractor shall notify the owner within ten days. So that is an obligation. We may request more time, but only provided that we give notice in writing. So we must notify; the extra time is optional.
exercises.explanation: Você separou o dever (shall) da opção (may) com a condição (provided that). É exatamente assim que se interpreta uma cláusula.

exercises.title: 3. 'Shall' significa o quê?
exercises.prompt: A cláusula diz: "The contractor shall notify the owner within ten days." O que isso significa?

options.text: É uma obrigação: a Racional tem o dever de avisar em até 10 dias.
É uma opção: a Racional pode avisar se quiser.
options.whyWrong: Opção seria 'may'. 'Shall' carrega obrigação, não escolha.

options.text: É uma proibição: a Racional não pode avisar.
options.whyWrong: Proibição seria 'shall not'. 'Shall' sozinho significa dever.

exercises.explanation: Em contrato, 'shall' = obrigação. Reconhecer esse verbo é o primeiro passo para interpretar qualquer cláusula.

exercises.title: 4. Leia a obrigação de prazo
exercises.explanation: Quem (contractor) + obrigação (shall notify) + a quem (the owner) + prazo (within ten days). Essa é a anatomia da cláusula.

exercises.title: 5. Leia e interprete em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Let me read this clause. The contractor shall notify the owner within ten days. 'Shall' means it is an obligation, not a choice. We may request more time, but only provided that we give notice in writing.
exercises.translation: Deixe-me ler esta cláusula. O contratado deve notificar o contratante em até dez dias. 'Deve' significa que é uma obrigação, não uma escolha. Podemos pedir mais tempo, mas somente se dermos aviso por escrito.
exercises.prompt: Você está revisando o contrato AWS com o time. Leia a cláusula em voz alta e explique o que é obrigação e o que é opção.
exercises.explanation: Note como você lê devagar e traduz o sentido jurídico em palavras simples — essa é a leitura de contrato na prática.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, pegue uma frase de contrato com 'shall' ou 'may' e explique, em 15-20 segundos, se é obrigação, permissão ou proibição. Pode misturar inglês e português.
takeaways: I can read a clause and find the obligation word: shall, may or shall not.
I can tell the difference between an obligation, a permission and a prohibition.
I can understand conditions with 'provided that', 'subject to' and 'unless'.
I can read deadlines with 'within ten days' or 'in writing'.
I can interpret a clause in simple words for my team and the client.
