lessons.title: Electrical systems & substations
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve, em inglês simples, o sistema elétrico do data center — substation, transformer, UPS e generator — e como a energia chega aos servidores da AWS.
lessons.overview:
A data center needs a lot of power, and it can never stop. The servers must run all day and all night. So the electrical system is one of the most important parts of the project. At the Amazon AWS site, Racional builds a strong and safe power path, from the street to the servers.

The power comes from the utility power (the public grid). It arrives at a high voltage at the substation. There, the transformer will step down the voltage to a safe level for the building. Then the switchgear sends the power to the right places. The system must distribute the power to every room with care.

But what happens if the utility power fails? The site must keep running. So we have a backup. The UPS gives power for a short time, with no break at all. Then the generator starts and gives power for a long time. The EPMS watches the whole system and shows the load in real time. For AWS, this redundancy is the heart of the design, and for you, as a contract manager, these words come up in almost every weekly meeting.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar o caminho da energia. Frases-âncora: "The power comes from the utility." e "The UPS and the generator back up the site."

Verbos úteis: to step down (reduzir a tensão), to back up (fazer o backup), to distribute (distribuir). O EPMS mostra o load em tempo real.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de prontidão, a AWS pergunta o que acontece se a energia da rua cair. Você explica o backup em inglês simples.
lessons.context: The power comes from the utility. It arrives at the substation. The transformer steps down the voltage for the building. If the utility power fails, the UPS gives power with no break, and then the generator starts. The EPMS shows the load all the time.

lessons.title: Medium voltage & low voltage distribution
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve, em inglês simples, a diferença entre medium voltage e low voltage e como a energia é reduzida e distribuída até a carga crítica do data center da AWS.
lessons.overview:
Inside the data center, the power moves at different levels. We call these levels voltage. The power comes in at a high level and goes down step by step. We split it into two main groups: medium voltage (MV) and low voltage (LV). To know the difference is key for any meeting about the power system at the Amazon AWS site.

The incoming power from the utility arrives at the substation at medium voltage. A feeder carries this power to the building. Then a transformer will step down the medium voltage to low voltage. Low voltage is the safe level we use to feed the equipment. The distribution system then sends the power to each room and each critical load — the servers that must never stop.

For Racional, the plan must be clear and safe. We read the single line diagram to see the whole path on one page. We check the rating of each part and the grounding for safety. When the system is ready, we energize it step by step. AWS follows this with strong attention, and as a contract manager you will hear these words in weekly meetings about milestones and tests.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar os níveis de tensão. Frases-âncora: "Medium voltage comes in; low voltage feeds the load." e "The transformer steps the voltage down."

Termos úteis: feeder (alimentador), single line diagram (diagrama unifilar), to energize (energizar), critical load (carga crítica).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião de comissionamento, a AWS pergunta como a energia desce de medium para low voltage até a carga crítica. Você explica em inglês simples.
lessons.context: The incoming power comes from the utility at medium voltage. A feeder carries it to the building. The transformer steps it down to low voltage. Then we distribute the low voltage to each critical load. We read the single line diagram to follow the whole path.

lessons.title: Switchgears, QGBTs & busways
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve, em inglês simples, o que são switchgears, QGBTs (main distribution boards) e busways, e como eles distribuem a energia no data center da AWS com segurança.
lessons.overview:
After the power becomes low voltage, we must send it to the right places in a safe way. This is the job of the switchgear, the main distribution board (the Brazilian QGBT), and the busway. These parts take the power and route it to each room and each rack at the Amazon AWS site. Racional installs and tests them with great care.

The switchgear is a big set of panels with circuit breakers. A circuit breaker will trip if there is a fault, so it protects the people and the equipment. From the switchgear, the power moves on a busbar or a busway — a strong metal path that carries a high rated current. A busway has many tap-off points, so we can feed each rack easily.

For Racional and AWS, two things matter a lot. First, safety: every part has an enclosure and a clear rating, and we only buy from an approved vendor like Eaton, Schneider, or Vertiv. Second, time: this equipment has a long lead time, so we must order it early to protect the schedule. As a contract manager, you talk about these vendors, lead times, and tests in many weekly meetings with the client.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar a distribuição final da energia. Frases-âncora: "The switchgear routes the power." e "The breaker trips if there is a fault."

Termos úteis: busway (barramento blindado), tap-off (ponto de derivação), lead time (prazo de entrega), approved vendor (fornecedor aprovado).

lessons.title: UPS systems & redundancy strategies
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe explicar, em inglês simples, o que é um sistema UPS e por que a redundância protege os servidores da AWS durante uma falta de energia.
lessons.overview:
A UPS (uninterruptible power supply) is a system that gives power for a short time. When the city power stops, the UPS uses its battery and the servers keep running. In a hyperscale data center for AWS, the power can never stop. So the UPS is one of the most important systems on the job.

Racional builds the AWS data center, and the electrical scope is large and complex. The UPS works with the generators. First the battery holds the load for a few minutes. Then the generator starts and takes over. This is the backup chain, and it must work every time. A short outage can cost the client a lot of money.

For high reliability we build redundancy. This means we have a spare module ready. If one UPS fails, another one takes the load. We avoid a single point of failure, so the data center protects its uptime. As contract manager, Júlio talks about these systems with AWS every week.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora que você vai usar com o cliente AWS:
"The UPS gives power for a few minutes." (presente simples)
"The battery takes over the load." (o que acontece na falta)
"If one unit fails, the spare will take over." (futuro com will para defender a redundância).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião semanal com o owner's representative da AWS, você precisa explicar como o sistema de energia se protege durante uma queda de energia.
lessons.context: A UPS gives power for a short time. When the city power stops, the battery takes over the load. The servers keep running. Then the generator starts and the UPS rests. We always have a spare unit. So we avoid a single point of failure and we protect uptime.

lessons.title: História Amazon 1: founding & the e-commerce years (1994–2005)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe contar, em inglês simples, a história inicial da Amazon — da fundação à era do e-commerce — para conversar sobre o seu cliente com naturalidade.
lessons.overview:
Amazon is the parent company of AWS, the client of Racional in the data center project. The story starts in 1994. Jeff Bezos was the founder. He started a small startup in a garage. The first idea was simple: an online bookstore. People could buy books on a website. This was new and brave in the early years.

In 1995 Amazon began to sell books online. The company grew fast. Soon Amazon began to sell more things: music, films, toys and more. It became a big marketplace. More and more people became Amazon customers. The company learned to put the customer first.

This is good context for Júlio. The client AWS is part of a company that likes to take a risk and grow. When you understand the history of the client, you talk with more confidence in the weekly meetings. It also helps your goal of a bilingual Executive MBA, because business and history go together.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE, mais leve, sobre a história da Amazon. Fixe três frases-âncora no passado simples:
"Jeff Bezos founded Amazon in 1994."
"The company started as an online bookstore."
"Amazon grew fast and became a big marketplace."

lessons.title: Generators: sizing, fuel & load testing
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe explicar, em inglês simples, como os geradores são dimensionados, abastecidos e testados para sustentar a obra da AWS.
lessons.overview:
The generator is the long-time power source in a data center. The UPS battery holds the load for a few minutes. After that, the generator takes over and runs for a long time. In the AWS project, the generators must carry the full demand of the building. So sizing is very important: the capacity must be big enough for the load.

A generator runs on diesel. There is a large fuel tank for many hours of run time. The team plans how to refuel the tank during a long outage. Vendors like Cummins make these big machines for hyperscale sites. Racional manages the install, the specs and the schedule for AWS.

Before handover, the team does a load test. They run a test with a real or fake load and check the exhaust and the temperature. The test proves the generator can back up the site. As contract manager, Júlio reports these test results to AWS every week.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora:
"The generator runs on diesel." (presente simples)
"We size the generator for the full load."
"We will run a load test before handover." (futuro com will).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com a AWS, você precisa confirmar que os geradores foram dimensionados e testados corretamente antes da entrega.

lessons.title: BMS & EPMS — building & electrical monitoring
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe explicar, em inglês simples, o que fazem o BMS e o EPMS e por que monitorar em tempo real protege o data center da AWS.
lessons.overview:
The BMS (building management system) and the EPMS (electrical power monitoring system) are the eyes of the data center. The BMS watches the building: cooling, temperature and air. The EPMS watches the power: the UPS, the generators and the load. Both systems monitor the site all the time.

These systems use many sensors. A sensor sends a reading to a dashboard in the control room. The team looks at the dashboard in real time. If something is wrong, the system sends an alarm. The team can react fast and avoid downtime for AWS.

For Racional, the BMS and EPMS scope is part of the critical MEP work on the AWS project. Vendors like Schneider provide these systems. To detect a problem early is the goal. As contract manager, Júlio talks about alarms, readings and downtime with the client almost every week.

"The EPMS monitors the power."
"If there is a problem, the system sends an alarm." (presente simples).

lessons.title: Cables: power, control, BMS, fire alarm
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe explicar, em inglês simples, os tipos de cabo de um data center e como eles são instalados e organizados na obra da AWS.
lessons.overview:
A data center has many cables. Each cable has a job. A power cable carries energy to the equipment. A control cable carries a signal to start or stop a machine. A fire alarm cable connects the smoke sensors. Cables are the veins of the building.

On the AWS project, the team must route all these cables with care. They use a cable tray to hold the cables. They keep a power cable away from a signal cable to avoid interference. The team also picks the right gauge (the cable size) for each load. This is part of the critical MEP work that Racional manages.

Good work means good order. The team must label every cable, so people can find it later. At each end, the termination must be clean and safe. To pull cable the right way protects the schedule and the quality. As contract manager, Júlio reports cable progress to AWS every week.

lessons.title: Fire protection & plumbing for mission critical
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe explicar, em inglês simples, como funcionam a proteção contra incêndio e o sistema hidráulico de um data center mission critical da AWS.
lessons.overview:
A data center is a mission critical building. The servers must never stop, and they must never burn. So fire protection is very important. In a server room we do not use water first. We use a clean agent: a special gas for fire suppression that does not harm the equipment. Smoke detection finds the fire early.

In other areas we use a sprinkler system. A data center often uses a pre-action system: the water enters the pipe only when there is real smoke and heat. This protects the servers from a false alarm. Racional manages this fire and life-safety scope on the AWS project, with strict specs and quality control.

The plumbing is also critical. The cooling needs chilled water, and the system needs makeup water to stay full. The team installs pipes and valves with care, and uses leak detection to find any water problem fast. As contract manager, Júlio must flag a risk early and report it to AWS with confidence.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora:
"We use a clean agent in the server room."
"The cooling needs chilled water."
"We use leak detection to find a leak fast." (presente simples).

lessons.title: Sotaque 3: Australian English
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai entender melhor o sotaque australiano (Australian English) e usar frases simples para pedir, com educação, que a pessoa repita ou fale mais devagar.
lessons.overview:
This is a bridge lesson about the Australian accent. You like learning many kinds of English, so today we listen to people from Australia. The Australian accent is friendly but fast. People use short words like arvo for afternoon. They also say G'day and no worries many times.

In your work at Racional, you talk with people from many countries. The Amazon AWS project is big, and global vendors join the calls. A supplier from Australia can come to a meeting. So a good ear for the Australian accent helps you on the data center project.

The key skill today is simple: when you do not understand, you ask again. A good manager does not pretend to understand. You say "Could you say that again?" and you make sure the message is clear. This protects the schedule and stops costly mistakes.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai praticar duas coisas: (1) reconhecer palavras australianas curtas — G'day, no worries, mate, arvo; (2) pedir ajuda com educação.

Guarde estas frases-âncora: "Could you say that again?" (pode repetir?), "Could you slow down a little?" (pode falar mais devagar?) e "I want to make sure I follow you." (quero ter certeza de que entendi).
lessons.situation: Um fornecedor australiano entra numa call do projeto AWS e fala rápido. Você não entende tudo e pede, com calma, para ele repetir.
lessons.context: G'day, mate! How ya going? I will send the parts this arvo. No worries. The shipment will land next week. Sorry, the accent is hard. Could you say that again? Yes, of course. I will send the parts this afternoon. They arrive next week. Now it is loud and clear.

vocab.example: G'day, how are you?
G'day, how ya going today?
No worries, I can do that.
Thanks, mate.
I will call you this arvo.
His accent is hard at first.
Could you slow down a little?
Could you repeat the last part?
Sorry, could you say that again?
I did not catch the last word.
I want to make sure I follow you.
The shipment will land next week.
The parts will land on Monday.
Now it is loud and clear.

exercises.explanation: Pedir para repetir ou desacelerar é profissional, não é fraqueza.

exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases respondendo a um fornecedor australiano numa call. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (por exemplo: no worries, shipment, to land, accent).
exercises.modelAnswer: No worries, mate. I understand now. The shipment will land next week and I will follow it.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso correto dos termos da aula.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por uns 15-20 segundos, finja que um fornecedor australiano falou rápido demais. Cumprimente, diga que o sotaque é difícil e peça, com educação, para ele repetir e falar mais devagar.
takeaways: I can understand simple Australian words like G'day and no worries.
I can ask people to repeat or slow down.

lessons.title: Building envelope & facade for data halls
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai descrever, em inglês simples, o envelope e a fachada das data halls e dizer por que eles precisam ser bem vedados.
lessons.overview:
This lesson is about the building envelope and the facade of the data halls. The building envelope is the outside skin of the building. It is the wall, the roof, and the panels that keep out rain, dust, and hot air. The facade is the front face that people see. Both protect the servers inside.

On the Amazon AWS data center, this is very important. The data hall holds many machines. The machines need cool, dry air. So the envelope must be airtight and watertight. A small gap lets moisture in, and moisture is bad for the servers and the cooling load.

At Racional, with more than fifty years and many projects, your team knows how to seal a building well. Good cladding, good insulation, and a strong vapor barrier protect the data hall. As contract manager, you talk about these parts with the AWS client every week, so the words must be clear.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você vai falar das partes externas do prédio e da vedação. Pense no envelope como a "pele" da obra.

Frases-âncora para a prática: "The envelope must be airtight." (o envelope deve ser hermético), "We need to seal the joints." (precisamos vedar as juntas) e "This keeps moisture out." (isso mantém a umidade do lado de fora).
lessons.situation: Numa visita de obra do data center AWS, você explica ao cliente como a fachada e o envelope mantêm a água e a umidade fora das data halls.
lessons.context: The building envelope is the skin of the data hall. It must be airtight and watertight. We use good cladding and strong insulation. A vapor barrier keeps moisture out. We seal every joint and every panel. This protects the servers and helps the cooling load. The facade looks clean, and the weatherproofing is strong.

vocab.example: The building envelope is airtight.
The facade looks clean and strong.
The cladding protects the wall.

The vapor barrier keeps moisture out.
The weatherproofing is very good.
The envelope must be airtight.
Moisture is bad for the servers.
This helps the cooling load.
We seal every joint.
The joint is sealed well.
We check each panel.
The roof is watertight.
This keeps water out.

lessons.title: Specifications (spec) & technical documentation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai falar, em inglês simples, sobre especificações (specs) e documentação técnica, e dizer quando algo está ou não conforme.
lessons.overview:
This lesson is about specifications, or specs, and technical documentation. A spec is a written rule. It says what we must build and how. Every drawing, every material, and every part of the scope of work must follow the spec. When the work follows the spec, we say it is compliant.

On the Amazon AWS data center, the specs are strict. The client sets a high standard. As contract manager, you must comply with each requirement. When something is different from the spec, that is a deviation or a non-conformance, and you must report it fast.

At Racional, with hundreds of projects, clear documentation keeps the work safe and on time. You read the spec, you reference the right drawing, and you make sure the team meets the standard. Good specs and good documents stop costly mistakes with the AWS client.
lessons.intro:
Hoje o foco é o vocabulário de specs e documentos. Pense na spec como a "regra escrita" da obra.

Frases-âncora: "This is per the spec." (isto está conforme a especificação), "The work is compliant." (o trabalho está conforme) e "We must comply with the requirement." (precisamos atender ao requisito).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião semanal com a AWS, você confirma que o trabalho está conforme a spec e registra um ponto de não conformidade para corrigir.
lessons.context: We read the spec before we start. Every part must comply with the requirement. The drawing shows the scope of work. This wall is per the spec, so it is compliant. But this panel is a deviation. It is a non-conformance. We will fix it to meet the standard. The documentation references the right drawing.

vocab.example: We read the spec first.
Every part has a requirement.
This wall is per the spec.
We build it as specified.
The work is compliant.
This is a non-conformance.
This panel is a deviation.
We comply with the requirement.
The spec requires a test.
The drawing shows the wall.
The scope of work is clear.
We meet the standard.
The standard is high.
We reference the right drawing.

exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso correto dos termos da aula.

lessons.title: Submittals, substitutions & RFIs in English
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai falar, em inglês simples, sobre submittals, substituições e RFIs, e dizer se algo está aprovado, pendente ou rejeitado.
lessons.overview:
This lesson is about submittals, substitutions, and RFIs. A submittal is a document you send to the client for approval. A substitution is when you offer an equivalent product. An RFI is a Request for Information: you ask a question to clarify something on the project.

On the Amazon AWS data center, these papers move all the time. You submit a product, the client will review it, and then the client will approve or reject it. While you wait, the status is pending. A fast turnaround keeps the work on time.

At Racional, with many large projects, a clear submittal and a clear RFI save days. When you raise an RFI early, you avoid a long lead time problem later. As contract manager, you control this flow with the AWS client every week.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você aprende o fluxo de documentos: enviar, revisar, aprovar ou rejeitar. Pense no submittal como o "pedido de aprovação".

Frases-âncora: "I will submit the spec sheet today." (vou enviar a ficha técnica hoje), "The submittal is pending." (o submittal está pendente) e "Can I raise an RFI to clarify this?" (posso abrir um RFI para esclarecer isso?).
lessons.situation: Numa call com a AWS, você confirma o status de um submittal pendente e abre um RFI para esclarecer um detalhe antes de pedir aprovação.
lessons.context: I will submit the spec sheet today. The submittal is pending now. The client will review it this week and then approve or reject it. We also offer an equivalent product as a substitution. I want to raise an RFI to clarify one point. A fast turnaround helps, because the lead time is long.

A fast turnaround helps.

lessons.title: Procurement & sourcing for hyperscale projects
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai falar, em inglês simples, sobre compras (procurement) e sourcing para o data center, e controlar prazos de entrega e ordens de compra.
lessons.overview:
This lesson is about procurement and sourcing for hyperscale projects. Procurement is the work of buying. Sourcing is finding the right vendor. You send an RFQ to ask for a price, you compare quotes, and then you issue a PO, a purchase order, to the best vendor.

On the Amazon AWS data center, some items are long-lead items. They have a long lead time, so you must order them early. If you place an order late, the delivery date slips and the work is not on schedule. A strong supply chain keeps the project safe.

At Racional, with global vendors like Eaton, Schneider, Cummins, and Vertiv, good procurement is key. As contract manager, you source the right parts, watch each delivery date, and keep the AWS project on schedule. Buying early and buying well protects the deadline.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você controla compras e prazos. Pense no PO como a "ordem de compra" que fecha o pedido.

Frases-âncora: "We will issue a PO today." (vamos emitir a ordem de compra hoje), "This is a long-lead item." (este é um item de prazo longo) e "We are on schedule." (estamos no prazo).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com a AWS, você confirma que vai emitir o PO de um item de prazo longo a tempo de manter o data center no cronograma.
lessons.context: First we send an RFQ to three vendors. We compare quotes and pick the best one. Then we issue a PO and place the order. This is a long-lead item, so the lead time is long. We must order it early. The vendor will ship it on time. The delivery date is in June, and the project is on schedule.

vocab.example: Procurement is my job here.
Sourcing finds the right vendor.
The vendor will ship it soon.
We send the purchase order today.
We will issue a PO today.
We send an RFQ to vendors.
This is a long-lead item.
The lead time is long.
The delivery date is in June.
The vendor will ship it on time.
We source the right parts.
A strong supply chain helps us.
We compare quotes first.
We place the order today.

options.text: Send an RFQ, compare quotes, then issue a PO.

options.whyWrong: A cotação (RFQ) vem antes da ordem de compra (PO).

options.text: Ship the item, then compare quotes.
options.whyWrong: Comparar cotações vem antes do envio.

exercises.title: 4. Ligue o termo ao sentido
exercises.explanation: Esses são os termos centrais de procurement.

exercises.title: 5. Escreva sobre uma compra
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases dizendo que você vai emitir o PO de um item de prazo longo para manter a obra no prazo. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (por exemplo: to issue a PO, long-lead item, on schedule, delivery date).
exercises.modelAnswer: We will issue a PO today for this long-lead item. The delivery date is in June, so the project stays on schedule.

exercises.prompt: Tranquilize o cliente AWS sobre a compra de um item crítico.
exercises.explanation: Use "but" para mostrar o desafio e a boa notícia juntos.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por uns 15-20 segundos, explique ao cliente AWS o plano de compra: enviar o RFQ, comparar cotações, emitir o PO de um item de prazo longo (long-lead item) e confirmar que a obra segue no prazo (on schedule).
takeaways: I can say procurement and sourcing in English.

lessons.title: MBA Marketing 2: brand & customer experience (Amazon case)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai falar, em inglês simples, sobre marca e experiência do cliente (customer experience), usando o caso da Amazon como exemplo.
lessons.overview:
This is a bridge lesson for your MBA track. The topic is brand and customer experience, or CX. A brand is the name and the promise of a company. Customer experience is how a client feels at every touchpoint. When the experience is good, the client comes back. That is loyalty.

Amazon is a strong example. Amazon is very customer-centric. They talk about customer obsession and they work backwards from the client's need. They want to deliver on a promise every time. This builds trust and a strong reputation.

This idea also fits Racional. With clients like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, a strong value proposition and good service help you stand out. Happy clients talk about you; that is word of mouth. As a manager, a clear focus on the customer makes the brand strong.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE, da sua trilha de MBA. O foco é marca e experiência do cliente. Pense na marca como a "promessa" da empresa.

Frases-âncora: "Amazon is very customer-centric." (a Amazon é muito centrada no cliente), "We deliver on our promise." (cumprimos nossa promessa) e "This builds trust." (isso constrói confiança).
lessons.situation: Numa conversa leve com o time da AWS, você comenta por que a obsessão pelo cliente faz a marca da Amazon ser tão forte.
lessons.context: A brand is the name and the promise of a company. Amazon is very customer-centric. They talk about customer obsession. They work backwards from the customer's need. They want to deliver on a promise every time. This builds trust and a strong reputation. Good customer experience also creates loyalty and good word of mouth.

Brand value grows with trust.

lessons.title: Vendors: Eaton, Schneider, Cummins, Vertiv
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe nomear, em inglês simples, os quatro grandes fornecedores de equipamento crítico do data center — Eaton, Schneider, Cummins e Vertiv — e dizer o que cada um entrega e em que status está a entrega.
lessons.overview:
The Amazon data center is a very big project for Racional. Inside the building, the most important parts are the power and the cooling. A data center cannot stop. So the equipment must be strong and safe. Racional buys this equipment from global vendors. The main names are Eaton, Schneider, Cummins, and Vertiv. Each vendor delivers a different part of the system.

Eaton and Schneider make electrical equipment, like switchgear and the UPS (uninterruptible power supply). Cummins makes the diesel generators. Vertiv makes the cooling units for the server rooms. These vendors are very busy because many data centers are built now. So the lead time can be long. The team must place the purchase order early.

As a contract manager, Júlio talks about these vendors in many meetings with AWS. He says what is on order, what is ready, and what is late. Simple and clear English helps here. When Júlio knows the right words, he can give a fast and good answer to the American client. This makes the client trust Racional more.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar três frases-âncora para falar de fornecedores em reunião: "This equipment is on order." (Este equipamento está em pedido.), "The lead time is twelve weeks." (O prazo de entrega é de doze semanas.) e "Vertiv will deliver the cooling units in May." (A Vertiv vai entregar as unidades de resfriamento em maio).

Note o futuro com will e o presente simples — você vai usar muito os dois para dizer status de entrega.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião semanal com a AWS, o cliente pergunta sobre o status dos equipamentos críticos. Júlio precisa dizer, em inglês, quem entrega o quê e quando.
lessons.context: We work with four main vendors. Eaton and Schneider supply the switchgear and the UPS. Cummins supplies the diesel generators. Vertiv supplies the cooling units. The UPS is on order now. The lead time is twelve weeks. Cummins will deliver the generators in June. We placed the purchase order last month. We track every item every week.

lessons.title: Subcontractor management & manning curves (histograma)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe falar, em inglês simples, sobre gestão de subcontratados e sobre a curva de mão de obra (manning curve / histograma) — quantas pessoas estão na obra e se o efetivo sobe ou desce.
lessons.overview:
A big project like the Amazon data center needs many people. Racional does not do all the work alone. Many subcontractors work on the site. Each one has a trade: electrical, concrete, piping, and more. The contract manager must know how many people are on the site each week. This number is the headcount.

To plan the people, the team uses a manning curve. It is a histogram — a simple chart with bars. The chart shows the workforce for each week. At the start, the team is small. Then the project must ramp up: more people come every week. At the peak, the site is very full. Near the end, the team will ramp down.

AWS wants to see this curve in many meetings. If a trade is understaffed, the work is slow. So Júlio must say, in clear English, if he needs to staff more people or mobilize a new crew. Simple numbers and simple words help the client trust the plan and help Racional keep the work on time.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar três frases-âncora da curva de mão de obra: "We have 300 people on site this week." (Temos 300 pessoas na obra esta semana.), "We will ramp up next month." (Vamos aumentar o efetivo no mês que vem.) e "This trade is understaffed." (Esta especialidade está com pouca gente).

Repare nos números e no futuro com will — você vai usá-los para mostrar o histograma ao cliente.
lessons.situation: Na reunião semanal, a AWS olha a manning curve e pergunta por que o efetivo de uma frente está baixo. Júlio precisa explicar o headcount e o plano de ramp up em inglês.
lessons.context: We have three hundred people on site this week. The electrical crew is understaffed now. We will mobilize a new crew next week. The manning curve shows the peak in August. We must ramp up the concrete trade soon. The histogram is clear. Headcount goes up every week until the peak. After the peak, we ramp down slowly.

vocab.example: This subcontractor is very good.
The manning curve shows the plan.

The headcount is three hundred now.
The workforce grows every week.
We will ramp up next month.
We ramp down after the peak.
We need to staff this trade.
This crew is understaffed today.
We will mobilize a new crew.
Electrical is a key trade here.
The crew starts work at seven.
The peak is in August.
We need more labor on site.

exercises.explanation: "Mobilize" mostra ação; "will" mostra o plano futuro.

takeaways: I can say the headcount on site this week.

lessons.title: Quality control & QA inspections
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe falar, em inglês simples, sobre controle de qualidade e inspeções de QA — pedir uma inspeção, dizer se um serviço passou ou reprovou, e tratar uma não conformidade.
lessons.overview:
In a data center, quality is very important. The client AWS pays for high quality. If the work has a problem, the data center can fail later. So Racional checks the work many times. This is quality control and quality assurance (QA). The team does an inspection for each important step.

When the team inspects the work, it can pass or it can fail. If there is a small problem, the team writes a punch list — a list of items to fix. If there is a bigger problem, the team writes a non-conformance report (NCR). Then the crew must rework the part and fix the defect. After the fix, the work must be compliant with the spec.

AWS often joins the inspections. So Júlio must talk about quality in clear English. He asks for an inspection, he says if the work passed or failed, and he gives the plan to close out each item. Good and simple words show that Racional has control of the quality. This is key to keep the client happy on the Amazon project.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar três frases-âncora de qualidade: "The inspection passed." (A inspeção passou.), "This item is on the punch list." (Este item está na punch list.) e "We will rework this part and close it out." (Vamos refazer esta parte e encerrar o item).

Repare no par pass / fail e no verbo to close out — você vai usá-los para reportar o status de cada item.
lessons.situation: Durante uma inspeção conjunta com a AWS, um item reprova. Júlio precisa dizer, em inglês, o que falhou e como vai resolver.
lessons.context: Today we have a QA inspection with the client. The concrete work passed. The electrical work failed one item. We will open a non-conformance report for this defect. The crew will rework the part this week. We put two small items on the punch list. After the fix, the work will be compliant. Then we close out the report.

vocab.example: Quality control is our job every day.
The QA team checks the work.
We have an inspection today.
We inspect the work every step.
The concrete work passed.
One item failed today.
This item is on the punch list.
We found a non-conformance here.
We open an NCR for this defect.
The crew will rework this part.
We need the sign-off from the client.
There is a small defect here.
The work is compliant now.
We close out the report after the fix.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo ao significado

exercises.explanation: Esses quatro termos cobrem o ciclo de qualidade: achar, registrar, refazer e ficar conforme.

exercises.title: 2. Reporte o resultado da inspeção
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2-3 frases curtas para a AWS com o resultado de uma inspeção. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (ex.: pass, fail, punch list, rework, close out).
exercises.modelAnswer: The concrete work passed. One item failed. We will rework the part and close it out this week.
exercises.explanation: Use o passado para o que já foi inspecionado e "will" para a ação de correção.

exercises.title: 3. Escolha a frase correta
exercises.prompt: Um item reprovou na inspeção. Como você diz que vai refazer e encerrar?

options.text: We will rework the part and close it out.
We pass the punch list to fail.
options.whyWrong: A frase mistura termos e não faz sentido.

options.text: The defect is a sign-off.
options.whyWrong: Defeito e aprovação final são coisas opostas.

exercises.title: 4. Coloque na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: Presente simples: sujeito + verbo "to be" + adjetivo. "The work is now compliant."

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: The inspection passed, but one item is on the punch list.
exercises.translation: A inspeção passou, mas um item está na lista de pendências.
exercises.prompt: Você dá ao cliente o resultado da inspeção do dia.
exercises.explanation: Use "but" para ligar a parte boa e a parte que ainda falta resolver.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por ~15-20 segundos, reporte uma inspeção de QA para a AWS: diga o que passed, o que failed, se há item na punch list ou um NCR, e como você vai rework e close out.
takeaways: I can ask for a QA inspection in English.
I can say if the work passed or failed.
I can talk about a punch list and an NCR.
I can explain how we close out a defect.

lessons.title: Schedule management & critical path
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe falar, em inglês simples, sobre gestão de cronograma e caminho crítico — dizer se a obra está no prazo, atrasada ou adiantada, e apontar o que está no critical path.
lessons.overview:
The Amazon data center has a very tight schedule. AWS wants the power on by a fixed date. So time is the most important thing for Racional on this project. The contract manager looks at the schedule every week. He must know if the work is on schedule, behind schedule, or ahead of schedule.

Some tasks are more important than others for the date. These tasks are on the critical path. A task on the critical path has zero float: if it is late, the whole project is late. Other tasks have float: they can wait a few days with no problem. The team also tracks the big milestones and the final deadline.

In the AWS meetings, Júlio must explain the schedule in clear English. He says if a task will slip, he points to the critical path, and he compares the plan to the baseline. Simple time words — on schedule, behind, ahead, delay, end date — help the client see the real status fast. This builds trust on a project where every day counts.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar três frases-âncora de cronograma: "We are on schedule." (Estamos no prazo.), "This task is on the critical path." (Esta tarefa está no caminho crítico.) e "The milestone has zero float." (O marco tem folga zero).

Repare nos três status: on schedule / behind schedule / ahead of schedule — você vai usá-los para mostrar o status à AWS.
lessons.situation: Na reunião de andamento com a AWS, o cliente quer saber se a data final está segura. Júlio precisa explicar o status do cronograma e o critical path em inglês.
lessons.context: We are on schedule this month. The cooling task is on the critical path. This task has zero float. If it slips, the end date slips too. The electrical task has some float, so it can wait two days. We track every milestone against the baseline. The deadline is still safe. We are not behind schedule now.

vocab.example: We check the schedule every week.

lessons.title: Sotaque 4: Eastern European English (Ukrainian patterns)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você treina o ouvido para o inglês falado por pessoas do Leste Europeu — em especial padrões ucranianos — e aprende frases simples para confirmar e pedir para repetir.
lessons.overview:
Global tech teams have people from many countries. On a data center project, you can meet engineers from the United States, India, and also from Eastern Europe. Many of them speak very good English, but with a different accent. This is normal and very common today. The goal is not a perfect accent — the goal is to understand each other and finish the work.

Speakers from Ukraine and nearby countries often have clear patterns. For example, they sometimes drop the small words a and the. They may say "is no problem" for "there is no problem". They often end a sentence with "right?" to confirm. When you know these patterns, your ear is ready and you follow the talk with no stress.

For Júlio, this skill is very useful. He talks with global vendors like Eaton, Schneider, and Vertiv, and with international teams on the Amazon project. When he does not catch a word, he has simple phrases: "So you mean…", "Can you rephrase that?", or "Let me confirm." These short phrases keep the meeting smooth and show respect for the other person.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula-ponte (BRIDGE), mais leve. Vamos retomar três frases para confirmar e pedir repetição: "So you mean the UPS, right?" (Então você quer dizer o no-break, certo?), "Can you rephrase that?" (Pode dizer de outro jeito?) e "Let me confirm." (Deixa eu confirmar).

O foco é o ouvido e a conexão — não o sotaque perfeito.
lessons.situation: Numa call com um engenheiro de origem ucraniana de um fornecedor global, Júlio não pega uma palavra e precisa confirmar com educação, sem travar a conversa.
lessons.context: On the call, the engineer says: "Is no problem, we ship next week, right?" Júlio does not catch one word. So he says: "Sorry, can you rephrase that?" The engineer repeats slowly. Then Júlio says: "So you mean the UPS ships next week, right?" The engineer says yes. Júlio says: "Great, let me confirm the date. Thank you." The meeting goes well.

lessons.title: Schedule recovery plans — explaining delays in English
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe explicar um atraso e apresentar um plano de recuperação de cronograma (recovery plan) em inglês simples — assumir o fato, dar a causa e mostrar a ação para voltar ao prazo.
lessons.overview:
On a big project, some delay can happen. Rain, a late vendor, or a design change can move a date. AWS knows this. The client does not want excuses — the client wants a clear plan. So when a task is behind, Racional must show a strong recovery plan in the next meeting.

A good recovery plan has three simple parts. First, you say the fact: the task is behind and what is the root cause. Second, you give the action to catch up: maybe a second shift, more overtime, or a new crew. Third, you say the new date and you commit to it. The goal is to get back on track and to make up time.

For Júlio, the words matter a lot here. With a North American client, it is good to be direct and honest. A phrase like "to be straight with you" shows trust. He explains the delay, gives the root cause, and shows how Racional will recover. A clear progress report in simple English keeps the client calm and protects the Amazon contract.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar a estrutura de três partes do recovery plan: "We are two weeks behind." (Estamos duas semanas atrasados.), "This is due to a late delivery." (Isso é por causa de uma entrega atrasada.) e "We will add a second shift to catch up." (Vamos colocar um segundo turno para recuperar).

Repare em due to (causa) e to catch up (recuperar) — são o coração do plano.
lessons.situation: Uma frente do data center atrasou por causa de uma entrega de equipamento. Na reunião com a AWS, Júlio precisa assumir o atraso e apresentar o recovery plan em inglês.
lessons.context: To be straight with you, we are two weeks behind on the cooling task. This is due to a late delivery from the vendor. The root cause is the long lead time. Here is our recovery plan. We will add a second shift and some overtime. With this, we will make up time and get back on track. I will send a progress report every week. We commit to the new date.

lessons.title: Cost control & budget tracking
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe falar sobre custo e orçamento da obra em inglês simples: dizer se o projeto está no orçamento, acima ou abaixo, e reportar uma variação ou um aditivo à AWS.
lessons.overview:
Every big project has a budget. The budget is the money plan for the work. As a contract manager at Racional, you watch this plan every week. You check the actuals — the real money you spend — and you compare them to the plan. This is called cost control, and it is one of your main jobs on the AWS data center.

When the real cost is the same as the plan, the project is on budget. When you spend more, you are over budget. When you spend less, you are under budget. A small difference is normal and we call it a variance. Racional builds large data centers for Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, so even a small variance can mean a lot of money. You also keep a contingency — extra money for surprises.

In your weekly meetings with AWS, you will track the cost and give a clear forecast — what the final cost will be. When the client asks for a change, you write a change order and explain the new cost. Good English here helps you defend your numbers and keep the client's trust. This is why simple, clear words about money matter so much in your day.
lessons.intro:
Nesta aula você vai praticar três frases-âncora para reportar custo à AWS: "We are on budget." (estamos no orçamento), "We are over budget because..." (estamos acima porque...) e "We will track the variance." (vamos acompanhar a variação).

Lembre: para o passado use was/were, para o presente are e para o futuro will. Isso ajuda a explicar o que aconteceu, como está agora e o que virá.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião semanal com a AWS, você apresenta o status do orçamento do data center. O cliente pergunta por que um item está acima do plano e você precisa defender o número.
lessons.context: This week we are on budget. The structure work is on track. We spent a little more on steel, so this item is over budget. The variance is small and it is within tolerance. We have a contingency for this. I will track the actuals every week. Next month the forecast looks good. If AWS asks for a change, we will send a change order.

lessons.title: HSE on-site & incident reporting in English
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe falar de segurança na obra em inglês simples: avisar um perigo, reportar um incidente ou quase-acidente e dizer que parou o trabalho para proteger a equipe.
lessons.overview:
On a large construction site, safety comes first. Every day, your team works near heavy machines, electrical panels, and high places. A hazard is anything that can hurt a person. Your job as a contract manager is to keep people safe and to report problems in clear English to the AWS team.

Sometimes there is a near miss — almost an accident, but nobody was hurt. Sometimes there is a real incident. In both cases, you must report it. You explain what happened, where, and why. You also look for the root cause — the real reason — so it does not happen again. Racional has built more than 620 projects in over 50 years, and a strong safety record is part of why clients like Amazon trust the company.

On the AWS data center, the rules are strict. Every worker must wear a helmet and use PPE — personal protective equipment. If you see danger, you can stop the work at any time. This lesson gives you the simple words to report a hazard, an incident, or a near miss to the client in English.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três frases-âncora de segurança: "There is a hazard here." (há um perigo aqui), "We had a near miss, but nobody was hurt." (tivemos um quase-acidente, mas ninguém se feriu) e "We stopped the work." (paramos o trabalho).

Repare nos tempos: is/are para agora, was/were e had para o passado. Reportar incidente quase sempre usa o passado.
lessons.situation: Houve um quase-acidente perto de um painel elétrico no data center da AWS. Você precisa reportar o ocorrido ao cliente, em inglês, e dizer o que foi feito.
lessons.context: Today we had a near miss near an electrical panel. A worker almost slipped, but nobody was hurt. The area was wet. I stopped the work right away. We checked the area and made it safe. Everyone must wear a helmet and use PPE here. We will look for the root cause. I will send the incident report today.

vocab.example: Safety comes first on site.
There is a hazard near the panel.
We had a near miss this morning.
I will report the incident today.
We report every incident to AWS.
The floor was wet and he almost slipped.
Nobody was hurt, good news.
We stopped the work to be safe.
Everyone must use PPE here.
The first aid kit is ready.
We check the area before work.
Now the area is safe.
You must wear a helmet on site.
We will find the root cause.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e digite
exercises.correctText: We had a near miss, but nobody was hurt.
exercises.explanation: Frase-âncora para reportar um quase-acidente. "Had" e "was" estão no passado.

exercises.title: 2. Coloque na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: "We stopped the work right away" = paramos o trabalho imediatamente. Verbo no passado: stopped.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: Everyone must ___ a helmet on the AWS site.
exercises.explanation: "Wear a helmet" = usar capacete. Depois de "must" o verbo vem no infinitivo sem "to".

exercises.title: 4. Escolha a frase correta
exercises.prompt: Você viu um perigo e quer avisar o time da AWS. Qual frase usar?

options.text: There is a hazard here. We stopped the work.
The area is safe and we will report it.
options.whyWrong: Se a área já está segura, não há perigo a avisar — a frase não combina com a situação.

options.text: Nobody must wear PPE.
options.whyWrong: É o oposto da regra: todos DEVEM usar PPE.

exercises.title: 5. Fale em voz alta
exercises.targetText: There is a hazard here. We stopped the work and checked the area.
exercises.translation: Há um perigo aqui. Paramos o trabalho e verificamos a área.
exercises.prompt: Você está reportando um perigo ao engenheiro da AWS na obra. Fale firme e claro.
exercises.explanation: Avisar o perigo + dizer a ação tomada. Presente para o perigo, passado para a ação.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, reporte ao time da AWS um quase-acidente: diga o que aconteceu (near miss), que ninguém se feriu, que você parou o trabalho e que vai procurar a root cause.
takeaways: I can report a hazard, a near miss, or an incident in simple English.
I can say nobody was hurt and we stopped the work.
I can say everyone must wear a helmet and use PPE.
I can say we will find the root cause.

lessons.title: Commissioning routine: daily stand-ups & pré-marco checklist
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe conduzir um stand-up diário em inglês simples: dar um update, sinalizar um bloqueio e dizer o que está no prazo antes de um marco do data center.
lessons.overview:
Before a big milestone, teams meet every morning for a short meeting. This is the daily stand-up. It is fast — only a few minutes. Each person gives an update: what is done, what is open, and what is a problem. On the AWS data center, the commissioning phase has many stand-ups, because the team tests every system before handover.

In the stand-up you use a short checklist. You say if items are all green (everything is good) or if there is a blocker — something that stops the work. You also say what is pending and what is on track. As a contract manager at Racional, you lead these meetings with the AWS team and keep everyone aligned.

The goal is simple: no surprises before the milestone. You flag problems early, so the team can fix them in time. Racional runs this routine on its large, complex projects to protect the schedule. This lesson gives you the simple English to run a clear and fast stand-up with the client.
lessons.intro:
Pratique três frases-âncora do stand-up: "All systems are on track." (tudo no prazo), "We have one blocker." (temos um bloqueio) e "We are waiting for the test report." (estamos esperando o relatório de teste).

Use o presente para o status de hoje e "will" para o que vem a seguir (ex.: "We will wrap up by noon").
lessons.situation: É o stand-up matinal da fase de comissionamento do data center da AWS. Você precisa dar o status, sinalizar um bloqueio e dizer o que ficará pronto até o meio-dia.
lessons.context: Good morning. Here is the update. Most items are all green and on track. We have one blocker: we are waiting for the test report from the vendor. This item is still pending. I will flag it to the AWS team now. The cooling test is done. We will wrap up the checklist by noon. We need one sign-off today.

vocab.example: The stand-up is at eight.
We are in the commissioning phase.
Here is the morning checklist.
I will give a short update.
We have one blocker today.
We are waiting for the report.
This item is still pending.
Most items are all green.
The work is on track.
We test every system today.
We will wrap up by noon.
The test ends by noon.
I will flag this to AWS.
We need one sign-off today.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo ao significado
exercises.explanation: Termos centrais para reportar status no stand-up com a AWS.

exercises.title: 2. Escreva o seu update
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas para o stand-up: diga o que está no prazo e qual é o bloqueio. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (ex.: on track, blocker, pending, sign-off).
exercises.modelAnswer: Most items are on track. We have one blocker and we are waiting for the test report.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso correto dos termos da aula.

exercises.title: 3. Escolha a frase correta
exercises.prompt: Tudo está bem, sem problemas hoje. Como dizer no stand-up?

options.text: We have one blocker today.
options.whyWrong: "Blocker" é um problema — não combina com "tudo bem".

options.text: All items are all green and on track.
This item is still pending.
options.whyWrong: "Pending" significa pendente — ainda há algo aberto.

exercises.title: 4. Coloque na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: "We will wrap up the checklist by noon" = vamos concluir a lista até o meio-dia. Futuro com "will".

exercises.title: 5. Fale em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Most items are on track. We have one blocker, and I will flag it now.
exercises.translation: A maioria dos itens está no prazo. Temos um bloqueio, e eu vou sinalizá-lo agora.
exercises.prompt: Você está abrindo o stand-up com o time da AWS. Fale rápido e claro, como em uma reunião curta.
exercises.explanation: Status no presente + ação com "will". É o ritmo típico do stand-up.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, conduza um mini stand-up para a AWS: dê o update (o que está on track), aponte um blocker, diga o que está pending e termine com o que você vai fazer ("I will flag...").
takeaways: I can give a short update in a daily stand-up.
I can say what is on track, pending, or a blocker.
I can say we will wrap up the checklist by noon.
I can flag a problem to the AWS team in simple English.

lessons.title: Geopolítica 1: trade, sanctions & global affairs
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe falar de comércio, tarifas e sanções em inglês simples e dar uma opinião curta sobre economia global numa conversa com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
The world economy connects every country. Companies import and export goods every day. This is called trade. When a government adds a tariff — an extra tax on imports — prices can go up. When a country puts sanctions on another country, the supply chain can stop or slow down.

This matters for big projects too. A data center needs many parts from global vendors like Eaton, Schneider, Cummins, and Vertiv. If trade rules change, costs and delivery times can change. So a global market story is not far from your work at Racional — it can raise costs and move a schedule.

This is a bridge lesson, lighter and more personal. You like economy and geopolitics, so this is a great topic to talk about with the AWS team over coffee. The goal here is simple English to follow the news and share a short opinion: "In my view...", "It depends on...". A small talk like this builds a strong relationship with the client.
lessons.intro:
Pratique três frases-âncora de opinião: "In my view, tariffs raise costs." (na minha opinião, tarifas aumentam custos), "It depends on the policy." (depende da política) e "That is an interesting point." (esse é um ponto interessante).

Em conversa leve, o presente simples basta. Use "and", "but" e "because" para ligar as ideias.
lessons.situation: Numa conversa informal com um gerente da AWS, surge o tema de tarifas e cadeia de suprimentos. Você quer participar e dar uma opinião curta, em inglês.
lessons.context: Trade is important for every country. We import and export many goods. When a government adds a tariff, prices go up. Sanctions can slow the supply chain. In my view, this can raise costs for big projects. It depends on the policy. For a data center, we buy parts from global vendors, so the global market matters. That is an interesting point for the news today.

vocab.example: Trade connects many countries.
A new tariff can raise prices.
Sanctions can slow the supply chain.
The supply chain is global.
The global market moves fast.
We import some parts from Asia.
Brazil exports many goods.
I like to read about the economy.
Tariffs can raise costs.
The new policy is not clear yet.
Trade rules have an impact on prices.
In my view, this is a big change.
It depends on the policy.
That is an interesting point.

exercises.explanation: Termos para falar de comércio e dar opinião numa conversa leve.

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a frase correta

options.whyWrong: A frase não faz sentido: não se "importa" a cadeia de suprimentos por horário.

options.text: Sanctions export a tariff.
options.whyWrong: As palavras não combinam: sanções não "exportam" tarifas.

exercises.targetText: In my view, tariffs can raise costs. But it depends on the policy.
exercises.translation: Na minha opinião, tarifas podem aumentar custos. Mas depende da política.
exercises.prompt: Você está num bate-papo com o time da AWS sobre economia. Dê sua opinião com calma.
exercises.explanation: Opinião + ressalva: "In my view..." e "It depends on..." deixam a fala educada e segura.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva sua opinião
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas com a sua opinião sobre comércio ou tarifas. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (ex.: trade, tariff, supply chain, in my view).
keywords: in my view|it depends on|to raise costs
exercises.modelAnswer: In my view, a new tariff can raise costs. It can also slow the supply chain.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso correto dos termos da aula.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, dê sua opinião ao time da AWS sobre tarifas ou sanções: comece com "In my view...", explique o impacto no custo ou na supply chain e termine com "It depends on...".
takeaways: I can talk about trade, tariffs, and sanctions in simple English.
I can say how trade rules can raise costs.
I can give a short opinion with 'In my view...'.
I can say 'It depends on...' to sound polite and careful.

lessons.title: Marco Contratual 1: NEA — Notice of Energization Approval
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe falar do marco NEA — Notice of Energization Approval — em inglês simples: o que é, o que precisa estar pronto antes e como reportar o status à AWS.
lessons.overview:
The NEA — Notice of Energization Approval — is an important milestone on the AWS data center. It is the approval to bring utility power to the building. Before this point, the systems have no live power. After the NEA, the team can energize the substation and start the next phase.

To get the NEA, Racional must submit a package to AWS. The package shows that the work is ready and safe. The client does an inspection and checks every prerequisite. If everything is good, AWS will grant the approval. This is the green light to energize.

As a contract manager, you report this status often. You say what is done, what is pending approval, and when the energization is planned for. Clear English here keeps the AWS team confident. This lesson gives you the simple words to talk about the NEA and defend your schedule.
lessons.intro:
Pratique três frases-âncora do NEA: "We submitted the package." (enviamos o pacote), "It is pending approval." (está pendente de aprovação) e "Energization is planned for next week." (a energização está planejada para a próxima semana).

Note os tempos: submitted (passado), is pending (presente) e will grant / is planned for (futuro). Isso ajuda a contar a história do marco.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com a AWS, você apresenta o status do NEA: o pacote já foi enviado, falta a inspeção e você precisa dizer quando a energização está planejada.
lessons.context: The NEA is the approval to energize the substation. We submitted the package last week. Now it is pending approval. AWS will do the inspection on Monday. All prerequisites are ready. When AWS grants the NEA, we have the green light. Then we can energize and use utility power. Energization is planned for next week.

vocab.example: The NEA is a key milestone.
Energization is planned for next week.
We are waiting for the approval.
We submitted the package last week.
The package is ready for AWS.
The substation is almost ready.
AWS will do the inspection on Monday.
It is planned for next week.
The package is pending approval.
We can energize after the NEA.
Then we use utility power.
AWS will grant the NEA soon.
All prerequisites are ready.
The NEA is our green light.

exercises.explanation: "Pending approval" = pendente de aprovação. É um estado atual, no presente.

options.text: stop the work for safety
options.whyWrong: Parar o trabalho é tema de segurança, não do NEA.

exercises.title: 4. Ligue o termo ao significado
exercises.explanation: Termos centrais do marco NEA com a AWS.

exercises.title: 5. Escreva o status do NEA
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas reportando o NEA à AWS. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (ex.: submit, pending approval, inspection, energization).
exercises.modelAnswer: We submitted the package and it is pending approval. Energization is planned for next week.
exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso correto dos termos da aula.

exercises.title: 6. Fale em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We submitted the package. It is pending approval, and energization is planned for next week.
exercises.translation: Enviamos o pacote. Está pendente de aprovação, e a energização está planejada para a próxima semana.
exercises.prompt: Você está reportando o status do NEA à AWS. Fale com clareza, marcando passado, presente e futuro.
exercises.explanation: A frase junta os três tempos: submitted (passado), is pending (presente), planned for (futuro).

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por 15-20 segundos, reporte o status do NEA à AWS: diga que enviou o package, que está pending approval, quando é a inspection e quando a energization está planned for.
takeaways: I can explain what the NEA milestone is in simple English.
I can say we submitted the package and it is pending approval.
I can talk about inspection, prerequisites, and energization.
I can say when energization is planned for.

lessons.title: Marco Contratual 2: H2C — Handover to Commissioning
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe falar do marco H2C — Handover to Commissioning — em inglês simples: o que significa entregar um sistema, o que precisa estar fechado antes e como confirmar a transferência à AWS.
lessons.overview:
The H2C — Handover to Commissioning — is the moment when Racional hands over a system to the commissioning team. It is a key milestone on the AWS data center. Before this point, the construction work must be complete. After the H2C, the system is in the hands of the commissioning team, which tests it.

To reach the H2C, you must close the punch list — the list of small open items. Every open item must be fixed. You also share the drawings and the test report, so the next team knows the full scope. This is a clean transition from build to test.

As a contract manager, you lead this handover with the AWS team. You confirm that the system is ready to hand over, and AWS will take over. Clear English here avoids confusion and keeps the schedule safe. This lesson gives you the simple words to manage the H2C with the client.
lessons.intro:
Pratique três frases-âncora do H2C: "The system is complete." (o sistema está concluído), "We closed all open items." (fechamos todos os itens abertos) e "We are ready to hand over." (estamos prontos para entregar).

Observe os tempos: is (presente), closed (passado) e will take over (futuro) ajudam a confirmar a transferência.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com a AWS, você confirma o H2C de um sistema: a obra está completa, a punch list foi fechada e o time de comissionamento vai assumir.
lessons.context: Today we confirm the H2C. The system is complete. We closed all the open items on the punch list. The drawings and the test report are ready. So the system is ready to hand over. We will hand over the full scope now. After this, AWS takes over and starts commissioning. It is a clean transition.

vocab.example: The handover is today.
We will hand over the system now.
The system is complete.
We closed the punch list.
We closed all the items.
There are no open items now.
We are ready to hand over.
The drawings are ready.
The test report is signed.
AWS will take over the system.
This is the full scope.
It is a clean transition.
We confirm the handover today.
Now it is in the hands of AWS.

exercises.explanation: Frase-âncora do H2C: confirma que o sistema está pronto para a entrega.

exercises.prompt: O H2C — Handover to Commissioning — marca o momento em que:

exercises.explanation: Termos centrais do marco H2C com a AWS.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva o status do H2C
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas confirmando o H2C à AWS. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (ex.: complete, punch list, hand over, take over).
keywords: to hand over|hand over|to take over|scope

exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso correto dos termos da aula.

exercises.prompt: Você está confirmando o H2C à AWS. Fale com firmeza, mostrando que tudo está pronto.
exercises.explanation: Confirma a conclusão (presente) + a punch list fechada (passado) + a prontidão para entregar.

lessons.title: Marco Contratual 3: PFHO — Power for Hand Over
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue reportar o marco PFHO à AWS em inglês simples: dizer que a energia está estável, que o sistema é redundante e que o teste de backup funcionou.
lessons.overview:
The PFHO milestone means Power for Hand Over. It is the moment when the electrical system is ready. The power is on. The power is stable. The site is almost ready for the client. For a contract manager at Racional, this is a big day on the Amazon project. The data center cannot work without good power.

In a hyperscale data center, power can never stop. So the system has redundancy. This means there is always a plan B. When the main power fails, the UPS holds the load for a few seconds. Then the generators start. Big vendors like Cummins and Eaton supply this equipment. At PFHO, you show the client that all of this works together.

Racional builds for clients like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. These clients want one thing: reliable power. When you report PFHO, you do not only say "the power is on". You say "the power is stable and the backup works". This is the language that the AWS team wants to hear in the meeting.
lessons.intro: Antes de praticar, fixe três frases-âncora. "Power is stable." (presente — a energia está estável agora). "The system is fully redundant." (há backup completo). "The generators kicked in." (passado — os geradores entraram no teste). Repare na diferença entre presente (is) e passado (kicked in).
lessons.situation: Reunião técnica com a AWS sobre o PFHO. O cliente quer confirmar que a energia está estável e redundante antes da entrega. Você reporta em inglês.
lessons.context: Power is stable now. The system is fully redundant. We tested the backup. We cut the main power, and the generators kicked in fast. The UPS held the load. There was no interruption. We are ready for hand over.

lessons.title: Marco Contratual 4: PCO — Project Completion Outage
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue explicar o marco PCO à AWS em inglês simples e defender a sua data segura na segunda e na terceira insistência (tréplica).
lessons.overview:
The PCO milestone means Project Completion Outage. It is the last big test. The team shuts the full system down. Then the team brings it back up under control. This is a planned outage, not a failure. If the data center passes this test, the project is complete. For a contract manager at Racional, this is the final step on the Amazon project.

An outage is a power stop. People hear that word and feel worried. So you must explain the "why" first. The PCO is planned. We choose the time. We control it. We do it to prove that the whole system works together. When the client understands the why, the meeting is calm.

The PCO is also a moment of pressure. The AWS team may push for an early date. Here you need the tréplica: you defend your position in the second and the third turn. You say "I understand the urgency, but my concern is safety". You stay calm. You do not rush. Racional protects the project, the people, and the client. A safe date is the right date.
lessons.intro: Fixe a estrutura da tréplica. Primeiro reconheça: "I understand the urgency, but..." (entendo a urgência, mas...). Depois sustente: "My concern is safety." (minha preocupação é a segurança). Por fim, ofereça o caminho seguro: "I'd rather test next week than rush it." (prefiro testar na semana que vem a apressar).
lessons.situation: Reunião final com a AWS. O cliente pressiona para antecipar o PCO. Você explica a parada final e defende a data segura, mesmo na segunda e na terceira insistência.
lessons.context: The PCO is the final planned outage. We shut the system down. Then we bring it back up under control. I understand the urgency, but my concern is safety. I'd rather test next week than rush it now. Once the PCO passes, the project is complete.

lessons.title: MBA Innovation: disruptive innovation & business models
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar, em inglês simples, sobre inovação disruptiva e modelos de negócio — vocabulário central de uma sala de MBA — conectando ao Executive MBA bilíngue que você quer fazer.
lessons.overview:
This is a lighter bridge lesson, built around your personal goal: a bilingual Executive MBA. Today the topic is the heart of any innovation class: why some small companies beat big giants. The idea is called disruptive innovation. A new company arrives with a cheaper, simpler product. At first it looks weak. But it grows, and it takes the market.

A business model is the way a company makes money and creates value. There are simple models. A subscription means the client pays every month. Pay-as-you-go means the client pays only for what they use. A marketplace is a platform that connects sellers and buyers. Each model creates value in a different way.

You see this every day on your project. Amazon started as a small bookshop online. Big companies ignored it. Then it built AWS, with a pay-as-you-go model, and it changed the whole cloud market. As a contract manager at Racional, you work for clients like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google — the same companies that an MBA class studies as great cases.
lessons.intro: Fixe duas estruturas simples. "It is a low-cost business model." (é um modelo de negócio de baixo custo). "It creates value for the client." (cria valor para o cliente). E lembre da regra do aluno: diga o porquê antes do quê — qual dor do cliente a inovação resolve.
lessons.situation: Numa conversa de estilo MBA, alguém do time da Amazon comenta como a AWS nasceu de uma ideia disruptiva, e você participa com o vocabulário de gestão.
lessons.context: AWS started as a simple, low-cost idea. You rent computing power. You do not buy servers. At first, big companies ignored it. But the pay-as-you-go model was disruptive. Today AWS creates value for the whole cloud market.

lessons.title: Closeout: as-built, punch list & lessons learned
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar, em inglês simples, sobre o fechamento de contrato (closeout): as-built, punch list e lessons learned com a AWS.
lessons.overview:
The closeout is the end of the contract. The data center is built and tested. Now you finish the paperwork and hand the site to the client. For a contract manager at Racional, this is the last phase on the Amazon project. A clean closeout shows that Racional is a serious and reliable builder.

Three things matter at closeout. The as-built drawings show the site as it was really built, not only the first plan. The punch list is a list of small items to fix before the end. And the O&M manuals teach the client how to operate and maintain the data center. When all of this is ready, the client gives final acceptance and you sign off.

There is one more step that good teams never skip: lessons learned. The team meets and asks two simple questions. What went well? What can we do better next time? Racional has built more than 620 projects in 50 years. Each closeout makes the next project better. For a client like AWS, with many projects, this is a strong reason to come back.
lessons.intro: Fixe três frases-âncora. "The as-built drawings are ready." (as plantas como construído estão prontas). "We closed the punch list." (passado — fechamos a lista de pendências). "The client signed off." (o cliente aprovou e assinou). Repare no presente e no passado.
lessons.situation: Reunião de encerramento com a AWS. Você confirma que as plantas finais, a lista de pendências e os manuais estão prontos para a aceitação final.
lessons.context: We are in the closeout now. The as-built drawings are ready. We closed the punch list last week. The O&M manuals are ready too. The client can give final acceptance. Then we sign off and wrap up the project.

lessons.title: Meeting fundamentals: agenda, minutes, action items
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue conduzir o básico de uma reunião em inglês simples: abrir com a pauta, registrar decisões e fechar com os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
You have many meetings every week in English with the AWS team. A good meeting has three simple parts. First, the agenda: the list of topics for the meeting. Second, the minutes: the notes of what the team decided. Third, the action items: the tasks for after the meeting. With these three parts, every meeting stays clear and short.

Each action item has an owner and a due date. The owner is the person who does the task. The due date is the day to finish it. At the end, you recap the decisions and the next steps. This way nobody leaves with a doubt. For a contract manager at Racional, this structure saves time in a busy week of work.

The AWS team is North American. They like meetings that start on time and end on time. They like a clear agenda and clear next steps. When you run the meeting well, you build trust. A good agenda and good minutes show that Racional is organized and reliable on a large project like a hyperscale data center.
lessons.intro: Fixe três frases-âncora para conduzir a reunião. "Let's start with the agenda." (vamos começar pela pauta). "Who is the owner of this action item?" (quem é o responsável por esta ação?). "Let me recap the next steps." (deixe-me recapitular os próximos passos).
lessons.situation: Você conduz uma reunião de status semanal com a AWS. Precisa abrir pela pauta, registrar as decisões e fechar com os próximos passos.
lessons.context: Let's start with the agenda. We have three topics today. I will capture the minutes. Each action item has an owner and a due date. At the end, I will recap the next steps. Then we wrap up.

lessons.title: First meeting & introductions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue se apresentar e apresentar a sua função em uma primeira reunião com a AWS, em inglês simples.
lessons.overview:
The first meeting is important. It is the start of the relationship with the client. In the first minutes, you introduce yourself and you say your role. A clear and warm introduction builds trust from the first day. For a contract manager at Racional on the Amazon project, this happens many times: new people join, and you meet your counterparts on the AWS side.

An introduction is short and simple. You say your name. You say your role: "I am the contract manager". You say what you are responsible for. And you answer with the classic line: "Nice to meet you". With a few phrases, you sound professional and open. You do not need long sentences.

You are also the point of contact for the contract. This means people come to you with questions about scope, time, and cost. In a hyperscale data center project, many teams work together. So a clear introduction helps everyone know who does what. The AWS team is North American and likes a friendly, direct "Nice to meet you" at the start.
lessons.intro: Fixe três frases-âncora para a primeira reunião. "Nice to meet you. I'm Júlio." (prazer em conhecê-lo). "I'm the contract manager." (sou o gerente de contratos). "I'm responsible for the contract." (sou responsável pelo contrato).
lessons.situation: Primeira reunião com novos integrantes do time da AWS. Você se apresenta, diz a sua função e quem é o seu ponto de contato.
lessons.context: Nice to meet you. I'm Júlio. I'm the contract manager at Racional. I'm responsible for the contract on this project. I work closely with the site team. I am your point of contact for scope, time, and cost.
