lessons.title: Conference calls & virtual meetings (Teams)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe participar e conduzir reuniões virtuais no Teams em inglês — entrar na call, pedir a palavra, resolver problemas de áudio e compartilhar a tela — nas suas reuniões semanais com a AWS.
lessons.overview:
Most of your weekly meetings with AWS happen on Teams. You join a conference call, you wait, and you talk. This is your real day. At Racional, on the Amazon data center, the team is in many places. So the call is the room. You need clear words for this room.

A virtual room has small problems. Someone is on mute. The signal can cut out. People talk over each other. These problems are normal. But they cost time. When you say the right short phrase, the call moves fast and the message is clear. This is good for the project and good for you.

You also need to lead. You can share your screen to show the schedule. You can jump in when you have a point. You can wrap up the call and follow up by email. These are simple actions, but they make you look calm and in control with the American client.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE do eixo de interação operacional. Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "Can you hear me?" (você me ouve?), "You're on mute." (você está no mudo) e "Let me share my screen." (vou compartilhar a tela).

Lembre da regra de ouro: garanta o canal antes do conteúdo. Confirme que ouvem você e que veem sua tela. Sem canal, não há mensagem.

lessons.title: História Amazon 2: AWS pivot & the cloud era (2006–today)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe contar, em inglês simples, a história da virada da Amazon — o nascimento da AWS e a era da nuvem (de 2006 até hoje) — ligando o cliente que você atende ao seu interesse por economia.
lessons.overview:
You work with AWS every day on the Amazon data center. But where did AWS come from? The story is one of the biggest business changes in recent history. It is a good story for your Executive MBA dream, and it is good English reading practice for you.

Amazon started in 1994 as a small online bookstore. The company grew fast, so it built a very big computer infrastructure. In 2006, the founder had a bold idea: rent out this computer power to other companies. This was the AWS pivot. A bookstore became a cloud computing leader.

Today AWS is the largest cloud provider in the world. It makes a big part of Amazon's profit. The data centers that Racional helps to build are the physical base of this cloud era. So your work in São Paulo is part of this global story.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE, mais leve, da trilha "História da Amazon". Aqui você treina o eixo de Tempos Verbais ao contar uma história.

Fixe a regra: use o passado para o que aconteceu ("Amazon started…", "AWS launched…") e o presente para hoje ("AWS is now…").
lessons.situation: Numa conversa leve de estilo MBA com o time da AWS, você comenta a história da empresa e a virada para a nuvem.
lessons.context: Amazon started in 1994 as an online bookstore. In 2006, it made a bold pivot and launched AWS. It rented its computer power to other companies. Today, AWS is the largest cloud provider in the world.

lessons.title: Status updates — daily stand-ups
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe dar seu status na daily stand-up com a AWS em inglês simples — o que fez ontem, o que faz hoje e se há algum bloqueio.
lessons.overview:
On a data center project in a critical phase, the team meets every morning. This is the daily stand-up. It is short. Each person gives a fast status update: what they did yesterday, what they do today, and any blocker. At Racional, with the AWS team, this happens many times a week.

The stand-up has a simple shape. You say if you are on track or behind schedule. You say if you are blocked by something or if there are no blockers. You flag a risk early, so the team can help. Then you hand over to the next person. Short, clear, and on time.

This is one of your most common meetings, so good English here saves time every day. When you give a clean status, the AWS client trusts the work. They see that the obra is under control. A clear stand-up is small, but it builds your reputation as a strong contract manager.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE do eixo de interação operacional. Antes da prática, fixe a estrutura da stand-up: "Yesterday I…" (ontem eu…), "Today I…" (hoje eu…), "No blockers." ou "I'm blocked by…".

Lembre: passado para ontem, presente/futuro para hoje. Esse é o seu eixo de Tempos Verbais aplicado à rotina.

lessons.title: Status updates — weekly gerencial com Amazon
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe dar o seu status na reunião gerencial semanal com a Amazon em inglês simples — o que foi feito na semana passada, o que está na semana atual e o que vem na próxima.
lessons.overview:
Once a week, you join a bigger meeting with the Amazon team. This is the weekly management status update. Here you look at a wider view: last week, this week, and next week. It is not as fast as the daily. The client wants to see the trend of the work.

In this meeting you report what you completed, what you are working on, and what you will wrap up soon. You say if the obra is on track, ahead of schedule, or behind schedule. You flag the main risks and give one or two highlights. This is the moment to show progress with confidence.

For Racional, this weekly call is key. The AWS data center moves fast, and the client decides next steps based on your report. A clear weekly update, with the right verb tenses for past, present, and future, protects the schedule and the relationship. This is one of the most important meetings of your week.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE do eixo de interação operacional. Antes da prática, fixe os três marcos de tempo: "Last week we completed…" (semana passada), "This week we are working on…" (esta semana), "Next week we will…" (próxima semana).

Aqui o eixo de Tempos Verbais aparece inteiro: passado, presente e futuro numa mesma fala.
lessons.situation: Reunião gerencial semanal com a Amazon: você apresenta o avanço da semana e o plano para a próxima.
lessons.context: Last week we completed the foundation. This week we are working on the electrical room. Next week we will start the cooling system. We are on track. I want to flag one risk.

Last week we completed phase one.

lessons.title: Status updates — overview geral do projeto
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe dar uma visão geral do projeto do data center em inglês simples — o quadro completo, as fases, o percentual concluído e o que ainda vem pela frente.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes the AWS client does not want the daily detail. They want the big picture. This is the project overview: where the obra started, where it is now, and when it will be done. As a contract manager at Racional, you give this view to leaders and to the client's senior team.

For the overview you use simple numbers and steps. You say when the project will break ground or when it broke ground. You name each phase and say the percent complete. You say if the project is on schedule. You point to the timeline, the energization date, and the hand over. It is a calm, high-level story of the whole build.

This view matters because data centers are huge and run for years. The AWS leaders plan their cloud capacity around your dates. When you give a clear overall picture in English, you show that Racional controls the project end to end. The big picture builds trust at the top.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE do eixo de interação operacional. Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "Here is the big picture.", "We are 60 percent complete." e "We plan to hand over in March."

O eixo de Tempos Verbais aparece ao misturar o que já aconteceu, o estado atual e a previsão futura.

lessons.title: Project kickoff meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe abrir uma reunião de kickoff de projeto com a AWS em inglês simples — apresentar-se, alinhar objetivo e escopo, definir papéis e combinar a forma de trabalho.
lessons.overview:
Every new project or new phase starts with a kickoff meeting. This is the first real meeting of the team. People introduce themselves, agree on the objective, and align on the scope. A good kickoff saves many problems later. For Racional on the AWS data center, a clear kickoff sets the tone with the American client.

In the kickoff you cover the basics. You walk through the agenda. You say what is in scope and what is out of scope. You name the roles, the deliverables, and the point of contact for each side. You align on the ways of working and the expectations. Everyone leaves the room with the same picture.

This meeting matters because AWS projects are fast and complex. If the scope is not clear from day one, time and money are lost. When you kick off well in English, you show that Racional is organized and ready. A strong start builds trust for all the meetings that come after.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE do eixo de interação operacional. Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "Let me introduce myself.", "Let's align on the scope." e "This is in scope; that is out of scope."

Aqui o foco é abrir bem: nome, objetivo, escopo e papéis, com frases curtas e claras.

lessons.title: Sotaque 5: Latin American English (Chilean, Colombian)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue entender o inglês falado por latino-americanos (sotaque chileno e colombiano) e pedir, com educação, que repitam ou falem mais devagar.
lessons.overview:
The world speaks English with many accents. People from Chile and Colombia speak English in a clear and friendly way. For a Brazilian speaker, this accent is easy to follow because the sounds are close to Portuguese. You will hear it at conferences, with regional suppliers, and with colleagues from all of Latin America.

This topic is close to your interests. You like economy and geopolitics, and you want to do a bilingual Executive MBA. In these spaces, you meet people from many countries. The data center market in Latin America is growing fast, and a lot of investment comes from North American clients like Amazon. Good listening helps you join these talks with confidence.

Racional works with global clients, so you will meet engineers and managers from the whole region. The goal here is simple exposure to spoken English. You do not need to speak like a native. You only need to understand and to ask for help when you miss a word. A short, polite question solves almost everything.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE, mais leve, sobre sotaques — um tema que você levantou. Hoje: o inglês de chilenos e colombianos.

Relembre três frases-âncora de apoio: Could you repeat that? (pedir para repetir), Could you slow down a little? (pedir ritmo mais lento) e Just to make sure I understood… (confirmar o que entendeu).
lessons.situation: Numa conferência de infraestrutura, você conversa com um engenheiro colombiano e uma gestora chilena sobre o mercado de data centers na região.
lessons.context: It is great to meet you. I work on data center projects in Santiago. The market here is growing fast. We see a lot of investment from North American clients. The energy transition is a big topic for us. How is the sector in Brazil these days?

lessons.title: Pre-construction meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe participar de uma reunião de pré-construção (pre-construction) com a Amazon — falar de projeto, materiais, prazos e riscos antes de a obra física começar.
lessons.overview:
A pre-construction meeting happens before the physical work starts. The team reviews the plan, the schedule, the materials, and the risks. The goal is simple: no surprises later. In a hyperscale data center for Amazon, one small delay can move a big start date, so this meeting is very important.

Here you talk about the future, because nothing has started yet. You say when the crew will arrive, when the steel will arrive, and when you will begin the foundation. You also talk about lead time — how long a material takes to come — and about the permits you need to confirm.

Racional has more than fifty years of experience and over 620 projects. A good pre-con shows this experience. You think about the risk early and you plan for it. When you speak clear English in this meeting, the Amazon team trusts your plan and the project starts well.
lessons.intro:
Nesta pre-con, tudo ainda vai acontecer — então o tempo verbal é o futuro.

Relembre duas formas-âncora: will (decisão/promessa: "we will start") e going to (plano já combinado: "the steel is going to arrive"). E uma frase de risco: If the permits are late, the start date will move.
lessons.situation: Reunião de pré-construção de uma nova fase do data center. Você revisa o plano com o time da Amazon antes de mobilizar a obra.
lessons.context: Let us review the plan before we start. We are going to mobilize the crew next month. The steel will arrive in two weeks, and we will begin the foundation right after. One risk: if the permits are late, the start date will move. We need to confirm them this week.

vocab.example: This is the pre-construction meeting.
We will mobilize the crew next month.
The crew arrives next week.
We will begin the foundation soon.
The steel will arrive on Monday.
The lead time is long.
We need to confirm the permits.
Let us confirm the dates this week.
The start date is Monday.
The start date may move.
Let us review the latest drawing.
We are going to mobilize next month.
One risk is the permit delay.
We anticipate the materials early.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva o plano
exercises.correctText: The crew will arrive next month.
exercises.explanation: Frase no futuro com "will". É o jeito de dizer quando a equipe chega.

exercises.title: 2. Sinalize o risco do prazo
exercises.explanation: "If the permits are late, the start date will move": presente na condição (are late) + futuro na consequência (will move). É o jeito certo de antecipar um risco.

exercises.title: 3. Plano já combinado (going to)
exercises.prompt: The steel is ___ to arrive in two weeks.
exercises.explanation: "Is going to arrive" mostra um plano já combinado. Usamos "going to" para algo programado, como uma entrega agendada.

exercises.title: 4. O tempo verbal da pre-con
exercises.prompt: Tudo na pre-con ainda vai acontecer. Qual frase usa o futuro corretamente?

options.text: Last month we mobilize the crew.
options.whyWrong: "Last month" é passado, mas "mobilize" está no presente; e a pre-con fala do futuro.

options.text: We will mobilize the crew next month.
We mobilized the crew next month.
options.whyWrong: "Mobilized" é passado, não combina com "next month", que é futuro.

exercises.explanation: Como tudo ainda vai acontecer, usamos o futuro: "will mobilize" + marca de tempo futura (next month).

exercises.title: 5. Apresente o plano em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We are going to mobilize the crew next month. The steel will arrive in two weeks, and we will begin the foundation right after. One risk: if the permits are late, the start date will move.
exercises.translation: Vamos mobilizar a equipe no próximo mês. O aço chegará em duas semanas, e iniciaremos a fundação logo em seguida. Um risco: se as licenças atrasarem, a data de início será adiada.
exercises.prompt: Você conduz a pre-con com a Amazon. Apresente o plano em voz alta, soando seguro sobre o que vem.
exercises.explanation: Você falou de tudo que ainda vai acontecer com will e going to — e antecipou o risco. Domínio do futuro em ação.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, descreva o plano de início de uma fase nova do data center: quando mobiliza, quando o material chega e qual o maior risco. Use o futuro. Pode misturar inglês e português onde precisar.
takeaways: I can take part in a pre-construction meeting with the Amazon team.
I can talk about plans using will and going to.
I can describe mobilization, materials and permits.
I can anticipate a risk: if X is late, the date will move.

lessons.title: Site meetings & toolbox talks
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe conduzir uma reunião de campo (site meeting) e uma toolbox talk de segurança no canteiro do data center — falar do que está sendo feito agora e dar instruções claras de segurança.
lessons.overview:
A site meeting happens at the construction site, close to the work. A toolbox talk is a short safety meeting at the start of the shift. In a data center for Amazon, these meetings are part of the daily routine. Safety always comes first, so the team talks about it every day before the work begins.

In the field you talk about the work now: the crew is installing the busway, the team is working near a live panel. You also give clear safety rules: Wear your hard hat. Stay alert. Report any hazard. PPE means Personal Protective Equipment, and on a site everybody must wear it.

Racional works on large and complex projects, and a clean safety record protects the people and the schedule. When you run a clear site meeting and a strong toolbox talk in English, the AWS team sees a professional and careful partner. Clear words keep the workers safe.
lessons.intro:
No campo, o tempo dominante é o presente contínuo — o que está acontecendo agora: The crew is installing the busway.

Para segurança, use o imperativo (verbo no início): Wear your PPE. · Stay alert near the live busway. · Report any hazard.
lessons.situation: No canteiro do data center, você abre o turno com uma toolbox talk e depois conduz uma rápida site meeting perto da área de instalação elétrica.
lessons.context: Good morning, team. Before we start, wear your PPE and your hard hat. The crew is installing the busway near a live panel today. This is a hazard, so stay alert and keep the walkway clear. If you see a problem, report it now.

vocab.example: We have a quick site meeting now.
The toolbox talk is short.
Safety comes first here.
Wear your PPE on the site.
Put on your hard hat.
This is a hazard. Be careful.
Stay alert near the panel.
Keep the walkway clear.
The crew is installing the busway.
The busway carries the power.
That panel is live. Do not touch it.
You must wear your hard hat.
Report any problem now.
The shift starts at seven.

exercises.title: 1. Termo de segurança → tradução
exercises.explanation: Estas são as palavras-chave de uma toolbox talk no canteiro.

exercises.title: 2. Escreva sua toolbox talk

exercises.explanation: Você abriu o turno com instruções de segurança curtas e diretas — o coração de uma toolbox talk.

exercises.title: 3. Instrução de segurança clara

options.text: Maybe you can wear a hard hat sometimes.

options.text: Wear your hard hat at all times.
I wore my hard hat yesterday.
options.whyWrong: Isso é passado e fala de você. A instrução é uma ordem para a equipe, no imperativo.

exercises.explanation: Instruções de segurança usam o imperativo: verbo no início, frase curta e clara. "Wear your hard hat" não deixa dúvida.

exercises.title: 4. Descreva o trabalho de agora
exercises.explanation: "The crew is installing the busway": presente contínuo (is + verbo-ing) para o que está acontecendo agora no canteiro.

exercises.title: 5. Abra o turno em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Good morning, team. Wear your PPE and your hard hat. The crew is installing the busway near a live panel. Stay alert and report any hazard.
exercises.translation: Bom dia, equipe. Usem o EPI e o capacete. A equipe está instalando o barramento perto de um painel energizado. Fiquem atentos e reportem qualquer perigo.
exercises.prompt: Você abre o turno no canteiro do data center. Diga a toolbox talk em voz alta, com voz firme e clara.
exercises.explanation: Você juntou presente contínuo (o que acontece agora) e imperativo (as regras) — exatamente como num diálogo de segurança real.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, abra o turno com uma toolbox talk de 15-20 segundos: peça o EPI, descreva o trabalho de hoje e aponte um perigo. Pode misturar inglês e português onde precisar.
takeaways: I can run a short toolbox talk at the start of the shift.
I can describe the work now with the present continuous.
I can give clear safety instructions with the imperative.
I can name PPE, hard hat, hazard and busway in English.

lessons.title: War rooms & crisis meetings — operational
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe participar de uma war room (reunião de crise) operacional com a AWS — explicar uma falha, dizer o que já foi feito, o que será feito e segurar sua posição com calma.
lessons.overview:
A war room is a crisis meeting. The team meets fast to fix a serious problem. In a data center, a power failure or a broken part can stop critical work, so people need answers now. The room is tense, and everybody looks for the root cause and a clear plan to bring the system back online.

In this meeting you use three times. You explain the past: what happened and what you already did. You explain the present: where things are now and if the system is stable. You explain the future: what you will do next. You also defend your position with calm: I hear you, but the safest path is to test first.

Racional manages large and complex sites, so a calm and clear voice in a crisis builds trust. When the AWS client feels pressure, your job is to stay calm, show the root cause, and hold the line on the safe plan. Clear English under pressure is real leadership.
lessons.intro:
Numa war room você navega três tempos: passado (what happened / what we did), presente (it is stable now) e futuro (we will bring it back online).

E pratique a tréplica — segurar a posição na 2ª e 3ª troca: I hear you, but the safest path is to test first.
lessons.situation: Houve uma falha em um equipamento crítico do data center. Você está numa war room com o time da AWS, sob pressão para dar uma data de retorno.
lessons.context: Here is the status. A cooling unit failed last night. We found the root cause this morning. The system is stable now, but it runs on backup. We are bringing in a replacement part. We will be back online in two days. I hear you, but the safest path is to test it first.

vocab.example: We are in a war room now.
This is a crisis. Stay calm.
The unit failed last night.
We had a failure in the system.
The system runs on backup now.
We are bringing in a part.
The replacement part arrives today.
We will be back online soon.
The system is stable now.
We found the root cause.
I understand the urgency.

vocab.pt: eu te entendo / entendo seu ponto
vocab.example: I hear you, but we must test first.
We hold the line on safety.
The safest path is to test first.

exercises.title: 1. Sob pressão, segure a posição
exercises.prompt: O cliente da AWS pede o retorno hoje, mas o teste leva dois dias. Qual é a melhor tréplica?

options.text: Okay, we will be back online today.
options.whyWrong: Você cede sob pressão e promete algo inseguro. Isso traz risco para a operação.

options.text: I hear you, but the safest path is to test it first.
I do not know. Maybe two days, maybe more.
options.whyWrong: Soa inseguro e sem controle. Numa crise, o cliente precisa de uma posição clara.

exercises.explanation: A boa tréplica reconhece o ponto do outro ("I hear you") e segura a posição segura ("the safest path is to test first"). Firme e respeitoso.

exercises.title: 2. Termo de crise → tradução
exercises.explanation: Estas palavras descrevem o estado do sistema numa war room.

exercises.title: 3. Ouça e escreva o status
exercises.correctText: The system is stable now.
exercises.explanation: Frase no presente para descrever o estado atual do sistema na war room.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva o status da crise
exercises.prompt: Em 3 frases, dê o status de uma falha: o que aconteceu (passado), como está agora (presente) e o que você vai fazer (futuro). Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: A cooling unit failed last night and we found the root cause this morning. The system is stable now, but it runs on backup. We are bringing in a replacement part and we will be back online in two days.
exercises.explanation: Você juntou os três tempos numa fala de crise: passado, presente e futuro. É a base de qualquer status numa war room.

exercises.title: 5. Conduza a war room em voz alta
exercises.targetText: A cooling unit failed last night. We found the root cause this morning. The system is stable now on backup. We will be back online in two days. I hear you, but the safest path is to test it first.
exercises.translation: Uma unidade de refrigeração falhou ontem à noite. Encontramos a causa raiz hoje de manhã. O sistema está estável agora, no backup. Estaremos de volta em dois dias. Entendo seu ponto, mas o caminho mais seguro é testar primeiro.
exercises.prompt: Você conduz a war room com a AWS sob pressão. Dê o status e segure a posição em voz alta, com calma e firmeza.
exercises.explanation: Você navegou os três tempos verbais e ainda segurou a posição na pressão — as duas dores que você trouxe, juntas numa fala só.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, conduza uma war room: explique a falha (passado), o estado agora (presente) e o plano (futuro). No fim, segure a posição quando o cliente pressionar por uma data mais cedo. Pode misturar inglês e português onde precisar.
takeaways: I can give a crisis status using past, present and future.
I can explain a failure and its root cause.
I can hold the line under pressure with I hear you, but.
I can defend the safest path with calm and respect.

lessons.title: Steering committees with hyperscale clients
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe participar de um steering committee com a AWS — seguir a pauta, dar status, sinalizar um risco, registrar uma decisão e fechar com os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
A steering committee is a high-level meeting with the client. Senior people from Racional and from Amazon meet to look at the big picture: the project status, the risks, and the key decisions. It is not about small details. It is about direction. The person who chairs the meeting keeps it short and follows the agenda.

In this meeting you give a clear status update: what is on track and what is not. You flag a risk early, so there is no surprise later. Every decision gets an action item, an owner, and a deadline. At the end, you wrap up with clear next steps.

Racional works with hyperscale clients like Amazon, where many meetings happen every week. In a steering committee, senior leaders have little time, so a short and clear voice wins trust. When you speak simple, organized English here, you show control of the project and you follow up well. That is the mark of a strong contracts manager.
lessons.intro: Num steering committee a fala é organizada e curta. Relembre frases-âncora: Let me give a quick status update. · The schedule is on track. · I want to flag one risk. · Let me wrap up with the next steps.
lessons.situation: Steering committee mensal com a liderança da AWS. Você apresenta o status da sua frente de contrato e sinaliza um risco.
lessons.context: Let me give a quick status update. The schedule is on track. The foundation is done. I want to flag one risk: a long lead time on the chillers. The decision today is to order them early. The owner is my team, and the deadline is Friday. Let me wrap up with the next steps.

vocab.example: We have a steering committee today.
This topic is on the agenda.
She will chair the meeting.
Here is a quick status update.
The schedule is on track.
I want to flag one risk.
The decision is to order early.
We have one action item.
The owner is my team.
The deadline is Friday.
Let us keep it short.
Let me wrap up now.
Here are the next steps.
I will follow up by email.

exercises.title: 1. Abra com o status
exercises.explanation: "Let me give a quick status update" é a frase-âncora para abrir sua fala num steering committee. Curta e direta.

exercises.title: 2. Sinalize o risco
exercises.prompt: I want to ___ one risk: the chillers have a long lead time.
exercises.explanation: "To flag a risk" é sinalizar um risco cedo, antes que vire problema. É esperado num comitê diretivo.

exercises.title: 3. Registre a decisão
exercises.prompt: O comitê decidiu comprar os chillers mais cedo. Qual frase registra bem a decisão?

options.text: Maybe we buy the chillers someday.
options.whyWrong: Vago e sem responsável nem prazo. Uma decisão de comitê precisa de owner e deadline.

options.text: The decision is to order early. The owner is my team. The deadline is Friday.
We ordered the chillers last year.
options.whyWrong: Isso é passado e não é a decisão de hoje. O comitê registra a ação futura.

exercises.explanation: Toda decisão num steering committee vira um action item com owner e deadline. Sem isso, nada acontece.

exercises.title: 4. Termo do comitê → tradução
exercises.explanation: Estas palavras estruturam a fala de um comitê diretivo.

exercises.title: 5. Escreva seu status de comitê
exercises.prompt: Em 3 frases, dê seu status no steering committee: diga o que está no prazo, sinalize um risco e registre uma decisão com responsável e prazo. Use ao menos 3 termos em inglês desta aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: Here is a quick status update. The schedule is on track and the foundation is done. I want to flag one risk: a long lead time on the chillers. The decision is to order them early. The owner is my team and the deadline is Friday.
exercises.explanation: Você seguiu a estrutura do comitê: status, risco, decisão com owner e deadline. Curto e claro, como a liderança espera.

exercises.targetText: Let me give a quick status update. The schedule is on track. I want to flag one risk: a long lead time on the chillers. The decision is to order them early. Let me wrap up with the next steps.

lessons.title: MBA Finance 2: valuation, M&A & growth investing
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende o vocabulário básico de finanças de MBA — valuation, fusões e aquisições (M&A) e investimento em crescimento — e consegue falar deles em inglês simples.
lessons.overview:
This BRIDGE lesson connects to your goal of a bilingual Executive MBA. Today the topic is finance. Valuation answers one big question: how much is a company worth? Investors look at the revenue and the profit to find the value. A clear valuation helps people make good decisions about money.

The lesson also covers M&A — mergers and acquisitions. A merger is when two companies join. An acquisition is when one company buys another. Before a company closes a deal, the team does due diligence: they check the numbers and the risks with care. Investors who like growth put their money where revenue is rising fast.

This world is close to your work. Amazon is one of the biggest companies in the world, and it grows through smart investment. Racional builds for these large clients in Brazil. When you understand finance words in English, you read the news with more confidence, and you get closer to your MBA dream. Strong vocabulary opens that door.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE, ligada ao seu objetivo de MBA. Tema de hoje: finanças.

Relembre três ideias-âncora: valuation (how much a company is worth), M&A (a merger joins two companies; an acquisition buys one) e growth investing (investors put money where revenue grows fast).
lessons.situation: Num intervalo de café com um colega da AWS, vocês falam sobre uma notícia de negócios: uma grande aquisição no setor de tecnologia.
lessons.context: Did you see the news? A big tech company acquired a smaller one. The valuation was very high because the revenue grows fast. Investors like growth, so they pay more. Before the deal, the team did due diligence. Now the shareholders are happy.

vocab.example: The valuation was very high.
The company is worth a lot.
The merger joins two companies.
The acquisition was big news.
They acquired a smaller company.
The shareholders are happy.
They reinvest the profit to grow.
Investors like fast growth.
The revenue grows fast.

lessons.title: Negotiation fundamentals (BATNA, ZOPA)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende e usa, em inglês simples, os termos básicos de uma negociação (BATNA, ZOPA, walk-away point) para se preparar antes de falar com a AWS.
lessons.overview:
Every week you have many meetings with the AWS team. In these meetings you talk about price, scope and time. This is negotiation. Good negotiation is not about winning by force. It is about being ready. Before any meeting, you prepare. You think about your interests and the interests of the client.

Two ideas help you a lot. The first is your BATNA, your best alternative if there is no deal. The second is the ZOPA, the zone where both sides can agree. When you know your walk-away point, you feel calm and strong. You do not accept a bad deal because you have a plan B.

Racional is a large construction company with more than 620 projects. On the Amazon data center, you negotiate big numbers with a North American client. When you prepare well, you protect Racional and you build common ground with the AWS team. Preparation gives you leverage and helps you reach a fair agreement.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, relembre três frases-âncora: "Let me prepare first" (deixe-me preparar antes), "Our best alternative is..." (nossa melhor alternativa é...) e "This is our walk-away point" (este é o nosso limite).

A ideia central: você não vai à reunião sem plano. Conhecer seu BATNA e seu limite (walk-away point) dá segurança para defender a posição da Racional.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião de preço com a AWS, você se prepara: define qual é o seu limite e qual é a faixa de acordo possível.
lessons.context: Before the meeting, I prepare. I know my interests. I know the client's interests too. My best alternative is clear, so I am calm. I also know my walk-away point. I want a fair deal, and I look for common ground. Good preparation gives us leverage.

vocab.example: The negotiation starts on Monday.
I prepare before the meeting.
Our BATNA is a strong plan B.
We have a good alternative.
The ZOPA is the zone of agreement.
This is my walk-away point.
I can walk away if it is bad.
Preparation gives us leverage.
I know my interests well.
We look for common ground.
Time for cost is a trade-off.
This price is my bottom line.
We want to reach an agreement.
It is a fair deal for both.

I can say what a fair deal is for us.

lessons.title: Negotiation tactics & language
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa frases simples em inglês para fazer ofertas e contrapropostas na reunião com a AWS, propondo trocas justas (if… then…).
lessons.overview:
In a negotiation, you make an offer. Then the AWS team makes a counteroffer. This is normal. Both sides talk, and both sides move a little. This is give and take. You do not give everything, and you do not get everything. You meet in the middle.

Good language helps a lot. You can say "if… then…" to propose a trade. For example: if the client moves the date, then you can hold the price. You can also say "in exchange for" when you ask for something back. These small phrases make you sound clear and professional.

On the Amazon data center, you negotiate cost, scope and time many times each week. Racional has more than 50 years of experience with big clients like Microsoft, Amazon and Google. When you use clear words and propose fair trades, you protect the margin and you keep a good relationship with the client. The goal is a win-win deal.
lessons.intro:
Relembre três frases-âncora para a prática: "Let me make an offer" (deixe-me fazer uma oferta), "If you do X, then we can do Y" (se você fizer X, então podemos fazer Y) e "In exchange for that, we ask..." (em troca disso, pedimos...).

O segredo da tréplica é nunca dar de graça: toda concessão vem com um pedido. "If… then…" é a sua ferramenta favorita.
lessons.situation: A AWS pede um desconto. Você não diz só "sim" nem só "não": você propõe uma troca, com uma contraproposta justa.
lessons.context: Let me make an offer. If you move the deadline, then we can hold the price. We need something in exchange. This is give and take. I want a fair deal for both sides. Let's meet halfway and find a win-win.

vocab.example: Let me make an offer.
The client sent a counteroffer.
I propose a small change.
If you wait, then we can help.
In exchange for time, we hold the price.
Negotiation is give and take.
We made one concession.
Let's meet halfway.
We can hold the price.
We cannot absorb the cost.
I will get back to you tomorrow.
That's difficult for us right now.
This deal is fair.
We want a win-win.

exercises.explanation: Estrutura "if… then…" para propor uma troca. Note "hold the price" (manter o preço).

exercises.title: 2. Ordene a frase
exercises.explanation: "We need something in exchange" = precisamos de algo em troca. Toda concessão pede algo de volta.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase

exercises.explanation: "To meet halfway" = encontrar-se no meio. É a forma simpática de pedir que os dois lados cedam.

exercises.title: 4. A melhor resposta
exercises.prompt: A AWS pede um desconto. Você quer manter o preço, mas sem fechar a porta. Qual é a melhor resposta?

options.text: "No. The price is the price."
options.whyWrong: É fechado demais; corta a negociação e prejudica o relacionamento.

options.text: "If you move the deadline, then we can hold the price."
"Okay, I give you the discount."
options.whyWrong: Você cedeu sem pedir nada em troca; perdeu margem e leverage.

exercises.title: 5. Diga em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Let me make an offer. In exchange for more time, we can hold the price.
exercises.translation: Deixe-me fazer uma oferta. Em troca de mais tempo, podemos manter o preço.
exercises.prompt: Você está respondendo a uma contraproposta da AWS. Leia em voz alta, com firmeza tranquila.
exercises.explanation: Note "in exchange for" (em troca de) e "hold the price" (manter o preço).

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em 15 a 20 segundos, responda a um pedido de desconto da AWS. Faça uma contraproposta justa usando "if… then…" ou "in exchange for". Pode misturar inglês e português.
takeaways: I can make an offer and a counteroffer.
I can propose a trade with "if… then…".
I can ask for something in exchange.
I can look for a fair, win-win deal.

lessons.title: Hard bargaining vs. principled negotiation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe diferenciar barganha dura de negociação por princípios e usar frases em inglês para defender sua posição com respeito e firmeza.
lessons.overview:
There are two ways to negotiate. The first is hard bargaining. Here, one side only pushes for its position and uses pressure. The second is principled negotiation. Here, both sides look at interests and use objective criteria, like the market rate. The second way is better for a long relationship.

You can be firm and respectful at the same time. You can say "I hear you" to show respect, and then push back on the idea, not on the person. This is the rule: separate the people from the problem. You stand firm on facts, not on emotion.

On the Amazon data center, the AWS team is strong and fast. Racional must hold its ground but keep trust. When you base your position on objective criteria, the client respects you more. You are not difficult; you are professional. This protects both the deal and the relationship.
lessons.intro:
Relembre três frases-âncora: "I hear you, but..." (eu entendo você, mas...), "We base this on the market rate" (baseamos isto na taxa de mercado) e "I have to stand firm on this point" (preciso ser firme neste ponto).

A ideia da tréplica aqui: separar a pessoa do problema. Você é firme com o fato e gentil com a pessoa.
lessons.situation: A AWS pressiona com força por uma posição. Você responde com respeito, mas defende a posição da Racional com base em critérios objetivos.
lessons.context: I hear you. I understand your point. But I have to stand firm here. We base our position on the market rate, not on pressure. Let's separate the people from the problem. I want a fair deal, and I want to stay respectful.

vocab.example: Hard bargaining hurts trust.
Principled negotiation is better.
I will defend my position.
We look at the real interests.
We use objective criteria.
This is the market rate.
I stand firm on this point.
I hold my ground here.
I hear you, but I disagree.
I push back on this idea.
We want a fair deal.

vocab.en: to separate the people from the problem
vocab.example: We separate the people from the problem.
We do not give in to pressure.
I stay calm and respectful.

exercises.explanation: A correção olha só o uso dos termos em inglês da aula.

exercises.title: 3. Firme e respeitoso

options.text: "You are wrong. This is final."
options.whyWrong: Ataca a pessoa e fecha a conversa; é barganha dura.

options.text: "I hear you, but we base this on the market rate."

options.whyWrong: Cede só por pressão, sem critério objetivo; perde a posição.

exercises.title: 4. Ordene a frase
exercises.explanation: "Let's separate the people from the problem" é a regra de ouro: firme com o fato, gentil com a pessoa.

exercises.title: 5. Diga em voz alta

exercises.translation: Eu te entendo, mas preciso ser firme. Baseamos isto na taxa de mercado.
exercises.prompt: A AWS te pressiona na segunda troca da reunião. Leia a frase em voz alta, calmo e firme.
exercises.explanation: Note "I hear you" (respeito) seguido de "stand firm" (firmeza). Os dois juntos.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em 15 a 20 segundos, defenda uma posição da Racional sob pressão da AWS. Comece com "I hear you", seja firme e use "market rate" como critério. Pode misturar inglês e português.
takeaways: I can tell hard bargaining from principled negotiation.
I can say "I hear you" and still stand firm.

lessons.title: Pricing negotiations
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa frases simples em inglês para falar de preço, custo e margem e para responder a pedidos de desconto da AWS.
lessons.overview:
Price is a big topic in every negotiation. The client asks for a lower price. You send a quote. The client asks for a discount. You must protect the margin. To do this, you need clear, simple words about cost and price.

Sometimes costs go up. Steel, energy or labor can be more expensive. Then you say: "the current price is X" and "prices will rise". You can also add value instead of cutting the price. For example, you give a small extra service at no cost. This keeps the client happy and protects your margin.

On the Amazon data center, the numbers are very large. Racional builds for big clients like Amazon, Microsoft and Google, so price talks happen often. When you explain costs clearly and offer value, the AWS team trusts your numbers. You do not just come down on the price; you show why the price is fair.
lessons.intro:
Relembre três frases-âncora: "The current price is..." (o preço atual é...), "Our costs went up" (nossos custos subiram) e "We can add value instead" (podemos agregar valor no lugar).

A ideia central: antes de baixar o preço, explique o custo e ofereça valor. Use os tempos verbais: custo subiu (passado), preço atual é (presente), preços vão subir (futuro).
lessons.situation: A AWS pede um desconto grande. Você explica que os custos subiram e oferece valor em vez de simplesmente baixar o preço.
lessons.context: Let me explain the price. Our costs went up last month. The current price is fair. I cannot give a big discount, because the margin is small. But I can add value at no cost. Prices will rise next year, so this is a good deal now.

lessons.title: MBA People: talent management & high-performance teams
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende e usa, em inglês simples, o vocabulário de gestão de pessoas e times de alta performance, um tema do seu interesse de MBA.
lessons.overview:
This is a lighter MBA People topic. Companies grow with good people. So leaders must hire and retain the right talent. This is talent management. When good people leave, the company has high turnover, and that costs money and time.

A high-performance team is not only about skills. It is also about trust and engagement. A good leader gives clear feedback, runs a fair performance review, and helps people grow. When people feel valued, they are more motivated, and the team delivers more.

Racional has more than 50 years and thousands of workers on sites like the Amazon data center. On a big project, you lead engineers, suppliers and partners. Good leadership keeps the team strong under pressure. This is why "MBA People" topics matter for a contracts manager: your results depend on your people.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula BRIDGE, mais leve, ligada ao seu desejo de fazer um MBA executivo. Relembre três frases-âncora: "We hire and retain good people", "A high-performance team needs trust" e "Good leaders give feedback".

O foco aqui é exposição ao inglês e conexão com um tema que você gosta.
lessons.situation: Numa conversa leve com a AWS, surge o tema de liderança e times. Você fala sobre como mantém um time de alta performance na obra.
lessons.context: Good leaders hire the right people. They also retain them, because turnover is expensive. A high-performance team needs trust and clear feedback. We run a fair performance review every year. When people feel valued, they stay motivated and the team delivers more.

lessons.title: Scope negotiations & change orders
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe negociar mudanças de escopo em inglês e explicar o impacto de uma change order em prazo e custo para a AWS.
lessons.overview:
On a big project, the scope can change. The client asks for something new, or a field condition is different. When the work is out of scope, you need a change order. This is the formal way to add work to the contract. Without it, the contract is not clear, and that creates risk.

Every change order has an impact. New work can move the schedule and raise the cost. So you do an impact analysis first. You explain the impact, and then you ask the client to approve. You always register the change in a formal way before you move forward.

On the Amazon data center, scope changes happen often, because it is a fast hyperscale project. Racional protects the contract by handling each change the right way. When you compare the new request to the baseline and show the impact clearly, the AWS team understands the cost and the time. This keeps the project clean and the relationship strong.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CORE do ciclo do contrato. Relembre três frases-âncora: "That request is out of scope" (esse pedido está fora do escopo), "This will impact the schedule and the cost" (isto vai impactar o prazo e o custo) e "We need a formal change order to move forward".

A ideia central: nada de trabalho novo sem change order. Primeiro o impacto, depois o avanço. Use o futuro (will impact) para mostrar a consequência.
lessons.situation: A AWS pede um item novo que não estava no contrato. Você explica que é fora do escopo, faz a análise de impacto e propõe uma change order formal.
lessons.context: Let me check the baseline. This request is out of scope. It is not in the original contract. The new work will impact the schedule and the cost. So we need a formal change order. Let me do an impact analysis first. Then we can register it and move forward.

This is additional work.

Let me do an impact analysis.
Then we can move forward.

Let me check the baseline.
We register the change.

lessons.title: Tréplica 1: when "ok" isn't enough — defending your position
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue defender sua posição na segunda troca de uma reunião — quando um "ok" simples não basta e o cliente da AWS volta a insistir.
lessons.overview:
In a long project like the AWS data center, one meeting is never the end. The client says "ok", and then the client comes back. As the contract manager at Racional, you talk again, and again. This second moment is the moment to defend your position. You do not fight. You stay calm, and you hold your point.

The American client likes a clear answer. But a hard "no" can hurt the relationship. So you do two things. First, you agree a little: "I hear you." Then you defend your point: "However, two weeks earlier is not realistic." You show respect, and you stay firm. This is the heart of a good tréplica (second reply).

Racional has more than fifty years and more than 620 projects. The team knows what is realistic and what is not. Your job is to put that experience into simple English, so the AWS team trusts your date. When you can commit to a real number and stand by it, the client feels safe — and that is your goal.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você pratica a segunda troca: reconhecer e depois defender. Três frases-âncora vão guiar a aula: "I hear you" (eu te entendo), "However, that is not realistic" (no entanto, não é realista) e "What I can commit to is this date" (o que posso me comprometer é com esta data).

A regra de ouro: primeiro reconheça, depois defenda. Reconhecer não é ceder — é abrir espaço para o seu "mas".
lessons.situation: Na reunião semanal, a AWS recebe seu prazo e diz "ok", mas volta dizendo que precisa de tudo duas semanas antes. Você defende o prazo possível sem dar um "não" seco.
lessons.context: I hear you, and I know the date matters. However, two weeks earlier is not realistic with this crew. What I can commit to is this date. Let me explain why this is the safe number. I stand by it.

I push back on the date.
That date is not realistic.

I hold the line here.

Let me reassure you on quality.

lessons.title: Tréplica 2: pushing back without burning the bridge
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue discordar e rebater sem prejudicar o relacionamento — usando linguagem suave que protege a parceria com a AWS enquanto defende o seu ponto.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes you do not agree with the client. That is normal. But with an American client like AWS, the way you say "no" is very important. You can disagree, but you must not burn the bridge. The relationship must stay strong, because you have many more meetings after this one.

The tool is soft language. Small words take away the hard edge. You do not say "You are wrong." You say "I see it a bit differently." You do not attack the person; you talk about the problem. You look for common ground — a place where both teams agree. This keeps the conversation open and friendly.

At Racional, the AWS data center is a long partnership. Quality and safety come first, always. So when the client wants to cut a test step to go faster, you push back — but with care. You show that you are not against speed; you only want a safe way to get there. Soft words protect both the project and the partnership.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você pratica discordar com tato. Frases-âncora: "I see where you're coming from" (entendo de onde você vem), "I'm not sure I agree" (não tenho certeza se concordo) e "I'd suggest we keep the testing step" (eu sugeriria manter a etapa de teste).

A regra de ouro: ataque o problema, nunca a pessoa. Diga "I see it differently", não "you are wrong".
lessons.situation: A AWS propõe acelerar a obra cortando uma etapa de teste. Você discorda — mas é uma parceria de longo prazo, então rebate de forma colaborativa.
lessons.context: I see where you're coming from, but I'd suggest we keep the testing step. I'm not against speeding up. Perhaps we can change the sequence instead of cutting tests. I think there is a safer way.

vocab.example: I don't want to burn a bridge.
I soften the message a little.
I'm not sure I agree with that.
I'd suggest we keep the test.

vocab.pt: de onde você vem (seu ponto de vista)
vocab.example: I see where you're coming from.

I'm not against speeding up.
Let's keep this collaborative.
I see it a bit differently.

My concern is the test step.

lessons.title: Tréplica 3: handling unexpected questions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue lidar com uma pergunta inesperada numa reunião com a AWS — confirmando o que foi perguntado e respondendo com calma em vez de travar.
lessons.overview:
In a meeting in English, the hardest moment is the unexpected question. The AWS team asks something you did not plan for. Your mind goes blank. This happens to everyone, and it is normal. The skill is not to know every answer — the skill is to stay calm and buy a little time.

The trick is simple: confirm before you answer. You repeat the question in your own words. You say "Just to make sure, are you asking about the cooling or the power?" This does two things. It gives you time to think, and it shows the client that you listen with care. A good question deserves a clear, correct answer — not a fast, wrong one.

As the contract manager on the AWS data center, you are in many meetings every week. Technical questions come fast. If you do not have the exact figure, that is fine. You say "Let me come back to you with the right number." At Racional, a correct answer one hour later is much better than a wrong answer now.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você pratica a pergunta que não esperava. Frases-âncora: "That's a good question" (boa pergunta), "Just to make sure, are you asking about...?" (só para garantir, você está perguntando sobre...?) e "Let me come back to you with the exact figure" (deixa eu te retornar com o número exato).

A regra de ouro: confirme a pergunta antes de responder. Isso ganha tempo, evita erro e mostra controle.

lessons.title: Economia global 2: Fed, inflation & interest rates
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue entender e comentar, em inglês simples, o tema de juros e inflação — o trabalho do Fed nos Estados Unidos.
lessons.overview:
You said you love economics and you want a bilingual Executive MBA. So this bridge lesson is for you. We look at the Fed — the central bank of the United States. The Fed controls the interest rate, and this rate touches the whole American economy, including big tech companies like Amazon.

The idea is simple. When prices go up too fast, we have inflation. To fight inflation, the Fed can raise rates. Higher rates make money more expensive to borrow, so people and companies spend less, and the economy starts to cool down. When the economy is slow, the Fed can cut rates to help growth. It is a balance.

Why does this matter for Racional? Your client AWS is part of Amazon, a giant American company. Interest rates change how big companies invest in new projects, like data centers. When you read the news in English about the Fed, you understand the world of your clients — Microsoft, Amazon, Google — a little better.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma bridge de economia. Frases-âncora: "The Fed raises rates to fight inflation" (o Fed sobe os juros para combater a inflação) e "Higher rates cool down the economy" (juros altos esfriam a economia).

Foco: vocabulário simples de economia para você ler e comentar a notícia em inglês.

lessons.title: Tréplica 4: buying time when you don't know the answer
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue ganhar tempo de forma profissional quando não sabe a resposta — sem inventar números e sem perder a confiança da AWS.
lessons.overview:
Nobody has every answer ready. In a fast meeting with AWS, the client asks for a number, and you do not have it yet. This is not a problem — it is a normal part of the job. The skill is to buy time in a clear, professional way, and never to give a guess as if it were a fact.

The key phrases are short and honest. "Let me check with my team." "Let me get back to you by this afternoon." "I'd rather confirm than give you the wrong number." These sentences protect you and the client. They show that you care about the right number, not just a fast answer.

For a contract manager on the AWS data center, this matters a lot. One wrong figure can move a deadline, a cost, or a decision. At Racional, with more than 620 projects of experience, the rule is the same: double-check, then commit. When you promise a clear time to come back — "by this afternoon" — the client trusts you even more.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você aprende a ganhar tempo sem inventar. Frases-âncora: "Let me get back to you" (deixa eu te retornar), "Let me check with my team" (deixa eu confirmar com minha equipe) e "I'd rather confirm than give you the wrong number" (prefiro confirmar a te dar o número errado).

A regra de ouro: prometa um prazo claro para retornar. "By this afternoon" é melhor que um vago "later".
lessons.situation: Numa reunião, a AWS pede um valor que você ainda não confirmou. Em vez de chutar, você ganha tempo e promete retornar com o número certo no mesmo dia.

lessons.title: Tréplica 5: escalating without escalating
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue sinalizar um risco e levá-lo a um nível mais alto sem criar conflito — mantendo o tom neutro e factual com a AWS.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes a problem is too big for the meeting room. You need to escalate it — bring it to a higher level, like the steering committee. But "escalate" can sound like a fight. The skill in this lesson is to escalate without escalating the emotion: you raise the issue calmly and you keep the tone neutral.

The secret is to be factual, not personal. You do not assign blame. You do not say "this is your fault." You say "I want to flag a risk for visibility." You give the facts: the supplier is late, the date is at risk, here is a backup plan. You bring a problem and an option, not an attack. This keeps the partnership strong.

For the AWS data center, this is very important. The project is large and fast, and small risks can grow. At Racional, the right move is to flag a risk early, while there is still time to act. When you escalate in calm, factual English, the leaders trust your judgment and the client sees you as a real partner.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você pratica sinalizar um risco sem virar briga. Frases-âncora: "I want to flag a risk for visibility" (quero sinalizar um risco para dar visibilidade), "Let me keep this factual" (deixa eu manter isto factual) e "The date is at risk, and here is a backup plan" (a data está em risco, e aqui está um plano B).

A regra de ouro: traga fatos, não culpa. Você sinaliza o risco e oferece uma saída, mantendo o tom neutro.
lessons.situation: Um fornecedor está atrasado e isso pode afetar o prazo. Você leva o tema ao steering committee, sem acusar ninguém, apenas com os fatos e um plano B.
lessons.context: I want to flag a risk for visibility. The supplier is late, so the date is at risk. I'm not here to assign blame. Let me keep this factual. We have a backup plan, and I'd like a decision from the committee.

lessons.title: Tréplica 6: closing the rebuttal — landing the point
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe FECHAR a tréplica — a terceira e última troca de uma discussão — em inglês simples: resumir o ponto, propor o próximo passo e encerrar com firmeza, sem deixar a reunião em aberto.
lessons.overview:
Every week, contract managers at Racional Engenharia sit in meetings with the AWS team. On the Amazon data center, the schedule is tight and the pressure is high. Many talks become a debate: the client pushes, you defend your position, and the client pushes again. This third and last exchange is the moment to close the point. You do not reopen the fight. You land your idea and you move on.

A good rebuttal has three simple beats. First, you sum up the agreement: "We both want the system on time." Second, you give a clear proposal: "I will send the cost impact by Friday." Third, you close with a calm and firm line: "That is a fair way forward." You keep your point, but you also respect the time of the client.

This skill matters a lot for Racional. The company built more than 620 projects in 50 years, and it works with big clients like Amazon, Microsoft and Google. In a hyperscale data center, decisions cannot stay open for days. The contract manager who closes first, with a clear next step, controls the room and protects the project. Sum up, propose, close — in that order.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora do fechamento: "So, to wrap up, we both want it on time" (resumo), "My proposal is to send the data by Friday" (próximo passo) e "That's a fair way forward, let's move on" (encerramento firme).

A frase de ouro para segurar a posição até o fim: "I'd rather settle this now than leave it open". Mostra controle e respeita o tempo do cliente AWS.
lessons.situation: Terceira e última troca de uma reunião tensa com a AWS sobre uma mudança de escopo. Você já reconheceu a urgência e já defendeu a sua posição; agora você fecha o ponto e propõe o próximo passo.
lessons.context: So, to wrap up, we are closer than it sounds. We both want the system on time. My proposal is simple. I will send you the cost impact by Friday. Then we decide together on the call. I'd rather settle this now than leave it open. I think that is a fair way forward.

vocab.example: Let me wrap up my point.
I want to land the point now.
To sum up, we agree on two things.
My proposal is clear and simple.
That is a fair way forward.
Let's settle this now.
I don't want to leave it open.
We have common ground here.
Let's agree and move on.
I think that is fair for both.
The next step is your review.
Let's close out this item.
We align on the date today.
Let me recap what we agreed.

exercises.explanation: Resumo, proposta e fechamento firme: é assim que você aterrissa o ponto e sai com uma decisão clara.

takeaways: I can close a rebuttal instead of reopening the argument.
I can sum up the agreement and propose a clear next step.

I can end the meeting with a fair way forward.

lessons.title: Verb tenses 1: past, present & future under pressure
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe usar, em inglês simples, os três tempos básicos — passado, presente e futuro — para reportar o que JÁ aconteceu, o que ACONTECE agora e o que VAI acontecer numa reunião com a AWS.
lessons.overview:
In a weekly status update, the client wants a clear story of time. What is done? What is in progress now? What comes next? At Racional Engenharia, the contract manager reports the work on the Amazon data center almost every day. To do this well in English, you need three simple verb forms: past, present and future.

The past tells what the team finished: "Last week we finished the cables. We sent the report." The present tells what is happening now: "Right now we are testing the connections. The team is working on the documents." The future tells the plan: "Next week we will start the tests. We are going to send the final report on Friday." These three forms cover most of a real update.

This is a key skill for a hyperscale project. With 620+ projects in 50 years and clients like Amazon, Microsoft and Google, Racional reports a lot of data every week. When you follow the timeline — past, then present, then future — the AWS team follows the project with no confusion. Time order is your map.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe a linha do tempo do update: "Last week we finished..." (passado), "Right now we are testing..." (presente em andamento) e "Next week we will..." (futuro).

Regra simples: passado = verbo + -ed ou forma irregular; presente em andamento = am/is/are + verbo-ing; futuro = will ou going to.
lessons.situation: Status update semanal com a AWS. Você precisa dizer o que foi concluído na semana passada, o que está em andamento agora e o que será feito na próxima semana.
lessons.context: Last week we finished the cable pulling. We sent you the report. Right now we are testing the connections, and the team is working on the documents. Next week we will start the tests. We are going to send the final report by Friday.

The team is working on the plan.

options.whyWrong: Isto é presente em andamento; você quer falar do que já terminou.

exercises.explanation: Para o que já foi feito, use o passado: 'Last week we finished...'.

exercises.title: 5. Dê o update em voz alta

exercises.translation: Semana passada terminamos os cabos. Agora estamos testando-os. Semana que vem enviaremos o relatório.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, reporte o seu trabalho real desta semana à AWS em três frases: o que você terminou ('Last week we finished...'), o que está em andamento ('Right now we are...') e o que vem a seguir ('Next week we will...'). Pode misturar inglês e português onde travar.
takeaways: I can talk about the past with 'we finished' and 'we sent'.
I can talk about now with 'we are testing'.

I can give an update in time order: past, present, future.

lessons.title: Geopolítica 2: US–China & the semiconductor race
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe conversar, em inglês simples, sobre a disputa EUA–China e a corrida dos semicondutores (os chips) — um tema de geopolítica que conecta direto ao mundo da AWS.
lessons.overview:
This is a bridge lesson about a topic you enjoy: geopolitics. Today we look at the biggest economic race of our time — the United States and China and the fight over semiconductors. A chip is very small, but it runs everything: phones, cars and the servers in the AWS data center that Racional is building right now.

The story is simple. The most advanced chips come from only a few places, so there is a dependence and a risk in the supply. The US uses export controls to limit the sale of top chips to China. China wants to invest in its own manufacturing and lead the industry. Both sides want the competitive edge, because chips are now a question of national security.

For a contract manager at Racional Engenharia, this is more than news. A hyperscale data center is full of chips, and clients like Amazon, Microsoft and Google live inside this tech race. A short, friendly talk about it builds connection with the AWS team. You do not need to win the debate — you just share an idea and ask: "How do you see it?"
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora leves: "It's a strategic issue" (é uma questão estratégica), "Both sides want to lead" (os dois lados querem liderar) e "Chips power our data centers".

E a frase que devolve a conversa ao colega, mantendo o tom leve: "How do you see it?" (como você vê isso?).
lessons.situation: Conversa informal antes da reunião com um colega americano da AWS. Sai uma notícia sobre novos controles de exportação de chips, e você puxa um papo leve de geopolítica conectando ao mundo dos data centers.
lessons.context: Did you see the news on chip export controls? It is a strategic race between the US and China. Both sides want to lead in semiconductors, because chips power everything, including our data centers. Most advanced chips come from a few places, so there is a real risk. How do you see it?

lessons.title: Verb tenses 2: choosing the right tense in business meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe escolher o tempo verbal certo numa reunião de negócios com a AWS — quando usar passado, presente ou futuro para dizer o que já foi feito, o que está em andamento e o que está planejado.
lessons.overview:
In lesson 128 you learned the three verb forms: past, present and future. Now the question is harder and more useful: in a real meeting, which tense do you choose? The client asks a question, and the right tense gives the right answer. At Racional Engenharia, the contract manager makes this choice many times in every AWS call.

Three common cases on the Amazon data center. The client asks if a task is done: you answer with already or not yet — "I already sent it" or "Not yet, I will send it today." The client asks about a plan: you use we are planning to or as we planned — "We are planning to submit on Friday." The client asks about routine work: you use the present — "We review the reports every week."

This is a key business skill. With 620+ projects and clients like Amazon, Microsoft and Google, Racional must give clear and exact answers. The wrong tense sends the wrong message: "I sent it" and "I will send it" are very different promises. When you pick the right tense, the AWS team trusts your words and the project moves with no doubt.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três escolhas úteis: já feito = "I already sent it"; ainda não = "Not yet, I will send it today"; plano = "We are planning to submit on Friday".

Lembre-se da diferença que muda tudo: "I sent it" (já fiz) é diferente de "I will send it" (vou fazer). Escolha o tempo certo conforme a pergunta do cliente.
lessons.situation: Reunião com a AWS sobre a entrega de documentos. O cliente faz perguntas sobre o que já foi enviado, o que está planejado e o que é rotina, e você responde com o tempo verbal certo.
lessons.context: Did you send the report? Yes, I already sent it. The drawings are not ready yet, but we are planning to submit them on Friday, as we planned. At the moment we review the documents every week. I will let you know when the next set is ready.

lessons.title: Difficult conversations & conflict resolution
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe conduzir, em inglês simples, uma conversa difícil com a AWS — abrir o assunto com cuidado, descrever o problema sem culpar ninguém e buscar uma solução em conjunto.
lessons.overview:
On a tight project, not every talk is easy. Sometimes you must raise a problem: a late delivery, a quality issue, a cost change. This is a difficult conversation. The goal is not to fight or to blame someone. The goal is to name the problem, stay calm and find a solution together. At Racional Engenharia, the contract manager handles these talks with the AWS team many times in a critical phase.

A good difficult conversation has a clear shape. First, you open with care: "To be honest with you, I'm concerned about the schedule." Then you describe the issue, not the person: you address the problem, you do not attack. Then you invite the other side to help: "Let's find a solution" and "We need to be on the same page." And you ask the client not to take it personally — it is about the work, not the relationship.

This skill protects both the project and the partnership. With 620+ projects in 50 years and clients like Amazon, Microsoft and Google, Racional knows that a good relationship is built in hard moments, not only easy ones. When you raise a problem with respect and a calm tone, you clear the air and you move forward — together, not against each other.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: abertura cuidadosa = "To be honest with you, I'm concerned about the schedule"; foco no problema = "Let's address the issue, not the people"; convite à solução = "Let's find a solution together".

E a frase que protege a relação: "Please don't take it personally" (por favor, não leve para o lado pessoal). É sobre o trabalho, não sobre a pessoa.
lessons.situation: Reunião difícil com a AWS sobre um atraso na entrega. Você precisa levantar o problema com cuidado, sem culpar ninguém, e propor que vocês resolvam juntos.
lessons.context: To be honest with you, I am concerned about the schedule. I don't want to blame anyone. Please don't take it personally. Let's address the issue together and find a solution. We need to be on the same page. I think we can clear the air and move forward.

lessons.title: Saying no diplomatically
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe dizer NÃO com diplomacia em inglês simples — recusar um pedido da AWS com respeito, explicar o motivo e oferecer uma alternativa.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes the client asks for something you cannot give: a date that is too soon, a price that is too low, an extra task with no time. You must say no — but a hard "no" can hurt the relationship. The skill is to say no with respect. You turn down the request, you explain why, and you offer an alternative. At Racional Engenharia, the contract manager does this often with the AWS team.

A diplomatic no has three parts. First, a soft start: "I'm afraid that won't be possible." Second, a short reason: "The issue is that we need more time to test it." Third, a way forward: "What I can do is finish it by Monday. Would that work?" You do not just block the client — you give a real option and a clear trade-off.

This protects both the project and the trust. With 620+ projects and clients like Amazon, Microsoft and Google, Racional must be honest about what is possible. A safe "yes" that you cannot keep is worse than a polite "no." When you push back with care and never overpromise, the client respects your word and the partnership stays strong.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe as três partes do não diplomático: início suave = "I'm afraid that won't be possible"; motivo curto = "The issue is that we need more time"; alternativa = "What I can do is finish it by Monday. Would that work?".

Lembre-se: nunca prometa o que não pode cumprir (don't overpromise). Um 'não' com alternativa vale mais que um 'sim' impossível.
lessons.situation: Reunião com a AWS. O cliente pede uma entrega numa data muito apertada. Você precisa recusar com diplomacia, explicar o motivo e oferecer uma alternativa real.

lessons.title: Phone calls & voicemails in English
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe atender e fazer ligações em inglês e deixar um recado de voz (voicemail) claro — sem o apoio dos gestos e do rosto que você tem numa reunião presencial.
lessons.overview:
The phone is hard in English. You cannot see the face. You cannot use your hands. The sound is often bad. But phone calls are part of your week with the AWS team. As a contracts manager at Racional, you call people every day. You call the project manager. You call a supplier. You confirm a date. So you need simple words for the phone.

Good news: phone calls use fixed phrases. They are always the same. You say "this is Julio" to give your name. You say "could you repeat that?" when you do not understand. You say "I'm calling about..." to give the reason. You learn the phrase, and the phrase works every time. You do not need many words. You need the right words.

Many times the person does not answer. Then you leave a voicemail. A good voicemail has four parts: your name, the reason, your request, and your number. Short and clear is better than long and full. At Racional, on the AWS data center, a clear voicemail brings the client back to you fast. That is the goal.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar as frases-âncora do telefone: "Hello, this is Julio from Racional" para se identificar, "Sorry, could you repeat that?" quando não entender e "I'm calling about..." para dar o motivo.

Lembre as quatro batidas do voicemail: (1) quem é você, (2) por que ligou, (3) o que precisa e (4) seu número. Fale devagar e repita o número no fim.

lessons.title: Idioms 3: construction & meeting idioms (on track, in the pipeline)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende e usa expressões idiomáticas de obra e de reunião — como "on track", "in the pipeline" e "behind schedule" — para soar natural quando fala do andamento do projeto com a AWS.
lessons.overview:
This is a lighter BRIDGE lesson, from your idioms track. American managers do not say long words for simple things. They use short fixed phrases. When the work is good, they say it is on track. When the work is late, they say it is behind schedule. When the work is early, they say it is ahead of schedule. You hear these phrases in every meeting with the AWS team.

These phrases are like building blocks. You learn the full block, not the single words. "We are on track" means the project is fine. "It is in the pipeline" means it is coming soon. "I will keep you in the loop" means I will give you the news. "We are on the same page" means we agree. Simple blocks, big help.

At Racional, you talk about the data center every day. You give status to the client in the hall, in a call, in a quick chat. When you use the right idiom at the right time, you sound local and clear. The client trusts your words more. That is the value of this lesson: small phrases that make you sound like one of the team.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar os blocos prontos: "We're on track for August", "It's in the pipeline" e "We're a bit behind schedule, but we caught up".

Lembre: o idiom é um tijolo único. Decore o bloco inteiro, não as palavras soltas. Ele só funciona quando sai inteiro e na hora certa.
lessons.situation: Numa conversa rápida de corredor com um PM da AWS, ele pergunta como está a obra. Você responde com as expressões certas, sem soar de manual.
lessons.context: Hey, good to see you. The electrical works are on track for August. We had a small delay on the cooling pipes, but we caught up, so we are back on schedule. Two change orders are in the pipeline. I will keep you in the loop.

lessons.title: Email writing — formal vs. casual
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe diferenciar um e-mail formal de um casual em inglês — abertura, fechamento e tom — para escrever a mensagem certa para o cliente AWS em cada situação.
lessons.overview:
You write many emails every week with the AWS team. The words matter, but the tone matters too. A cold email can sound rude. A very casual email can sound too close. As a contracts manager at Racional, you must pick the right tone for each reader. This lesson helps you choose.

The difference is in three parts: the greeting, the body, and the close. A formal email opens with "Dear Mr. Smith," and closes with "Best regards,". A casual email opens with "Hi Sarah," and closes with "Thanks,". In a formal email you write "I would like to" and "Could you please". In a casual email you write "I'd like to" and "Can you".

The rule is simple. First contact, a hard topic, or someone outside your daily team → use formal. A colleague you talk to every day → casual is fine. When you are not sure, choose formal. On the AWS data center, the right tone keeps the client close and the message clear.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar as frases-âncora: formal abre com "Dear Mr. Carter," e fecha com "Best regards,"; casual abre com "Hi Dave," e fecha com "Thanks,".

Lembre: no formal use "Could you please..." e "I would like to..."; no casual, "Can you..." e "I'd like to...".
lessons.situation: Você precisa escrever dois e-mails: um para um diretor da AWS que você nunca conheceu, e outro para o PM com quem fala diariamente. O conteúdo é parecido, mas o tom muda.
lessons.context: Dear Mr. Carter, I would like to confirm our meeting on Thursday. Could you please tell me if the time works for you? Best regards, Julio. And to the PM: Hi Dave, just confirming Thursday. Does the time still work? Thanks, Julio.

vocab.example: This is a formal email to a director.
A casual email to a close colleague.
Match the tone to the reader.
The greeting sets the tone.
Dear Mr. Carter,
Best regards, Julio.
I am writing to follow up.
I would like to confirm the date.
Could you please reply today?
Please find attached the report.
I want to confirm the meeting.
I look forward to your reply.
Just a quick note to confirm.

exercises.explanation: Primeiro contato, diretor, tema sensível: vá de formal. Na dúvida, escolha o formal.

exercises.explanation: 'Could you please confirm the date?' é o pedido educado padrão de um e-mail formal.
