exercises.explanation: 'I look forward to your reply' e 'Best regards' fecham o e-mail formal com elegância.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, diga como você abriria e fecharia dois e-mails: um formal para um diretor novo da AWS ('Dear...', 'Best regards') e um casual para o PM do dia a dia ('Hi...', 'Thanks'). Explique em uma frase por que cada tom.
takeaways: I can open a formal email with 'Dear' and close with 'Best regards'.
I can open a casual email with 'Hi' and close with 'Thanks'.
I can use 'Could you please' and 'I would like to' in a formal email.
I can choose the right tone for each reader.

lessons.title: Email — escalations & complaints
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe escrever um e-mail em inglês para sinalizar um problema, escalar uma pendência ou registrar uma reclamação de forma firme e educada com o cliente AWS.
lessons.overview:
Sometimes the work has a problem. A part is late. A date is at risk. A supplier does not answer. When this happens, you must flag the issue in writing. As a contracts manager at Racional, you do this many times on the AWS data center. A clear email protects the project and protects Racional.

There is a way to do this well. You stay firm but polite. You name the concern. You explain how it can impact the schedule. You ask for a firm date. You do not get angry, and you do not hide the problem. You write things like "I'd like to flag a concern" or "This may impact the energization date."

When a problem is big, you escalate it. This means you send it to a higher level — a director, a steering committee. The email must be short, clear, and calm. The client must read it and understand the risk fast. On a hyperscale data center for AWS, a small delay can cost a lot, so a good escalation email is a strong tool for the manager.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar as frases-âncora: "I'd like to flag a concern about..." para sinalizar, "This may impact the energization date" para mostrar o risco e "Could you confirm a firm date?" para pedir solução.

Lembre: firme e educado ao mesmo tempo. Nomeie o problema, mostre o impacto, peça uma data.
lessons.situation: Um fornecedor está atrasado e isso ameaça a data de energização. Você precisa escrever ao PM da AWS sinalizando o risco e pedindo uma data firme, sem perder o tom profissional.
lessons.context: Hi Dave, I would like to flag a concern. The cooling parts are overdue, and this may impact the energization date. This is urgent for us. Could you please confirm a firm date this week? I'd appreciate your help. Thanks, Julio.

takeaways: I can flag a concern in a clear and polite way.
I can say a part is overdue and a date is at risk.

I can write a short escalation email without sounding angry.

lessons.title: Meeting minutes & follow-up emails
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe escrever a ata de uma reunião (meeting minutes) e o e-mail de follow-up em inglês, com recap, action items, donos e prazos.
lessons.overview:
After every meeting with the AWS team, someone must write what happened. This is the meeting minutes and the follow-up email. As a contracts manager at Racional, you do this all the time. A clear recap stops fights later. Everyone reads the same notes and remembers the same plan.

A good follow-up has a few parts. First, a short recap of the meeting. Then the action items — the tasks. Each task has an owner (the person) and a due date (the day). You also write the next steps. You use simple phrases like "We agreed to...", "The team decided...", and "I will send the plan on Friday."

Here verb tenses matter. You write the past for what was decided ("we agreed"), the present for what is happening now ("the team is finalizing the plan"), and the future for what comes next ("I will circulate the minutes"). On the AWS data center, with many meetings each week, a clean follow-up email keeps the whole team aligned.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar as frases-âncora dos três tempos: passado para o que foi decidido ("We agreed to..."), presente para o que está em curso ("The team is finalizing...") e futuro para o próximo passo ("I will send the minutes").

Lembre a estrutura: recap → action items (owner + due date) → next steps.
lessons.situation: Você acabou de sair de uma reunião semanal com a AWS e precisa enviar a ata e o e-mail de follow-up, listando o que foi decidido, quem faz o quê e até quando.
lessons.context: Hi team, here is a quick recap of today's meeting. We agreed to start the energization tests next week. Action item: Carlos will send the test plan by Friday. The team is finalizing the safety check. I will circulate the minutes today. Next steps: confirm the final date.

vocab.example: I will write the meeting minutes.

exercises.explanation: Recap, action item, owner e due date são as quatro peças de um follow-up claro.

exercises.modelAnswer: Hi team, here is a quick recap. We agreed to start the tests next week. Action item: Carlos is the owner and the due date is Friday. I will circulate the minutes today. Next steps: confirm the final date.
exercises.explanation: Recap, action item com owner e due date, e next steps: a estrutura completa do follow-up.

exercises.title: 6. Leia o recap em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Here is a quick recap. We agreed to start next week. Carlos will send the test plan by Friday. I will circulate the minutes today.
exercises.translation: Aqui vai um resumo rápido. Concordamos em começar na semana que vem. Carlos vai enviar o plano de testes até sexta. Vou circular a ata hoje.

exercises.explanation: Passado para o que foi decidido, futuro para o próximo passo: os tempos certos na ata.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, faça o recap de 15 segundos de uma reunião com a AWS em inglês simples: diga o que 'we agreed to' (passado), o que o time 'is finalizing' (presente) e o que você 'will send' (futuro). Misture os três tempos.
takeaways: I can write a quick recap of a meeting.
I can list an action item with an owner and a due date.
I can use the past for decisions and the future for next steps.
I can say 'I will circulate the minutes today'.
I can keep the AWS team aligned with a clear follow-up email.

lessons.title: Project closeout meetings & lessons learned
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe conduzir uma reunião de encerramento de projeto (closeout) e falar das lições aprendidas (lessons learned) em inglês — o que foi bem, o que não foi e o que fazer diferente.
lessons.overview:
Every project ends one day. At the end, the team meets to wrap up the work. This is the closeout meeting. The team looks back and shares the lessons learned. As a contracts manager at Racional, you lead this meeting with the AWS team. It is a key moment, because the next project starts better when this one ends well.

A closeout has a simple shape. You say what is complete. You talk about what went well and what didn't go well. You agree on what to do differently next time. You write down each takeaway. You also do the handover — you give the work to the client team. And you thank the team for the effort.

Racional has more than fifty years and over six hundred projects. Each closeout makes the company stronger. On the AWS data center, a good lessons-learned meeting helps the next phase, the next building, the next client like Microsoft or Google. You speak simple English, you stay honest, and you end the project on a high note.
lessons.intro:
Vamos retomar as frases-âncora: "We delivered the work on time", "What went well was the safety plan", "Next time we will do this differently" e "Thank you to the whole team."

Lembre a estrutura: o que está complete → what went well → what didn't go well → what to do differently → thank the team.
lessons.situation: A fase da obra com a AWS terminou. Você conduz a reunião de encerramento, apresenta o que foi entregue, lista as lições aprendidas e agradece à equipe.
lessons.context: Hi everyone, thank you for joining. This phase is now complete, and we met the main milestone on time. What went well was the safety plan. What didn't go well was the parts delay. Next time we will order earlier. Thank you to the whole team for the great work.

vocab.example: This is the closeout meeting.
Let's share the lessons learned.
We will wrap up the project.
This phase is now complete.
We met the main milestone.
What went well was the safety plan.
What didn't go well was the delay.
Next time we will do this differently.
The main takeaway is to plan early.
We delivered the work on time.
Now we start the handover.
I want to thank the team.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: This phase is complete and we delivered on time.
exercises.explanation: 'Complete' e 'delivered on time' abrem o closeout com uma boa notícia clara.

exercises.title: 2. Fale do que não foi bem
exercises.prompt: Na reunião de encerramento, você quer dizer, com honestidade, o que não funcionou. Qual frase usar?

options.text: Everything was perfect, no problems.
options.whyWrong: Esconde o problema; uma boa lição aprendida precisa ser honesta.

options.text: What didn't go well was the parts delay.
It was bad and someone is to blame.
options.whyWrong: Procura culpado em vez de focar na melhoria; não ajuda o próximo projeto.

exercises.explanation: 'What didn't go well was...' nomeia o problema com honestidade, sem culpar pessoas.

exercises.title: 3. Termo e significado
exercises.explanation: Closeout, lessons learned, what went well e handover são as palavras-chave do encerramento.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva o resumo do closeout
exercises.prompt: Escreva 3 ou 4 frases para a reunião de encerramento da fase com a AWS: diga o que está complete, o que went well, o que didn't go well e o que fazer differently. Use ao menos 3 termos desta aula. A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
keywords: what went well|what didn't go well|root cause
exercises.modelAnswer: This phase is now complete, and we delivered on time. What went well was the safety plan. What didn't go well was the parts delay. Next time we will order earlier. Thank you to the team.
exercises.explanation: Complete, what went well, what didn't go well e do differently: a estrutura honesta do closeout.

lessons.title: Pitch comercial: Amazon AWS hyperscale data center proposal
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe abrir, desenvolver e fechar um pitch comercial em inglês simples para propor à Amazon AWS a construção de um data center hyperscale — apresentando a Racional, a proposta de valor e o pedido final.
lessons.overview:
A pitch is a short talk. You use it to win new work. In this lesson, Racional makes a pitch to Amazon AWS. The goal is one big project: a hyperscale data center. A good pitch has three parts. First, you say who you are. Then you show your value proposition — the reason to choose you. At the end, you make the ask: you ask to be the build partner.

Racional is a strong builder. The company started in 1971. That is more than fifty years of experience. Racional has a long track record: more than 620 projects and over ten million square meters. The company works for big global clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. This history helps Racional stand out. A data center is hard and fast work, so the client wants a reliable team.

For a manager like you, the pitch is the first step. You show that Racional can build at this scale. You show that the company can deliver on time and on budget. Numbers make the pitch strong, so use them. At the end, you say what you want with a clear ask. A pitch with no ask is only a chat. A good pitch opens a real partnership.
lessons.intro:
Esta é a primeira aula CAPSTONE: uma apresentação completa conduzida por você. Relembre as três frases-âncora que vão estruturar a sua fala.

"We're Racional, a Brazilian builder with over fifty years of experience." (abertura) · "We deliver on time and on budget." (proposta de valor) · "We'd like to be your build partner." (o pedido final).
lessons.situation: Você apresenta a Racional ao time de compras e operações da AWS, propondo que a construtora seja a parceira de construção do novo data center hyperscale.
lessons.context: Good morning, and thank you for your time. We are Racional, a Brazilian builder. We started in 1971. That is over fifty years of experience. We have a strong track record. We delivered more than 620 projects. We build on time and on budget. We understand hyperscale scale. We would like to be your build partner for this data center.

lessons.title: Kickoff meeting & mobilization pós-NEA
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe conduzir uma reunião de kickoff de obra com a AWS após a assinatura (NEA) — apresentando objetivos, equipe, plano de mobilização e os primeiros passos, falando no futuro.
lessons.overview:
The pitch worked. The contract is signed. This step is called NEA. Now the project starts. The first meeting is the kickoff meeting. In this meeting, the team and the client align on the plan. Everyone leaves the room with the same picture. As the contract manager, you lead this meeting for Racional and for Amazon AWS.

After the kickoff comes mobilization. To mobilize means to bring the team and the machines to the site. Racional knows this work well. In more than 620 projects, the company learned to set up the site fast and safe. A hyperscale data center needs a big crew and a clear timeline. Speed matters, but safety comes first.

A kickoff has four simple parts. You state the goal. You introduce the team and each role. You explain the mobilization plan. You set the first milestone with a date. Here you talk about the future, so you use will and going to. A clear start helps the whole project. When the team knows the goal and the first step, the work moves with no noise.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CAPSTONE: o pitch deu certo, o contrato foi assinado (NEA), e agora você conduz o kickoff com a AWS. Relembre as frases-âncora no futuro.

"Our goal is to deliver on time and on budget." · "Let me introduce the team." · "We are going to mobilize the crew and set up the site." · "Our first milestone is the site setup by next month."
lessons.situation: O contrato do data center foi assinado (NEA concluído). Você abre a reunião de kickoff com a AWS para alinhar objetivos, apresentar o time e dar início à mobilização do canteiro.
lessons.context: Welcome, everyone, and thank you. The contract is signed now. Our goal is clear: we will deliver this data center on time and on budget. Let me introduce the team and their roles. In the first weeks, we are going to mobilize the crew and set up the site. Our first milestone is the site setup by next month. Let's get started.

lessons.title: War room: comissionamento pré-H2C sob pressão
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe conduzir, em inglês simples, a sua parte de uma war room de comissionamento pré-H2C com a AWS — abrir com o contexto, mostrar o estado dos testes, nomear o bloqueador e defender o seu plano quando o cliente pressionar.
lessons.overview:
A war room is a crisis room. The team meets in one room to fix the last problems fast. In a data center project, this happens before H2C (Hand to Commissioning). H2C is the moment when the build team hands the work to the test team. The days before H2C are very tense. As the contract manager, you speak for Racional in this room with Amazon AWS.

Commissioning means the final tests of all systems. The team checks power, water, and cooling. If one system fails, the date is at risk. A hyperscale data center has a hard critical path, so one blocker can stop everything. Racional knows how to run these tests under time pressure. The goal is simple: clear every item and hold the date.

Your speech has four short parts. First you set the scene — you give the context. Then you show where commissioning stands. Then you name the one blocker. At the end, you give your plan with a date. The client may push back and say it is too slow. You do not fight and you do not panic. You stand your ground with a fact: "Based on the latest test, we can hold the date if we start tonight."
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CAPSTONE: você ensaia a sua parte numa war room pré-H2C com a AWS. Relembre as quatro batidas e a frase de tréplica.

"Let me set the scene." (contexto) · "Here is where commissioning stands." (status) · "The one blocker is the cooling loop." (bloqueador) · "Based on the latest test, we can hold the date." (defesa com dado).
lessons.situation: Faltam poucos dias para o H2C do data center da AWS. O time se reúne em war room e o cliente americano quer saber, sem rodeios, se o comissionamento estará pronto. A palavra passa para você.
lessons.context: Let me set the scene. We are three days from H2C. The war room is open to clear the last items. Here is where commissioning stands. The power systems passed. The cooling loop has one open blocker. My plan is to run the final test tonight. Based on the latest test, we can hold the H2C date.

lessons.title: Vendor negotiation: switchgear delivery 60 days behind
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe conduzir, em inglês simples, uma negociação tensa com um fornecedor cujo switchgear está 60 dias atrasado — abrir com o impacto, fazer um pedido firme e defender a sua posição na segunda e terceira troca quando o fornecedor empurrar de volta.
lessons.overview:
A switchgear is a big power panel. It is a key part of the data center. Without it, the building has no power. In this lesson, the supplier says the switchgear is sixty days late. This is a long slip. The slip puts the whole schedule with Amazon AWS at risk. So this negotiation is real and tense.

You speak in three parts. First, you show the impact with a fact. Then you make a firm ask: you want a recovery plan. At the end, you have a plan B, like a second supplier. Racional has worked with many vendors in 620 projects. A good manager stays calm and clear. You can be firm and still polite. You want common ground — a deal that works for both sides.

The hard part is the pushback. The vendor will say no. This is where you defend your position. In the second turn, the vendor says "We can't go faster." You answer with a fact: "I hear you, but a partial delivery still keeps us moving." In the third turn, you close: "Let's meet halfway. A partial shipment by week three. That works for both sides." The rule is simple. Do not raise your voice — raise your data.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CAPSTONE: você ensaia uma negociação com o fornecedor do switchgear atrasado. Relembre as frases-âncora da TRÉPLICA (defender na 2ª e 3ª troca).

"The sixty-day slip puts our schedule at risk." (impacto) · "We need a recovery plan by Friday." (pedido) · "I hear you, but a partial delivery keeps us moving." (réplica) · "Let's meet halfway. That works for both sides." (acordo).
lessons.situation: O fornecedor do switchgear avisa um atraso de 60 dias que pode mover a energização do data center da AWS. Numa call tensa, você faz o pedido, ouve a réplica do fornecedor e segura a sua posição até um acordo.
lessons.context: Thank you for joining. Let me be direct. The sixty-day slip on the switchgear puts our schedule at risk. We need a recovery plan by Friday. I hear you, the line is full. But a partial delivery by week three keeps us moving. Let's meet halfway. That works for both sides.

exercises.title: 1. O fornecedor empurra de volta. Como você reage?
exercises.prompt: Você pede um plano de recuperação. O fornecedor responde "We can't go faster." A melhor tréplica é:

options.text: Subir o tom e ameaçar cancelar tudo na hora.
options.whyWrong: Subir o tom fecha a porta; sob pressão você sobe o dado, não a voz.

options.text: "I hear you, but a partial delivery still keeps us moving."
Aceitar o atraso de 60 dias e encerrar a conversa.

exercises.title: 3. Defenda a sua posição em voz alta

lessons.title: QBR executivo: monthly review com Amazon NA
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe conduzir, em inglês simples, a sua parte de um QBR executivo com a Amazon North America — abrir com os destaques, reportar os números do trimestre, apontar a perspectiva e responder com firmeza a perguntas de uma audiência multinacional.
lessons.overview:
A quarterly business review (QBR) is a big meeting. It happens every three months. The team and the client look at the last quarter together. In this lesson, the room is Amazon North America. The people are senior and from many countries. So you speak slowly, with short sentences and clear numbers. As the contract manager, you lead Racional's part.

You open with the highlights — the good news first. Then you report the metrics: time, cost, and safety. Good numbers are simple. You say you are on schedule and on budget. You report the safety record and the milestones on time. After 620 projects, Racional knows that clients like Amazon trust clear, honest numbers quarter over quarter.

Then you give the outlook — what comes next quarter. At the end, there is a Q&A. A director may ask a hard question, like "Why was safety down?" You do not panic. You buy one second with "Good question." Then you give the context and a fact: "The dip was in week six, after the storm. We added training, and the rate recovered." The rule is simple: lead with the numbers and keep a fact ready for every question.
lessons.intro:
Esta é uma aula CAPSTONE: você ensaia o seu QBR com a Amazon NA. Relembre as quatro batidas e o modelo de resposta no Q&A.

"Three highlights this quarter." (destaques) · "We are on schedule and on budget." (números) · "Next quarter, the focus is energization." (perspectiva) · "Good question. The rate recovered after training." (Q&A).
lessons.situation: Reunião trimestral executiva com a Amazon North America sobre o data center hyperscale. Diretores de vários países estão na sala, e você representa a gestão de contratos com dez minutos e uma rodada de perguntas.
lessons.context: Good morning, everyone. Three highlights this quarter. We are on schedule. We are on budget. Our safety record is strong. The key metric is ninety-eight percent of milestones on time. Next quarter, our focus is energization. The one ask from this group is faster approval on change orders.

exercises.title: 2. Escreva a abertura do seu QBR
exercises.prompt: Em 2 ou 3 frases, escreva a abertura do seu QBR com a Amazon NA: dê os destaques, reporte um número e aponte o foco do próximo trimestre. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula (ex.: highlights, on schedule, on budget, metric, outlook). A correção olha só o uso dos termos.
keywords: on schedule|on budget|outlook|milestone|safety record|quarter over quarter
exercises.modelAnswer: Good morning. Three highlights this quarter. We are on schedule. We are on budget. Our safety record is strong. The key metric is ninety-eight percent of milestones on time. Next quarter, the focus is energization.
exercises.explanation: Destaques, um número forte e a perspectiva em frases curtas: essa é a sua abertura de QBR executivo em inglês.

exercises.title: 3. Responda no Q&A em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Good question. The safety rate was down in week six, after the storm. We added training right away. The rate recovered by week eight. We are back on track now.
exercises.translation: Boa pergunta. O índice de segurança caiu na semana seis, depois da tempestade. Adicionamos treinamento na hora. O índice se recuperou na semana oito. Estamos de volta ao prazo agora.
exercises.prompt: Um diretor americano pergunta "Why was safety down this quarter?" Responda em voz alta: ganhe um segundo com "Good question", contextualize e feche com o dado da recuperação.
exercises.explanation: Você acabou de responder a uma pergunta executiva sob pressão: contexto curto, um dado e o fechamento de que está sob controle.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 15 a 20 segundos, abra o seu QBR com a Amazon NA: dê dois ou três destaques, reporte um número (prazo, orçamento ou segurança) e aponte o foco do próximo trimestre. Pode misturar inglês e português onde precisar.
takeaways: I can open a QBR with the highlights of the quarter.
I can report on schedule and on budget in clear numbers.
I can give the outlook for the next quarter.
I can answer a tough question with a calm data point.
I can lead a multinational room with short sentences.

lessons.title: Handover PFHO → PCO & lessons learned
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe conduzir, em inglês simples, o handover final da transição PFHO → PCO com a AWS — marcar o marco, entregar os documentos, fechar com as lições aprendidas e abrir caminho para a próxima parceria.
lessons.overview:
The handover is the last step. It is the moment when Racional gives the finished data center to Amazon AWS. The project moves from PFHO to PCO — the client now takes ownership and the data center can go live. This is a big day. It is the moment to mark a milestone and to hand over the keys.

At handover, you sign off on the work and you give all the documents. You hand over the as-built drawings and the O&M manuals. These papers help Amazon run the building. Racional has done this in over 620 projects. A clean handover shows that the company is reliable and ready for the next job. It builds a real partnership.

At the end, you share the lessons learned. You say what worked well and what to improve next time. This is honest and useful. Then you look forward. You thank the team, you wrap up the project, and you talk about going forward with the client. A good closing today opens the door to the next data center tomorrow.
lessons.intro:
Esta é a última aula CAPSTONE: o handover final da obra. Relembre as frases-âncora que fecham o projeto.

"Today we mark a big milestone." (marco) · "We hand over the keys and the as-built drawings." (entrega) · "What worked well, and what to improve." (lições) · "We look forward to going forward together." (futuro da parceria).
lessons.situation: O data center da AWS está pronto e operacional. Você conduz a reunião de handover (PFHO → PCO), entrega a documentação e fecha o ciclo com as lições aprendidas.

Let me share two lessons learned: what worked well, and what to improve. We look forward to going forward together.

exercises.prompt: Em 2 ou 3 frases, escreva o fechamento do handover com a AWS: marque o marco, entregue a documentação e dê uma lição aprendida. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula (ex.: handover, milestone, as-built drawings, lessons learned, going forward). A correção olha só o uso dos termos.

exercises.modelAnswer: Today we mark a big milestone. The data center is ready to go live. We hand over the keys, the as-built drawings, and the O&M manuals. One lesson learned: clear planning worked well. We look forward to going forward together.
exercises.explanation: Marco, entrega e uma lição aprendida: você fecha o projeto com clareza e abre caminho para a próxima obra.

exercises.title: 3. Conduza o handover em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Thank you, everyone. Today we mark a big milestone. The data center is ready to go live. We hand over the keys and the as-built drawings. What worked well was clear planning. We look forward to going forward together.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 15 a 20 segundos, conduza o handover final com a AWS: marque o marco, diga o que está entregando, dê uma lição aprendida (o que funcionou bem) e feche com a parceria seguindo daqui para a frente. Pode misturar inglês e português onde precisar.
